3.7.s:
3.31
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhāvādhyāyamato vacmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu ..
hāsādyāḥ kathitā bhāvāḥ pañcāśattvekavarjitāḥ .. 1 ..
3.7.d:
3.31
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भावाध्यायमतो वच्मि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
हासाद्याः कथिता भावाः पञ्चाशत्त्वेकवर्जिताः ॥ 1 ॥
3.7.m: 3.31 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Next, I will tell the chapter on emotional states; hear that from me as I speak: / forty-nine emotional states, beginning with laughter, have been declared.

3.7.s:
paraceṣṭānukaraṇādyaddhāsyamupajāyate ..
smitahāsābhihasitairabhineyasya paṇḍitaiḥ .. 2 ..
3.7.d:
परचेष्टानुकरणाद्यद्धास्यमुपजायते ॥
स्मितहासाभिहसितैरभिनेयस्य पण्डितैः ॥ 2 ॥
3.7.m: The laughter that arises from imitating another’s actions / should be represented by the wise through smiles, laughter, and loud laughter.

3.7.s:
iṣṭārthaviṣayaprāptau ratirityupajāyate ..
saumyatvādabhineyā sā vāṅmādhuryādibhistathā .. 3 ..
3.7.d:
इष्टार्थविषयप्राप्तौ रतिरित्युपजायते ॥
सौम्यत्वादभिनेया सा वाङ्माधुर्यादिभिस्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
3.7.m: Upon attaining a desired object or sensory pleasure, love arises. / It should be represented through gentleness, sweetness of speech, and the like.

3.7.s:
iṣṭabandhuviyogena dhananāśena pārthiva ..
śoko bhavati tasya syādruditābhinayakriyā .. 4 ..
3.7.d:
इष्टबन्धुवियोगेन धननाशेन पार्थिव ॥
शोको भवति तस्य स्याद्रुदिताभिनयक्रिया ॥ 4 ॥
3.7.m: From separation from a dear relative or loss of wealth, O king, / sorrow arises; its dramatic action should be weeping.

3.7.s:
krodhaścatuḥprakāraśca kartavyo nāṭyayoktṛbhiḥ ..
ripujo gurujaścaiva bhṛtyajaḥ praṇayodbhavaḥ .. 5 ..
3.7.d:
क्रोधश्चतुःप्रकारश्च कर्तव्यो नाट्ययोक्तृभिः ॥
रिपुजो गुरुजश्चैव भृत्यजः प्रणयोद्भवः ॥ 5 ॥
3.7.m: Anger is of four kinds to be presented by directors of dramatic performance: / born of an enemy, born of a guru, born of a servant, and born of affection.

3.7.s:
niryantritaḥ sa śatrūṇāṃ gurūṇāṃ svedasaṃyutaḥ ..
bhṛtyānāṃ ca dayāluḥ syātstrīṇāṃ ca praṇayodbhavaḥ .. 6 ..
3.7.d:
निर्यन्त्रितः स शत्रूणां गुरूणां स्वेदसंयुतः ॥
भृत्यानां च दयालुः स्यात्स्त्रीणां च प्रणयोद्भवः ॥ 6 ॥
3.7.m: That [directed toward] enemies is unrestrained; toward gurus, it is accompanied by perspiration; / toward servants, it should be compassionate; and toward women, it arises from affection.

3.7.s:
karmātiśayanirvṛttau vismayo harṣasaṃbhavaḥ ..
siddhisthāne tvasau sādhyo romāñcahasanādibhiḥ ..7..
3.7.d:
कर्मातिशयनिर्वृत्तौ विस्मयो हर्षसंभवः ॥
सिद्धिस्थाने त्वसौ साध्यो रोमाञ्चहसनादिभिः ॥7॥
3.7.m: Upon the achievement of an extraordinary deed, astonishment arises, born of joy; / in the realm of success, it is to be effected through horripilation, laughter, and the like.

3.7.s:
asau mohābhinirvṛttau vyavasāyanayātmakaḥ..
utsāhastvabhineyaḥ syādapramādakriyādibhiḥ..8..
3.7.d:
असौ मोहाभिनिर्वृत्तौ व्यवसायनयात्मकः॥
उत्साहस्त्वभिनेयः स्यादप्रमादक्रियादिभिः॥8॥
3.7.m: In the absence of delusion, [arising] from resolve and prudent conduct, / enthusiasm should be represented through vigilant actions and the like.

3.7.s:
svāparādhasamudbhūtaṃ bhayaṃ nāmeha jāyate ..
vepathutrāsapatanairabhineyasya sambhramaiḥ..9..
3.7.d:
स्वापराधसमुद्भूतं भयं नामेह जायते ॥
वेपथुत्रासपतनैरभिनेयस्य सम्भ्रमैः॥9॥
3.7.m: Arising from one’s own offense, fear is produced here; / it is to be represented through trembling, terror, falling, and agitated movements.

3.7.s: bībhatsadarśanādyaistu jugupsā nāma jāyate..3.31.10..
3.7.d: बीभत्सदर्शनाद्यैस्तु जुगुप्सा नाम जायते॥3.31.10॥
3.7.m: Disgust arises from the sight of repulsive things.

3.7.s:
udvejanaissahṛllekhairabhineyo vikūṇanaiḥ..
dāridryeṣṭavināśe ca nirvedo nāma jāyate..11..
3.7.d:
उद्वेजनैस्सहृल्लेखैरभिनेयो विकूणनैः॥
दारिद्र्येष्टविनाशे च निर्वेदो नाम जायते॥11॥
3.7.m: It should be represented through shuddering, retching, and contracting the limbs. / Upon poverty or the destruction of what is dear, despondency arises.

3.7.s:
parasparaviniḥśvāsaistasyābhinayanakriyā..
vānte virakte śrānte ca glāniḥ syāttapasā tathā..12..
3.7.d:
परस्परविनिःश्वासैस्तस्याभिनयनक्रिया॥
वान्ते विरक्ते श्रान्ते च ग्लानिः स्यात्तपसा तथा॥12॥
3.7.m: Its dramatic representation is through mutual deep sighs. / In one who has vomited, one who is purged, one who is exhausted, or through asceticism, exhaustion occurs.

3.7.s: mandākramaṇakampādyaiḥ kṣāmatvenaṃ ca darśayet ..13..
3.7.d: मन्दाक्रमणकम्पाद्यैः क्षामत्वेनं च दर्शयेत् ॥13॥
3.7.m: One should show it through slow movement, trembling, and emaciation.

3.7.s:
cauryādibhirgṛhītasya śaṅkā nāmeha jāyate ..
ākārāvaraṇaṃ tasyāḥ kāryaṃ digavalokanam ..
parāparādhasambhūtā asūyā nāma jāyate .. 14 ..
3.7.d:
चौर्यादिभिर्गृहीतस्य शङ्का नामेह जायते ॥
आकारावरणं तस्याः कार्यं दिगवलोकनम् ॥
परापराधसम्भूता असूया नाम जायते ॥ 14 ॥
3.7.m: In one apprehended for theft and the like, apprehension arises here; / its representation should be concealment of the body and looking in all directions. / Arising from another's offense, envy arises.

3.7.s:
guṇanāśanavidveṣaiḥ sābhineyā tathā budhaiḥ ..
madyopayogena mado jāyate ca tribhistathā .. 15 ..
3.7.d:
गुणनाशनविद्वेषैः साभिनेया तथा बुधैः ॥
मद्योपयोगेन मदो जायते च त्रिभिस्तथा ॥ 15 ॥
3.7.m: It should be represented by the wise through decrying virtues and through malice. / Through the use of intoxicating liquor, intoxication arises, and it is threefold:

3.7.s:
uttamādhamamadhyatvātpuruṣāṇāṃ svabhāvataḥ ..
dṛgbhrameṇottamānāṃ syānmadhyānāṃ vākpralāpataḥ .. 16 ...
3.7.d:
उत्तमाधममध्यत्वात्पुरुषाणां स्वभावतः ॥
दृग्भ्रमेणोत्तमानां स्यान्मध्यानां वाक्प्रलापतः ॥ 16 ॥।
3.7.m: due to the nature of persons being superior, inferior, or middling. / For superior ones, it is by rolling of the eyes; for middling ones, through incoherent speech;

3.7.s:
adhamānāṃ ca patanairasambaddhaparikramaiḥ ..
āyāsenādhamanāñca śramo nāmeha jāyate..17..
3.7.d:
अधमानां च पतनैरसम्बद्धपरिक्रमैः ॥
आयासेनाधमनाञ्च श्रमो नामेह जायते॥17॥
3.7.m: and for inferior ones, through fallings and unsteady walking. / Through exertion and walking, weariness arises here.

3.7.s:
gātramardanaviśvāsajṛmbhaṇaistatprayojayet ..
garveṇa khedādrāgeṇa hyālasya syātsvabhāvataḥ .. 18 ..
3.7.d:
गात्रमर्दनविश्वासजृम्भणैस्तत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥
गर्वेण खेदाद्रागेण ह्यालस्य स्यात्स्वभावतः ॥ 18 ॥
3.7.m: One should employ it through rubbing the limbs, deep sighs, and yawning. / From pride, distress, or passion, indolence arises naturally.

3.7.s:
tasya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ śayanāsanasevanāt ..
daurgatyena manastāpāddainyaṃ nāmeha jāyate .. 19 ...
3.7.d:
तस्य प्रयोगः कर्तव्यः शयनासनसेवनात् ॥
दौर्गत्येन मनस्तापाद्दैन्यं नामेह जायते ॥ 19 ॥।
3.7.m: Its performance should be executed by resorting to lying down and sitting. / From destitution or mental distress, wretchedness arises here.

3.7.s:
hṛdayasya vitarkeṇa tasya tvabhinayo bhavet ..
asthāne taskarāndṛṣṭvā trāsanairvividhaistathā .. 3.31.20 ..
3.7.d:
हृदयस्य वितर्केण तस्य त्वभिनयो भवेत् ॥
अस्थाने तस्करान्दृष्ट्वा त्रासनैर्विविधैस्तथा ॥ 3.31.20 ॥
3.7.m: Its dramatic representation should be through deliberation of the heart. / Having seen thieves in an inappropriate place, and through various frights,

3.7.s:
tatpratīkāraśūnyasya mohaḥ samupajāyate ...
vyasanenābhighātena vairānusmaraṇena ca ..21 ..
3.7.d:
तत्प्रतीकारशून्यस्य मोहः समुपजायते ॥।
व्यसनेनाभिघातेन वैरानुस्मरणेन च ॥21 ॥
3.7.m: stupefaction arises in one who is devoid of remedy. / Through calamity, physical blow, or remembering enmity,

3.7.s:
sarvendriyāṇāṃ mohena sa tu kāryaḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ ..
smaraṇātpūrvavṛttānāṃ smṛtirnāmeha jāyate .. 22 ..
3.7.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां मोहेन स तु कार्यः प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥
स्मरणात्पूर्ववृत्तानां स्मृतिर्नामेह जायते ॥ 22 ॥
3.7.m: it must be enacted by performers through the stupefaction of all the senses. / From recollection of past events, memory arises here;

3.7.s:
bhṛśamutkṣepaṇāttasyāḥ prayogaḥ kāryalolanāt ..
lokaṃ vṛttāntavijñānād vṛttirnāmeha jāyate ..23..
3.7.d:
भृशमुत्क्षेपणात्तस्याः प्रयोगः कार्यलोलनात् ॥
लोकं वृत्तान्तविज्ञानाद् वृत्तिर्नामेह जायते ॥23॥
3.7.m: its performance is through raising [the brows] repeatedly and rolling the eyes toward the object. / From knowledge of the world’s events, fortitude arises here;

3.7.s:
prayojyo labdhabhogena alabdhasya vivarjitam ..
krīḍā nāmeha bhavati cāpalyāddharṣasaṃbhavā .. 24 ..
3.7.d:
प्रयोज्यो लब्धभोगेन अलब्धस्य विवर्जितम् ॥
क्रीडा नामेह भवति चापल्याद्धर्षसंभवा ॥ 24 ॥
3.7.m: it is to be presented through enjoying what has been obtained, avoiding [desire for] what is not obtained. / Sportiveness arises here from inconstancy, born of joy;

3.7.s:
krīḍanena prayojyā sā guruvākyapratikramaiḥ ..
kṛtākāryasya rājendra vrīḍā nāmeha jāyate ..25..
3.7.d:
क्रीडनेन प्रयोज्या सा गुरुवाक्यप्रतिक्रमैः ॥
कृताकार्यस्य राजेन्द्र व्रीडा नामेह जायते ॥25॥
3.7.m: it should be enacted through playing and transgressing the words of elders. / In one who has done what should not be done, O foremost of kings, shame arises here.

3.7.s:
adhomukhena sā kāryā mūle svīkaraṇena ca ..
jñeyā capalatā rājanna vicāryā kriyāvatā .. 26 ..
3.7.d:
अधोमुखेन सा कार्या मूले स्वीकरणेन च ॥
ज्ञेया चपलता राजन्न विचार्या क्रियावता ॥ 26 ॥
3.7.m: It should be enacted with a downcast face and drawing [lines] on the ground. / Inconstancy, O king, is to be understood as unconsidered action by an active person.

3.7.s:
ayameva prayogasya tathaiva samudāhṛtaḥ .. .
manorathānāṃ lābhe tu harṣo nāmeha jāyate ..27..
3.7.d:
अयमेव प्रयोगस्य तथैव समुदाहृतः ॥ ।
मनोरथानां लाभे तु हर्षो नामेह जायते ॥27॥
3.7.m: This very manner of its performance has been explained accordingly. / Upon the attainment of one’s desires, joy arises here;

3.7.s:
sukhaprasādaromāñcaprasvedairdarśayed budhaḥ ..
sambhramājjāyate rājannāvega iti sarvadā ..28..
3.7.d:
सुखप्रसादरोमाञ्चप्रस्वेदैर्दर्शयेद् बुधः ॥
सम्भ्रमाज्जायते राजन्नावेग इति सर्वदा ॥28॥
3.7.m: the wise should show it through ease, serenity, horripilation, and perspiration. / Agitation, O king, always arises from sudden alarm;

3.7.s:
āḥ śabdaiḥ sahasānarthā darśanīyā budhaistu te ..
viṣādasya samutpattiḥ kāryanāśena jāyate .. 09 ..
3.7.d:
आः शब्दैः सहसानर्था दर्शनीया बुधैस्तु ते ॥
विषादस्य समुत्पत्तिः कार्यनाशेन जायते ॥ 09 ॥
3.7.m: its sudden misfortunes should be shown by the wise with cries of 'Ah!' / The arising of despair occurs through the ruin of an undertaking;

3.7.s:
nidrāniḥśvasitavyājaiḥ sābhineyā tathā bhavet ..
utkaṇṭhākaraṇaiḥ sarvairautsukyaṃ nāma jāyate .. 3.31.30 ..
3.7.d:
निद्रानिःश्वसितव्याजैः साभिनेया तथा भवेत् ॥
उत्कण्ठाकरणैः सर्वैरौत्सुक्यं नाम जायते ॥ 3.31.30 ॥
3.7.m: it should be represented through sleepiness, sighs, and pretenses. / From all the causes of longing, impatience arises;

3.7.s:
ālasyagurugātratve dhyānenābhinavaiśca tat ..
rātrijāgaraṇālasyamadairnidreha jāyate .. 31 ..
3.7.d:
आलस्यगुरुगात्रत्वे ध्यानेनाभिनवैश्च तत् ॥
रात्रिजागरणालस्यमदैर्निद्रेह जायते ॥ 31 ॥
3.7.m: that is [to be represented] through indolence, heaviness of limbs, and deep reflection. / Sleep arises here from keeping awake at night, indolence, and intoxication;

3.7.s:
netrābhimardanātkāryā jṛmbhaṇā gātragauravāt ..
apasmārastu bhavati devādīnāṃ prakopataḥ .. 32 ..
3.7.d:
नेत्राभिमर्दनात्कार्या जृम्भणा गात्रगौरवात् ॥
अपस्मारस्तु भवति देवादीनां प्रकोपतः ॥ 32 ॥
3.7.m: it should be enacted through rubbing the eyes, yawning, and heaviness of limbs. / Epilepsy occurs from the wrath of gods and the like;

3.7.s:
niḥsaṃjñatvaṃ samūrddhānaṃ tasyehābhinayo bhavet ..
nidrāsamarthaṃ suptatvaṃ svapanaṃ tatra yojayet .. 33 ..
3.7.d:
निःसंज्ञत्वं समूर्द्धानं तस्येहाभिनयो भवेत् ॥
निद्रासमर्थं सुप्तत्वं स्वपनं तत्र योजयेत् ॥ 33 ॥
3.7.m: its representation here should be unconsciousness accompanied by fallen head. / Lying down fit for sleep—there one should employ slumber;

3.7.s:
nidrocchedāddhi bodhantu jṛmbhaṇaṃ tatra yojayet ..
vidyāśauryadhanādiryairamarṣo nāma jāyate .. 34 ..
3.7.d:
निद्रोच्छेदाद्धि बोधन्तु जृम्भणं तत्र योजयेत् ॥
विद्याशौर्यधनादिर्यैरमर्षो नाम जायते ॥ 34 ॥
3.7.m: and from the cessation of sleep, one should employ awakening and yawning. / From learning, valor, wealth, and the like, indignation arises;

3.7.s:
śirasaḥ kampanaistasya kāryastvabhinayo budhaiḥ ..
dhārṣṭyajaihmayādisambhūto hyavahitthobhayātmakaḥ .. 32..
3.7.d:
शिरसः कम्पनैस्तस्य कार्यस्त्वभिनयो बुधैः ॥
धार्ष्ट्यजैह्मयादिसम्भूतो ह्यवहित्थोभयात्मकः ॥ 32॥
3.7.m: its representation should be enacted by the wise through shaking the head. / Arising from insolence, deceit, and the like, dissimulation has a twofold nature;

3.7.s:
sarvāṃgagopanātkāryo'bhinayo nartanasya ca ..
cauryādijātamarthasya glāniḥ kāryā prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 36..
3.7.d:
सर्वांगगोपनात्कार्योऽभिनयो नर्तनस्य च ॥
चौर्यादिजातमर्थस्य ग्लानिः कार्या प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 36॥
3.7.m: its representation is to be enacted through concealing all the limbs and dancing. / Exhaustion born of the theft and the like of property is to be enacted by performers.

3.7.s:
vātaprāyastathonmādo yathā jñeyo viyogajaḥ ..
asacceṣṭāpralāpena tasyābhinayakāraṇam.. .. 37 ..
3.7.d:
वातप्रायस्तथोन्मादो यथा ज्ञेयो वियोगजः ॥
असच्चेष्टाप्रलापेन तस्याभिनयकारणम्॥ ॥ 37 ॥
3.7.m: Madness is mostly caused by wind, and likewise is to be understood as born of separation; / its dramatic representation is through improper actions and incoherent talk.

3.7.s:
vyādhibhirvā prahārairvā maraṇaṃ nāma jāyate ..
kartavyobhinayastasya mūḍhendriyaviceṣṭanaiḥ .. 38 ..
3.7.d:
व्याधिभिर्वा प्रहारैर्वा मरणं नाम जायते ॥
कर्तव्योभिनयस्तस्य मूढेन्द्रियविचेष्टनैः ॥ 38 ॥
3.7.m: From diseases or from blows, death arises; / its dramatic representation is to be enacted through senseless movements of the faculties.

3.7.s:
mahābhairavanādādyaistrāsaḥ samupajāyate ..
saṃkṣiptāṅgaprakampādyaistasya tvabhinayo bhavet .. 39 ..
3.7.d:
महाभैरवनादाद्यैस्त्रासः समुपजायते ॥
संक्षिप्ताङ्गप्रकम्पाद्यैस्तस्य त्वभिनयो भवेत् ॥ 39 ॥
3.7.m: Terror arises from loud, dreadful sounds and the like; / its dramatic representation should be through contracting the limbs, trembling, and the like.

3.7.s:
vicāraṇārthe saṃdehaḥ kāryo bhūkṣepakampanaiḥ ..
krodho'parādhādbhavati krodhābhinayadarśanaḥ .. 3.31.40..
3.7.d:
विचारणार्थे संदेहः कार्यो भूक्षेपकम्पनैः ॥
क्रोधोऽपराधाद्भवति क्रोधाभिनयदर्शनः ॥ 3.31.40॥
3.7.m: In the case of deliberation, doubt should be enacted through moving the brows and trembling. / Anger arises from an offense; it shows the representation of anger.

3.7.s:
bhayoparādhajo jñeyo dṛgbhayābhinayātmakaḥ ..
manorathāptijo harṣo romāñcena pradarśayet .. 41 ..
3.7.d:
भयोपराधजो ज्ञेयो दृग्भयाभिनयात्मकः ॥
मनोरथाप्तिजो हर्षो रोमाञ्चेन प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 41 ॥
3.7.m: Arising from fear or offense, it is to be known as having the representation of fearful eyes. / Joy born of the attainment of one’s desires should be shown through horripilation.

3.7.s:
bhītakrodhaśca ubhaye romāñcasya samudbhavaḥ ..
svarabhedo bhayādraukṣyātsvarabhedena darśayet .. 42 ..
3.7.d:
भीतक्रोधश्च उभये रोमाञ्चस्य समुद्भवः ॥
स्वरभेदो भयाद्रौक्ष्यात्स्वरभेदेन दर्शयेत् ॥ 42 ॥
3.7.m: In both fear and anger, the arising of horripilation occurs. / Change of voice arises from fear or harshness; one should show it through a broken voice.

3.7.s:
śokānandasamudbhūtamaśru syādrodanena tu ..
varṇāvaratvādvijñeyaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ nāṭyayoktṛbhiḥ ..43..
3.7.d:
शोकानन्दसमुद्भूतमश्रु स्याद्रोदनेन तु ॥
वर्णावरत्वाद्विज्ञेयं वैवर्ण्यं नाट्ययोक्तृभिः ॥43॥
3.7.m: Tears, born of sorrow or joy, occur through weeping. / Pallor is to be known by directors of dramatic performance from a diminution of complexion.

3.7.s:
vaivarṇyaṃ nābhinetavyaṃ prayatnāttaddhi duṣkaram ..
glāniḥ śaṅkābhyasūyā ca śramaścapalatā tathā .. 44 ..
3.7.d:
वैवर्ण्यं नाभिनेतव्यं प्रयत्नात्तद्धि दुष्करम् ॥
ग्लानिः शङ्काभ्यसूया च श्रमश्चपलता तथा ॥ 44 ॥
3.7.m: Pallor should not be represented by effort, for it is difficult to accomplish. / Exhaustion, apprehension, envy, weariness, and inconstancy,

3.7.s:
romāñcaharṣe nidrā ca unmādo mada eva ca..
svedaścaiva vahitthaśca bhāvā hāsyarase smṛtāḥ .. 45 ..
3.7.d:
रोमाञ्चहर्षे निद्रा च उन्मादो मद एव च॥
स्वेदश्चैव वहित्थश्च भावा हास्यरसे स्मृताः ॥ 45 ॥
3.7.m: horripilation, joy, sleep, madness, intoxication, / perspiration, and dissimulation are remembered as states in the comic sentiment.

3.7.s:
ālasyogryajugupsābhirbhāvā hi parivarjitāḥ ..
udbhāvayanti śṛṅgāraṃ rasamāsvādyasaṃjñakam .. 46 ..
3.7.d:
आलस्योग्र्यजुगुप्साभिर्भावा हि परिवर्जिताः ॥
उद्भावयन्ति शृङ्गारं रसमास्वाद्यसंज्ञकम् ॥ 46 ॥
3.7.m: The states, when free from indolence, ferocity, and disgust, / manifest the erotic sentiment, whose designation is enjoyable.

3.7.s:
vedasyaiva ca cintā ca dainyaglānyaśrupātanam ..
jaḍatā maraṇaṃ caiva vyādhiśca karuṇārase .. 47 ..
3.7.d:
वेदस्यैव च चिन्ता च दैन्यग्लान्यश्रुपातनम् ॥
जडता मरणं चैव व्याधिश्च करुणारसे ॥ 47 ॥
3.7.m: Anxiety, wretchedness, exhaustion, shedding of tears, / stupor, death, and disease belong to the pathetic sentiment.

3.7.s:
asammohastathonmādo viṣādo mada eva ca ..
mṛtyurvyādhirbhayaṃ caiva bhāvā bībhatsasaṃśrayāḥ .. 48 ..
3.7.d:
असम्मोहस्तथोन्मादो विषादो मद एव च ॥
मृत्युर्व्याधिर्भयं चैव भावा बीभत्ससंश्रयाः ॥ 48 ॥
3.7.m: Absence of bewilderment, as well as madness, despondency, and intoxication, / death, disease, and fear are the states residing in the odious [sentiment].

3.7.s:
stambhaḥ svedaśca romāñco jugupsā vismayastathā ..
pravego jaḍatā harṣo'sūyā daivādbhute rase .. .. 49 ..
3.7.d:
स्तम्भः स्वेदश्च रोमाञ्चो जुगुप्सा विस्मयस्तथा ॥
प्रवेगो जडता हर्षोऽसूया दैवाद्भुते रसे ॥ ॥ 49 ॥
3.7.m: Paralysis, perspiration, horripilation, disgust, and wonder, / agitation, stupor, joy, and envy belong to the wonderful sentiment pertaining to the divine.

3.7.s:
svedaśca vepathuścaiva romāñco gadgadastathā ..
matiścaiva tathogratvamamarṣo mada eva ca .. 3.31.50 ..
3.7.d:
स्वेदश्च वेपथुश्चैव रोमाञ्चो गद्गदस्तथा ॥
मतिश्चैव तथोग्रत्वममर्षो मद एव च ॥ 3.31.50 ॥
3.7.m: Perspiration, trembling, horripilation, faltering of voice, / intelligence, fieriness, indignation, and intoxication,

3.7.s:
romāñcaḥ svarabhedaśca krodho'sūyā dhṛtistathā ..
garvaścaiva vitarkaśca vīre bhāvā bhavanti vai..51..
3.7.d:
रोमाञ्चः स्वरभेदश्च क्रोधोऽसूया धृतिस्तथा ॥
गर्वश्चैव वितर्कश्च वीरे भावा भवन्ति वै॥51॥
3.7.m: horripilation, change of voice, anger, envy, firmness, / pride, and deliberation are the states that arise in the heroic.

3.7.s:
ye cānye sāttvikā bhāvā nānābhinayayonijāḥ ..
raseṣveteṣu te sarve vijñeyā nāṭyakovidaiḥ ..52..
3.7.d:
ये चान्ये सात्त्विका भावा नानाभिनययोनिजाः ॥
रसेष्वेतेषु ते सर्वे विज्ञेया नाट्यकोविदैः ॥52॥
3.7.m: And whatever other involuntary states arise from the manifold modes of acting, / all those are to be understood in these sentiments by experts in dramatic art.

3.7.s:
bahūnāṃ samavetānāṃ rūpaṃ yasya bhavedbahu ..
sa mantavyo rasaḥ sthāyī śeṣāḥ sañcāriṇaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 53 ..
3.7.d:
बहूनां समवेतानां रूपं यस्य भवेद्बहु ॥
स मन्तव्यो रसः स्थायी शेषाः सञ्चारिणः स्मृताः ॥ 53 ॥
3.7.m: Of many assembled together, that whose form is predominant / should be considered the permanent sentiment; the rest are remembered as transitory.

3.7.s:
śṛṅgāraṃ trividhaṃ vindyādvā nepathyakriyātmakam ..
aṅganepathyabhāvaśca hāsyaraudrau prakīrtitau ..54..
3.7.d:
शृङ्गारं त्रिविधं विन्द्याद्वा नेपथ्यक्रियात्मकम् ॥
अङ्गनेपथ्यभावश्च हास्यरौद्रौ प्रकीर्तितौ ॥54॥
3.7.m: One should know the erotic as threefold, consisting of speech, dress, and action; / and the states of limbs and costume are declared for the comic and furious.

3.7.s:
dharmārthabandhughātena karuṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
yuddhavīraṃ dayāvīraṃ dānavīraṃ tathaiva ca .. 55 ..
3.7.d:
धर्मार्थबन्धुघातेन करुणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ॥
युद्धवीरं दयावीरं दानवीरं तथैव च ॥ 55 ॥
3.7.m: The pathetic is traditionally threefold, arising from the destruction of dharma, wealth, and kin. / Likewise, heroic in battle, heroic in compassion, and heroic in generosity:

3.7.s:
rasaṃ vīramiti prāhustajjñāstrividhameva ca ..
vyājatrāsāparādhaiśca tridhā vidyādbhayānakam .. 56 ..
3.7.d:
रसं वीरमिति प्राहुस्तज्ज्ञास्त्रिविधमेव च ॥
व्याजत्रासापराधैश्च त्रिधा विद्याद्भयानकम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.7.m: the connoisseurs declare the heroic sentiment to be threefold in this way. / And one should know the terrible as threefold: through pretexts, fright, and transgression.

3.7.s:
na hyekarasajaṃ kāvyaṃ kiñcidasti prayogajam ..
bhāvo vāpi raso vāpi pravṛttirvṛttireva ca ..57..
3.7.d:
न ह्येकरसजं काव्यं किञ्चिदस्ति प्रयोगजम् ॥
भावो वापि रसो वापि प्रवृत्तिर्वृत्तिरेव च ॥57॥
3.7.m: Indeed, no dramatic work produced through performance arises from a single sentiment alone, / nor does a state, a sentiment, a regional style, or a dramatic style.

3.7.s:
ekonapañcāśadime samagrā bhāvavyavasthā gaditā mayā te ..
yuktyā ca ye yatra rase niyuktāḥ proktaṃ tadapyatra narendracandra .. 58..
3.7.d:
एकोनपञ्चाशदिमे समग्रा भावव्यवस्था गदिता मया ते ॥
युक्त्या च ये यत्र रसे नियुक्ताः प्रोक्तं तदप्यत्र नरेन्द्रचन्द्र ॥ 58॥
3.7.m: These forty-nine states in their entirety have been described by me to you as an orderly system; / and which ones are employed by rule in which sentiment has also been stated here, O moon among kings.

3.7.s:
3.32
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
athāto mudrāhastān vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ..
vāsasya prasāritāṅguṣṭhasyopari yadā kubjatarjanī bhavati tadoṅkāraḥ ..

sarvādhaḥparaṃ rekhāgatayā tavargaḥ .
tadupari bavaśatayaiḥ pavargaḥ.
tarjanyādyastu prathamaparvagatayā pavargaḥ.
agreṣu śavargaḥ.

kanīyasyā kanīyasī ceti, tarjanyā tarjanī aṅguṣṭhenāṅguṣṭha iti tārkṣyamudrā .

3.7.d:
3.32
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अथातो मुद्राहस्तान् व्याख्यास्यामः ॥
वासस्य प्रसारिताङ्गुष्ठस्योपरि यदा कुब्जतर्जनी भवति तदोङ्कारः ॥
करमध्य गतासु सर्वास्वंगुलीषु क्रमात्कुब्जीकृतास्वङ्गुष्ठाद्यासु अ इ उ ए ओ प्रसारितासु अ इ उ ऊ ऐ ओ अं मुकुलः अः मुकुलविशेषः अङ्गुष्ठमूलगतया परहस्ततर्जन्या क्रमात्कवर्गः।
सर्वाधःपरं रेखागतया तवर्गः ।
तदुपरि बवशतयैः पवर्गः।
तर्जन्याद्यस्तु प्रथमपर्वगतया पवर्गः।
अग्रेषु शवर्गः।
मध्यमा नखस्पर्शे र क्ष इति ।
अ वासुदेवः ।
आ सङ्कर्षणः। अं प्रद्युम्नः ।
अः अनिरुद्धः ।
अञ्जलिपुरुषः करयोः परस्परपृष्ठलग्नयोः ।
कनीयस्या कनीयसी चेति, तर्जन्या तर्जनी अङ्गुष्ठेनाङ्गुष्ठ इति तार्क्ष्यमुद्रा ।
पताकः कुञ्चिताग्रस्तालः तिर्यक्प्रसारिताङ्गुष्ठो मकरः।
कुञ्चिताङ्गुलिरर्धचन्द्रः ।
दृश्यशिखरौ कनीयस्यङ्गुल्यग्रलग्नौ ।
संहताङ्गुष्ठः शंखः ।
अः कारौ संहतौ स्पष्टाङ्गुलौ पद्मः ॥
कुब्जाङ्गुष्ठो लक्ष्मीः ।
मकरः प्रसारिताङ्गुलिः ।
शेषस्तदुपरि शिखरे भोगशमनः ।
अः कार एव प्रसारितमध्यमाङ्गुलिर्ग ऊउः ।
तत्रैव मध्यमाङ्गुलिः शिखरगृहीता गरुडवाहनम् ।
मध्यमानामिकयोरङ्गुष्ठयोश्चाग्रयोगे चक्रः ।
उपर्युपरि कपित्थयोरुपरि चिबुके गदा ।
कपित्थकुब्जमध्यमिको हलः ।
कर्कटके सुमूलम् ।
कपित्थमध्यभ्रष्टाङ्गुलिः ।
चर्म कपित्थं पृष्ठतलाङ्गुलिः खड्गः शिखरो मध्यभ्रष्टाङ्गुलिर्धनुः ।
तर्जनीमध्यमिकोङ्गुष्ठानां संहतानां वियोगाच्छरः।
मुकुलसञ्चितकनीनिकः कौस्तुभः ।
द्वौ शिखरौ पृथक् वनमाला ।
अः कारो पृथग्लग्नो नृसिंहः ।
शिखरप्रसारितकनीनिकाधो वराहः ।
इ हयशिरः ।
ओं वामनः ।
वितलि स्त्रिविक्रमः ।
अर्धचन्द्रो मत्स्यः।
अधोमुखः कुज्जपताकः कूर्मः।
शिखरप्रसारितकनीयानूर्ध्वमुखाङ्गुष्ठो हंसः।
पताकः कुब्जकरमध्यो दत्तात्रेयः॥
कपित्थः परशुरामः ।
द्वौ शिखरौ युक्तौ दाशरथी।
पताकः कृष्णः। त्रिपताको बलदेवः ।
शिखरो विष्णुः ।
उत्तानपताकः पृथिवी ।
कुब्जः पताकः प्रसारितोङ्गुष्ठ स्तोयः ।
अङ्गुष्ठाग्राङ्गुलिर्नखपरिमार्जितोऽग्निः ।
चलत्पताको वायुः ।
तिर्यङ्मुष्टिप्रसारिततर्जनीकोऽन्तरिक्षम् ।
वितस्तिद्वययोगो वर्तुलीकृतोऽर्कः अनामिकार्धेन वक्रश्चन्द्रः ।
सर्वासुमुकुलितासु प्रसारिते मध्यमा तर्जनी नरनारायणौ ।
तत्रैव प्रसारिताग्रनासिका गुणाः ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ।
वामस्य प्रसारिताङ्गुलेस्तदुपरि तथाविध एव दक्षिणः कपिलः ।
चतस्रोप्यंगुल्यः प्रसारितस्तन्मूले कुञ्चिताङ्गुष्ठश्चान्तरात्मा तोयः ।
प्रसारितकनि ष्ठिको ऋग्वेदः ।
सैवानामिकया सह प्रसारितो यजुर्वेदः ॥
चतुरात्मा प्रसारितांगुष्ठः सामवेदः ।
वेष्ट्यमानास्वंगुलीषु करमध्यगमनेन गायत्री ।
सामवेदोऽधोमुखांगुलिः शिक्षा ।
सैव दक्षिणदिशि नीता कल्पः ।
तर्जन्यंगुष्ठयोगे व्याकरणम् ।
शिखरेंगुष्ठेन तर्जनीमध्यगेन निरुक्तम् ।
खटकामुखाभ्यां ज्योतिषम् ।
अधोमुखश्छन्दोविचितिः ॥
एता रहस्यमुद्रास्ते मयोक्ता नृपसत्तम ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सामान्यांस्तान्निबोध मे ॥

3.32
The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, therefore, we shall explain the hand-gestures.
When the bent forefinger is over the extended thumb of the left [hand], that is oṃkāra.
When all the fingers have entered the palm of the hand and are curled in succession, beginning with the thumb, [they form] a, i, u, e, o; when extended, a, i, u, ū, ai, o, aṃ; [it is] mukula; aḥ is a special mukula. With the forefinger of the other hand placed at the base of the thumb, [it forms] the ka-varga in succession.
Placed on the line furthest below all, [it forms] the ta-varga.
Above that, with groups of b, v, and ś, the pa-varga.
The forefinger and others, when placed on the first knuckle, [form] the pa-varga.
On the tips, the śa-varga.
Upon touching the nail of the middle finger, ra and kṣa.
a is Vāsudeva.
ā is Saṅkarṣaṇa; aṃ is Pradyumna;
aḥ is Aniruddha.
Añjalipuruṣa is with the backs of the two hands joined to each other.
Little finger with little finger, forefinger with forefinger, and thumb with thumb: this is the Tārkṣya-mudrā.
Patāka with its tip bent is tāla; with the thumb extended sideways, it is makara.
With the fingers bent, it is ardhacandra.
Two visible śikharas joined at the tips of the little fingers [form …].
With the thumbs pressed together, it is a conch.
Two aḥ-kāras joined with clearly separated fingers form a lotus.
With the thumb bent, it is Lakṣmī.
With the fingers extended, it is a makara.
Śeṣa is on the śikhara above that, destroying worldly enjoyment.
The aḥ-kāra itself with the middle finger extended is Garuḍa.
The middle finger right there, held by a śikhara, is the mount of Garuḍa.
When the tips of the middle and ring fingers join with the thumbs, it is a discus.
With two kapitthas one above the other held at the chin, it is a mace.
Kapittha with the middle finger bent is a plough.
In karkaṭaka, it is sumūla.
Kapittha with the middle finger dropped [is …].
Kapittha is a shield; with fingers on the back of the palm, a sword; śikhara with the middle finger dropped is a bow.
From the separation of the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb when joined together, an arrow.
With the little finger drawn into a mukula, it is the Kaustubha.
Two separate śikharas are a garland of forest flowers.
aḥ-kāra joined separately is Nṛsiṃha.
A śikhara with the little finger extended downwards is Varāha.
i is the Horse-headed One.
oṃ is Vāmana.
Vitolita is Trivikrama.
Ardhacandra is the Fish.
With face turned down, a bent patāka is the Tortoise.
A śikhara with the little finger extended and the thumb turned upward is the Swan.
Patāka with the middle of the palm hollowed is Dattātreya.
Kapittha is Paraśurāma.
Two śikharas joined together are the two sons of Daśaratha.
Patāka is Kṛṣṇa; tripatāka is Baladeva.
Śikhara is Viṣṇu.
An upturned patāka is the earth.
A bent patāka with the thumb extended is water.
Fingers with the thumb-tip wiped over the nails is fire.
A trembling patāka is wind.
A fist held sideways with the forefinger extended is the intermediate space.
The union of two spans formed into a circle is the sun; curved with half the ring finger, it is the moon.
When all are formed into a mukula and the middle and forefinger are extended, they are Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
In that very [gesture], with the nose-tip extended, [they are] the qualities: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.
With fingers of the left hand extended, and the right hand likewise placed above it, it is Kapila.
All four fingers extended, with the thumb bent at their base, is the inner self, water.
With the little finger extended, it is the Ṛgveda.
That same [gesture] with the ring finger extended is the Yajurveda.
Caturātmā with the thumb extended is the Sāmaveda.
With the fingers being enveloped as they enter the middle of the palm, it is Gāyatrī.
The Sāmaveda [hand] with fingers turned downward is Śikṣā.
That very [hand] led to the right direction is Kalpa.
In the union of the forefinger and thumb is Vyākaraṇa.
In śikhara, with the thumb placed between the forefinger and middle finger, it is Nirukta.
With two khaṭakāmukhas, Jyotiṣa.
Turned downward, it is Chandoviciti.
These secret mudrās have been spoken to you by me, O best of kings.
Hereafter, I shall declare the common ones; listen to them from me.

3.7.d:
3.33
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
उत्तानं तु करं कृत्वा चतुरांगुलिकुञ्चितम् ॥
अंगुष्ठपार्श्वतो योज्यो भस्ममुद्राप्रकार्तिता ॥1॥
सा तिर्यगुच्छ्रितांगुलिलिङ्गमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
अंगुल्यस्त्रयः सकोऽस्याग्रांगुष्ठपरिसंचिताः ॥ 2 ॥
तर्जनीं प्रसृतां कृत्वा जटामुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
वेत्रमुद्रा यदा तस्यां नेत्रान्ते तर्जनी भवेत ॥ 3 ॥
बन्धस्थां तु प्रकुर्वीत चांगुष्ठं प्रसृतं तथा ॥
उत्तानं मूर्ध्नि संयोज्यं शशाङ्कं तु विनिर्दिशेत् ॥4 ॥
अंगुल्यः प्रसृताः सर्वा वर्तुलाः शृङ्गरूपकाः ॥
मूर्ध्नि कृत्वा तु तां मुद्रां गोवृषं तु विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 5 ॥
तिर्यक्कृत्वा तु तं हस्तं सर्वसङ्कुचितांगुलिम् ॥
अंगुष्ठं मध्यमावेष्ट्य पर्यस्तं तु विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 6 ॥
कनिष्ठिकां सङ्कुचितामंगुष्ठोपरि विन्यसेत् ॥
कनिष्ठानामिकामध्ये दक्षांगुष्ठं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.7.m:
3.33
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having made the palm upturned, with four fingers bent, / the thumb should be joined at the side; this is proclaimed as the bhasma-mudrā.
That [hand] with fingers raised obliquely is proclaimed as the liṅga-mudrā. / Three fingers with their tips gathered together with the thumb,
and having the forefinger extended, is proclaimed as the jaṭā-mudrā. / It is the vetra-mudrā when the forefinger in it is at the corner of the eye.
One should hold [the hand] firm and extend the thumb; / joined face upward on the head, one should indicate the moon.
All fingers extended, curved in the shape of horns; / having made that mudrā on the head, one should indicate the bull.
Holding that hand obliquely with all fingers contracted, / wrapping the middle finger around the thumb, one should indicate 'thrown down' (paryasta).
One should place the contracted little finger over the thumb; / the right thumb is placed between the little finger and the ring finger.

उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा अन्योन्यान्तरितांगुली ॥
कनिष्ठिकान्ते चांगुष्ठमनन्तेति प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 8 ॥
उत्तानं दक्षिणं हस्तं त्वधो वामं तथोपरि ॥
करजान्योन्यसंयोगाद्धर्मस्य परिकीर्तिता ॥ 9 ॥
सा चैव विपरीता तु ज्ञानस्य परिकीर्तितम् ॥
कनिष्ठिके द्वे चांगुष्ठौ युग्मीकृत्वा प्रसारयेत् ॥ 3.33.10 ॥
वैराग्यस्य भवेन्मुद्रा सर्वकर्मकरी शुभा ॥
पृष्ठे पृष्ठं तु संयोज्यं करयोरुभयोरपि ॥ 11 ॥
कनीन्यंगुष्ठयोगेन भवत्यैश्वर्यमेव च ॥
पद्माकारो भवेद्धस्तः कनिष्ठातर्जनीयुतः ॥ 12 ॥
चतस्र उच्छ्रिताः कृत्वा पृष्ठेन्योन्यं तु योजयेत् ॥
अंगुष्ठावेकतः कृत्वा प्रणालं चैव कारयेत् ॥ 13 ॥
सकलस्य भवेन्मुद्रा दुष्टानां शमनी शुभा ॥
त्रयः सङ्कुचिता यत्र कनिष्ठांगुष्ठकेकलाः ॥ 14 ॥
3.7.m:
Having turned both hands face upward, with the fingers interlaced with one another, / and the thumb at the edge of the little finger, it is proclaimed as the Anantā [mudrā].
The right hand turned face upward, and the left turned face downward above it; / by joining the fingernails of one another, it is proclaimed [the mudrā] of Dharma.
And that very [mudrā] reversed is proclaimed [the mudrā] of Knowledge. / Having paired the two little fingers and the two thumbs, one should extend them;
it is the auspicious mudrā of Dispassion, which accomplishes all rituals. / Joining back to back of both hands,
by connecting the little fingers and thumbs, it becomes Sovereignty. / The hand should take the shape of a lotus, joined with the little finger and forefinger.
Having raised four [fingers], one should join them back to back; / having brought the thumbs together on one side, one should form a spout.
It is the auspicious mudrā of the Manifest (sakala), which quells the wicked. / Where three [fingers] are contracted, and the little finger and thumb are separate,

उत्तानं दक्षिणांगुष्ठं वामांगुष्ठेन वेष्टयेत् ॥
दक्षिणांगुलिभिश्चात्र वामांगुष्ठं तु वेष्टयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
वामस्यांगुलिभिश्चात्र त्वंगुली परिवेष्टयेत् ॥
तर्जन्यौ कुञ्चितौ कृत्वा मुद्रा निष्कलरूपिणी ॥16॥
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा अंगुष्ठांगुलिकुञ्चितौ ॥
करमध्यस्थिता ह्येता नखाम्̐स्तासां तु गोपयेत् ॥ 17 ॥
पृष्ठं पृष्ठे तु संयोज्य त्वंगुष्ठौ विन्यसेत्समम् ॥
मालाकारं ततः कृत्वा देव्या मुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 18 ॥
अंगुष्ठोंगुष्ठके योज्यः कनिष्ठायां कनिष्ठिका ॥
करमध्ये तु तां कृत्वा षडाभ्यामेकतः कुरु ॥ 19 ॥
सकुच्य तु षडेतानि शक्त्याकारं तु कारयेत् ॥
स्कंदस्य तु स्मृता मुद्रा अभेद्या त्रिदशैरपि ॥ 3.33.20 ॥
अधोमुखं करं कृत्वा तिस्रोंगुल्यस्तु कुञ्चिताः ॥
त्रिताला मध्यमा तत्र किंचित्सङ्कुचिता भवेत् ॥ 21 ॥
3.7.m:
one should wrap the left thumb around the right thumb [turned] face upward; / and with the fingers of the right, one should wrap the left thumb.
And with the fingers of the left, one should wrap those fingers; / bending the two forefingers, this is the mudrā embodying the Unmanifest (niṣkala).
Having turned both hands face upward, with thumbs and fingers bent, / these being placed in the middle of the palms, one should conceal their nails.
Joining back to back, one should place the two thumbs evenly; / having then formed the shape of a garland, it is proclaimed the mudrā of the Goddess.
The thumb should be joined to the thumb, the little finger to the little finger; / having placed them in the middle of the hand, join these six together on one side.
Contracting these six, one should make the shape of a spear; / this is remembered as the mudrā of Skanda, unbreakable even by the gods.
Having turned the hand face downward, three fingers are bent; / there the middle finger of three spans should be slightly contracted.

3.7.d:
तर्जन्यां योजयांगुष्ठे दन्ताकारं तु दर्शयेत ॥
विघ्नराजस्य मुद्रैषा सर्वविघ्नप्रणाशिनी ॥ 22 ॥
उत्तानौ प्रसृतौ हस्तौ तर्जन्यंगुष्ठसंवृतौ ॥
अस्य वामौ तु संयोज्य शक्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 23 ॥
संकोच्य करजां मध्यां हस्तयोरुभयोरपि ॥
प्रसृतांगुष्ठमुत्तानां योज्या मुद्रा हुताशने ॥ 24 ॥
अधोमुखं करं कृत्वा यस्य स्यात्कुंचितांगुलिः॥
विरूपाक्षस्य मुद्रैषा भवेन्मध्या प्रसारिता ॥ 25 ॥
उत्ताने प्रसृतांगुल्यः करे भवति वारुणी ॥
तामेव तु यदा तिर्यक्तदा भवति मारुती ॥ 26॥
निकुंचिताश्च ताः सर्वाः कौबेरी तु प्रकीर्तिता ॥
मध्ये प्रसारितास्तिस्रो मुद्रेशानी प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 27 ॥
ब्रह्मजा पद्ममुद्रा स्याद्भोगोऽनंतस्य कीर्तिता ॥

3.7.m:
Join the thumb to the forefinger, and display the shape of a tusk; / this is the mudrā of the Lord of Obstacles, destroying all obstacles.
Both hands extended face upward, covered by the forefinger and thumb; / joining his left [fingers], it is proclaimed the mudrā of Śakra.
Contracting the nail of the middle finger of both hands, / with the thumb extended face upward, the mudrā is to be employed for the Fire-God.
Having turned the hand face downward, whose fingers are bent,
with the middle finger extended, this is the mudrā of Virūpākṣa.
With fingers extended on a hand turned face upward, it becomes the [mudrā] of Varuṇa; / and when that very [hand] is held obliquely, then it becomes the [mudrā] of the Wind-God.
And when all of them are bent, it is proclaimed the [mudrā] of Kubera. / Three extended in the middle is proclaimed the [mudrā] of Īśāna.
The lotus mudrā born of Brahmā is proclaimed the hood of Ananta. / When the left is fastened to the left, and upon withdrawal of the right [fingers],

तयोरग्राणि गृह्णीत तर्जन्यग्रद्वयेन तु ॥
संकोचयेत्षडेतानि स्वांगुष्ठे तर्जनीं न्यसेत् ॥ 29 ॥
वज्र एषः समाख्यातः शक्तिः पूर्वमुदाहृता ॥
करौ बाहुद्वयं चैव दण्डमुद्रा प्रसारिता ॥ 3.33.30 ॥
कनिष्ठानामिके द्वेद्वे अन्तर्यांगुष्ठकुंचितौ ॥
चत्वारः प्रसृता युग्मः खड्गमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 31 ॥
वर्तुलां तर्जनीं कृत्वा अंगुष्ठोपरि विन्यसेत् ॥
दक्षिणं तर्जनी चैव तस्यास्ये तु नियोजयेत् ॥ 32 ॥
दक्षिणं कुंचितं कृत्वा तिस्रो वामाः प्रसारिताः ॥
मुष्टिं कृत्वा तु वामेन त्वंगुष्ठं तु समुच्छ्रयेत ॥ 33 ॥
अंगुष्ठेन तु संगृह्य पताका प्रसृता करा ॥
तिर्यक्करं तु कृत्वा वै सङ्कुच्य चतुरंगुलीः ॥ 34 ॥
अंगुष्ठं प्रसृतं कृत्वा गदामुद्रा तथा परा ॥
अन्योन्यं योजयेद्धस्तौ कनिष्ठांगुष्ठयोजितौ ॥ 35 ॥
3.7.m:
one should grasp their tips with the tips of both forefingers; / one should contract these six, and place the forefinger on its own thumb.
This is declared to be the vajra; the spear was mentioned before. / Both hands and both arms extended is the daṇḍa mudrā.
Two little fingers and two ring fingers, with the thumbs bent inward; / four [fingers] extended in a pair is proclaimed the sword mudrā.
Having curved the forefinger, one should place it over the thumb; / and one should join the right forefinger to its tip.
Having bent the right [hand], three left [fingers] are extended; / making a fist with the left [hand], one should raise the thumb.
Grasping with the thumb, the hands are extended like flags; / having held the hand obliquely, contracting four fingers,
and extending the thumb, that is another, the mace mudrā. / One should join the hands to one another, with the little fingers and thumbs joined.

3.7.d:
तदेव युग्मं प्रसृता शूलमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
नित्यं प्रसारयेद्धस्तं स्वल्पाकारं तु योजयेत् ॥ 36 ॥
मध्यमेकन्यसेद्द्वेद्वे प्रसृताग्रे नियोजयेत् ॥
तर्जनीद्वयं संकुच्य मध्यमापृष्ठसंस्थिता ॥ 37 ॥
द्रव्यरूपा स्मृता ह्येषा आत्मभावे नियोजयेत् ॥
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा षडेतेंगुलयः स्मृताः ॥ 38 ॥
समानाः सुसमानाश्च योजिता वैष्णवी भवेत् ॥
तर्जन्यौ कुंचिते कृत्वा मध्यमा पृष्ठतो न्यसेत् ॥ 39 ॥
कनिष्ठोपरि चांगुष्ठौ वृतमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
उत्तानं वामहस्तं च दक्षिणं चाप्यधोमुखम् ॥ 3.33.40 ॥
मध्यमानामिके द्वे द्वे संकुच्यांगुष्ठसंस्थिते ॥
तर्जनीकन्यका चैव मध्यमाभ्यां समाक्रमेत् ॥ 41 ॥
द्वितीया द्रव्यरूपी च गन्धमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा कनिष्ठानामिका तथा ॥ 42 ॥
3.7.m:
That same pair extended is proclaimed the trident mudrā. / One should constantly extend the hand, making it small in form.
One should place one in the middle, and join two each at their extended tips; / having contracted the two forefingers, they rest on the back of the middle fingers.
This is remembered as the substance mudrā; one should apply it to one's own state. / Having turned both hands face upward, these six fingers are remembered;
equal and perfectly matched, when joined, it becomes the Vaiṣṇavī [mudrā]. / Having bent the two forefingers, one should place the middle fingers behind them.
With the thumbs over the little fingers, it is proclaimed the vṛta mudrā. / The left hand turned face upward and the right turned face downward,
two middle fingers and two ring fingers contracted and resting on the thumbs; / and the forefinger and little finger should press down with the middle fingers.
This second, embodying substance, is proclaimed the perfume mudrā. / Having turned both hands face upward, likewise the little and ring fingers;

3.7.d:
संकोचयित्वा चत्वारो मध्यमे द्वे प्रसारयेत् ॥
अंगुष्ठगे च तर्जन्यौ पुष्पमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 43 ॥
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा षडंगुलिनिकुंचितौ ॥
प्रसृते तर्जनीं कृत्वा चाग्रमग्रे नियोजयेत् ॥ 44 ॥
तयोर्मूले तथांगुष्ठौ धूममुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
तर्जन्या तर्जनी यत्र कनीयस्या कनीयसी ॥ 45 ॥
चतस्र उच्छ्रिताः कृत्वा पृष्ठं पृष्ठे नियोजयेत् ॥
अंगुष्ठावुच्छ्रितौ कृत्वा दीपमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 46 ॥
उच्छ्रितांगुलयः सर्वाः कनीयोरुभयोरपि ॥
पृष्ठं पृष्ठे तु संयोज्य अंगुष्ठाग्रे नियोजयेत् ॥ 47 ॥
नैवेद्यमुद्रा कथिता फलकारकरा शुभा ॥
अंगुल्यः संहताः सर्वास्तथा संकुचिताश्च याः ॥ 48 ॥
पुष्पमुद्रा विनिर्दिष्टा द्वितीया यदुनन्दन ॥
अंगुष्ठौ चैकतः कृत्वा अनामा च कनीयसी॥49॥
3.7.m:
having contracted the four, one should extend the two middle fingers; / and with the forefingers touching the thumbs, it is proclaimed the flower mudrā.
Having turned both hands face upward, with six fingers bent, / having extended the forefingers, one should join tip to tip.
Likewise, the two thumbs at their bases is proclaimed the incense mudrā. / Where forefinger is [joined] to forefinger and little finger to little finger,
having raised four [fingers], one should join back to back; / having raised the two thumbs, it is proclaimed the lamp mudrā.
With all fingers raised, and joining back to back
of both little fingers, one should place them at the tips of the thumbs.
This is declared to be the auspicious Naivedyamudrā, which brings about fruits.
When all fingers are drawn together and likewise contracted,
it is taught as the second Puṣpamudrā, O scion of Yadu.

मध्यमे द्वे च संकोच्य अनामा पृष्ठतो न्यसेत् ॥
दत्त्वा चैव तु तर्जन्यौ मध्यमाः परिविन्यसेत् ॥ 3.33.50 ॥
महामुद्रा भवत्येषा सर्वद्रव्यप्रपूरणी ॥

संयोज्य मध्यमे स्वाग्रं तर्जनीद्वयमेव च ॥
कनिष्ठाद्ये तथा द्वेद्वे स्वाग्रे नाम्नि नियोजयेत् ॥ 52 ॥
अर्धस्थितौ तथांगुष्ठौ अमृताख्या प्रकीर्तिता ॥
चण्डीशमुद्रा कथिता अञ्जलिः कुब्जतर्जनी ॥ ॥ 53 ॥
अस्त्रमुद्रा भवेद्राजन् पद्मः स्यात्संहताञ्जलिः ॥
दक्षिणेन तु हस्तेन मुष्टिं बद्ध्वा प्रयत्नतः ॥ 54 ॥
अडुष्ठमुन्नतं कृत्वा वामाङ्गुष्ठे तु निक्षिपेत् ॥
दक्षिणां च तथा मुष्टिं वामाङ्गुल्या तु वेष्टयेत् ॥ 55 ॥
सद्योजातस्य मुद्रैषा कथिता पापनाशिनी ॥
इयमेव विपर्यस्ता वामदेवस्य कीर्तिता ॥ 56 ॥
3.7.m:
and contracting both middle fingers, one should place them behind the ring fingers;
and having placed both index fingers, one should arrange the middle fingers.
This becomes the Mahāmudrā, which fills all objects.
When the two ring and middle fingers are interlaced with each other,
and both middle fingers are joined at their tips, as well as both index fingers,
and likewise each pair beginning with the little finger are joined at their tips to their counterparts,
with both thumbs placed halfway, it is proclaimed as the one named Amṛtā.
The gesture of hollowed palms with bent index fingers is declared to be the Caṇḍīśamudrā.
It becomes the Astramudrā, O king; the hollowed palms joined closely together becomes the lotus [mudrā].
Having carefully formed a fist with the right hand,
and raising the thumb, one should insert it into the left thumb;
and similarly, one should wrap the right fist with the left fingers.
This is declared to be the mudrā of Sadyojāta, which destroys sins.
This very same [gesture] reversed is proclaimed for Vāmadeva.

3.7.d:
ग्राह्या दक्षिणमुष्ट्या तु मुद्रा सर्वात्मना भवेत् ॥
वाममुष्टौ तथाङ्गुष्ठं दक्षिणं प्रक्षिपेद्बुधः ॥ 65 ॥
3.7.m:
it should be grasped with the right fist—this becomes the mudrā of the Universal Soul.
Likewise, the wise person should insert the right thumb into the left fist;

3.7.s:
karajā pṛṣṭhato yojyā mudraiṣā śivasaṃjñitā..
aṅgulyontarhitāḥ sarvā vartulā garbhasaṃsthitā .. 66 ..
3.7.d:
करजा पृष्ठतो योज्या मुद्रैषा शिवसंज्ञिता॥
अङ्गुल्योन्तर्हिताः सर्वा वर्तुला गर्भसंस्थिता ॥ 66 ॥
3.7.m:
the fingernails should be joined at the back—this is the mudrā named Śiva.
When all fingers are tucked inside, rounded, situated in the interior,

3.7.s:
prasṛtā madhyamā yuktā śikhāmudrā prakīrtitā ..
adhomukhāstu vai tisraḥ tiryaktāśca susaṃsthitāḥ .. 67 ..
3.7.d:
प्रसृता मध्यमा युक्ता शिखामुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
अधोमुखास्तु वै तिस्रः तिर्यक्ताश्च सुसंस्थिताः ॥ 67 ॥
3.7.m:
and the extended middle finger is joined, it is proclaimed as the Śikhāmudrā.
Three fingers turned downward and positioned sideways,

3.7.s:
kanīyasyupari tvāsāṃ tāśca sarvā adhomukhāḥ ..
tāsāmupari cāṅguṣṭhe dakṣiṇaṃ samprayojayeta .. 68 ..
3.7.d:
कनीयस्युपरि त्वासां ताश्च सर्वा अधोमुखाः ॥
तासामुपरि चाङ्गुष्ठे दक्षिणं सम्प्रयोजयेत ॥ 68 ॥
3.7.m:
all of them turned downward above the little finger;
and above them, on the thumbs, one should apply the right [finger].

3.7.s:
vāme dharmajñamudraiṣā kathitā lāṅgalasya tu ..
bandhe tvanāmikā tvasminmudrā hyastrasya kīrtitā .. 69 ..
3.7.d:
वामे धर्मज्ञमुद्रैषा कथिता लाङ्गलस्य तु ॥
बन्धे त्वनामिका त्वस्मिन्मुद्रा ह्यस्त्रस्य कीर्तिता ॥ 69 ॥
3.7.m:
On the left, O knower of dharma, this mudrā is declared to be that of the plow;
but when the ring finger is bound in this [gesture], it is proclaimed as the mudrā of the weapon.

3.7.s:
uttānau tu karau kṛtvā ubhāvekatra yojayeta ..
karajāstu smṛtāḥ sarvā mudrā gāyatrasaṃjñitāḥ .. 3.33.70 ..
3.7.d:
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा उभावेकत्र योजयेत ॥
करजास्तु स्मृताः सर्वा मुद्रा गायत्रसंज्ञिताः ॥ 3.33.70 ॥
3.7.m:
Having turned both hands upward, one should join them both together;
all fingernails are remembered [thus] in the mudrā named Gāyatra.

3.7.s:
muṣṭau prasārayedekāmaṃgulīṃ tu kramānnṛpa ..
tarjanyantāṃ kaniṣṭhādyāṃ śaktimudrā prakīrtitā .. 71 ..
3.7.d:
मुष्टौ प्रसारयेदेकामंगुलीं तु क्रमान्नृप ॥
तर्जन्यन्तां कनिष्ठाद्यां शक्तिमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 71 ॥
3.7.m:
From a fist, one should extend one finger in succession, O king,
beginning with the little finger and ending with the index finger—this is proclaimed as the Śaktimudrā.

3.7.s:
hṛdi nyasto'ñjalirjñeyo namaskāro narādhipa ..
kapitthayajanīṃ gṛhya śikhareṇa dhvajo bhaveta .. 72 ..
3.7.d:
हृदि न्यस्तोऽञ्जलिर्ज्ञेयो नमस्कारो नराधिप ॥
कपित्थयजनीं गृह्य शिखरेण ध्वजो भवेत ॥ 72 ॥
3.7.m:
The hollowed palms placed at the heart is to be known as Namaskāra, O lord of men.
Taking the Kapittha-holding [gesture], with the Śikhara it becomes the banner.

3.7.s:
aṅguṣṭhe yojya tarjanyau hastottānau smṛtāṅgulī ..
maṇibandhau nipīḍyaiva śaśikarṇī bhavennṛpa .. 73 ..
3.7.d:
अङ्गुष्ठे योज्य तर्जन्यौ हस्तोत्तानौ स्मृताङ्गुली ॥
मणिबन्धौ निपीड्यैव शशिकर्णी भवेन्नृप ॥ 73 ॥
3.7.m:
Joining the index fingers to the thumb, with the hands turned upward and fingers remembered [as such],
and pressing the wrists, it becomes the Śaśikarṇī, O king.

3.7.s:
sampuṭīkṛtya hastau dvau kiñcitsaṅkucitāṅguliḥ ..
mukulā tu samākhyātā paṅkajaṃ prasṛtaiva sā ..74 ..
3.7.d:
सम्पुटीकृत्य हस्तौ द्वौ किञ्चित्सङ्कुचिताङ्गुलिः ॥
मुकुला तु समाख्याता पङ्कजं प्रसृतैव सा ॥74 ॥
3.7.m:
Cupping both hands with the fingers slightly contracted,
it is proclaimed as Mukulā; that very same [gesture] expanded is the lotus.

3.7.s:
uttāno tu sṛtau hastau kṛtvāṅguṣṭhau tu kuñcitau ..
madhyasaṃsthau karau kṛtvā āvāhanyāstu lakṣaṇam .. 75 ..
3.7.d:
उत्तानो तु सृतौ हस्तौ कृत्वाङ्गुष्ठौ तु कुञ्चितौ ॥
मध्यसंस्थौ करौ कृत्वा आवाहन्यास्तु लक्षणम् ॥ 75 ॥
3.7.m:
Turning the hands upward and spreading them, with the thumbs bent,
and placing both hands in the middle, this is the characteristic of the Āvāhanī.

3.7.s:
aṅguṣṭhau kuñcitau dvau tu svakīyāṅguliveṣṭitau ..
ubhau cābhimukhau hastau yojayitvā tu riṣṭrarā .. 76 ..
3.7.d:
अङ्गुष्ठौ कुञ्चितौ द्वौ तु स्वकीयाङ्गुलिवेष्टितौ ॥
उभौ चाभिमुखौ हस्तौ योजयित्वा तु रिष्ट्ररा ॥ 76 ॥
3.7.m:
Both thumbs bent, wrapped by their own fingers,
and having joined both hands facing each other, O protector of the realm,

3.7.s:
uttānaṃ dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhaṃ vāmāṅguṣṭhena veṣṭayet ..
bhrāmayedvartulāṅguṣṭhā mudrā proktā visarjane .. 77 ..
3.7.d:
उत्तानं दक्षिणाङ्गुष्ठं वामाङ्गुष्ठेन वेष्टयेत् ॥
भ्रामयेद्वर्तुलाङ्गुष्ठा मुद्रा प्रोक्ता विसर्जने ॥ 77 ॥
3.7.m:
one should wrap the upturned right thumb with the left thumb;
rotating the thumbs in a circle, this mudrā is declared for dismissal.

3.7.s:
vitastidvayasaṃyogādbhadramudrā prakīrtitā ..
muṣṭiḥ pramārjitā jñeyā liṅgamudrā tathaiva ca .. 78..
3.7.d:
वितस्तिद्वयसंयोगाद्भद्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
मुष्टिः प्रमार्जिता ज्ञेया लिङ्गमुद्रा तथैव च ॥ 78॥
3.7.m:
By the union of two spans, it is proclaimed as the Bhadramudrā;
a smoothed fist is likewise to be known as the Liṅgamudrā.

3.7.s:
sandaṣṭe mārjitāvoṣṭhau tīrṇamudrā prakīrtitā ..
prasāritau bhujau kṛtvā bhujāgrau kuñcitau tathā .. 79 ..
3.7.d:
सन्दष्टे मार्जितावोष्ठौ तीर्णमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
प्रसारितौ भुजौ कृत्वा भुजाग्रौ कुञ्चितौ तथा ॥ 79 ॥
3.7.m:
When wiped over closed lips, it is proclaimed as the Tīrṇamudrā.
Extending both arms and bending the forearms,

3.7.s:
agrāgrau kuñcitāṃśena karapallavasannibhau ..
tarjanīṃ kuñcitāṃ kṛtvā aṅguṣṭhopari vinyaset .. 3.33.80 ..
3.7.d:
अग्राग्रौ कुञ्चितांशेन करपल्लवसन्निभौ ॥
तर्जनीं कुञ्चितां कृत्वा अङ्गुष्ठोपरि विन्यसेत् ॥ 3.33.80 ॥
3.7.m:
with the fingertips curved like sprouting leaves of the hand,
and bending the index finger, one should place it upon the thumb.

3.7.s:
nikubjau bāhudaṇḍau tu badhnīyācca pṛthakpṛthaka ..
kairiṇī nāma mudraiṣā kathitā sūryadevatā .. 81 ..
3.7.d:
निकुब्जौ बाहुदण्डौ तु बध्नीयाच्च पृथक्पृथक ॥
कैरिणी नाम मुद्रैषा कथिता सूर्यदेवता ॥ 81 ॥
3.7.m:
One should hold the rod-like arms bent downward separately;
this mudrā, named Kairiṇī, is declared to have the Sun as its deity.

3.7.s:
padmākārau karau kṛtvā saṃśliṣṭau grathitāṅgulīḥ ..
aṅgulyā kārayettasminviśvamudreti kīrtitā .. 82 ..
3.7.d:
पद्माकारौ करौ कृत्वा संश्लिष्टौ ग्रथिताङ्गुलीः ॥
अङ्गुल्या कारयेत्तस्मिन्विश्वमुद्रेति कीर्तिता ॥ 82 ॥
3.7.m:
Having made both hands lotus-shaped, joined together with fingers interlaced,
one should form it with the finger; it is proclaimed as the Viśvamudrā.

3.7.s:
sammukhau tu karau kṛtvā saṃśliṣṭau grathitāṅgulīḥ ..
kaniṣṭhāmadhyame yojyau tarjanyau madhyame tathā .. 83 ..
3.7.d:
सम्मुखौ तु करौ कृत्वा संश्लिष्टौ ग्रथिताङ्गुलीः ॥
कनिष्ठामध्यमे योज्यौ तर्जन्यौ मध्यमे तथा ॥ 83 ॥
3.7.m:
Having brought both hands facing each other, joined together with fingers interlaced,
the little and middle fingers should be joined, and likewise the index and middle fingers.

3.7.s:
hṛdi mūrdhni śikhābandhe mudreyaṃ vyomasaṃjñitā ..
muṣṭibandhocchritāṃ kṛtvā madhyahastasya tarjanīm .. 84 ..
3.7.d:
हृदि मूर्ध्नि शिखाबन्धे मुद्रेयं व्योमसंज्ञिता ॥
मुष्टिबन्धोच्छ्रितां कृत्वा मध्यहस्तस्य तर्जनीम् ॥ 84 ॥
3.7.m:
At the heart, on the crown of the head, or at the tying of the topknot, this mudrā is named Vyoma.
Having made a fist and raised the index finger of the middle hand,

3.7.s:
tālaśabdakṛtāsau tu mudrā cāsrasya kīrtitā ..
madhyamā tarjanī caiva savyahastasya cocchrite .. 85 ..
3.7.d:
तालशब्दकृतासौ तु मुद्रा चास्रस्य कीर्तिता ॥
मध्यमा तर्जनी चैव सव्यहस्तस्य चोच्छ्रिते ॥ 85 ॥
3.7.m:
and making a clapping sound, this is proclaimed as the mudrā of the weapon.
When the middle and index fingers of the right hand are raised,

3.7.s:
kaniṣṭhānāmike kubje sāṅguṣṭhenaiva saṃjñitā ..
netrapradarśitā jñeyā govṛṣāgamane tathā .. 86 ..
3.7.d:
कनिष्ठानामिके कुब्जे साङ्गुष्ठेनैव संज्ञिता ॥
नेत्रप्रदर्शिता ज्ञेया गोवृषागमने तथा ॥ 86 ॥
3.7.m:
and the little and ring fingers are bent along with the thumb, it is designated [as such];
it is to be known as indicated for the eye and on the approach of a bull.

3.7.s:
uttānau tu karau kṛtvā sarvāṅgulyo vikuñjitāḥ ..
kṛtvā copari cāṅguṣṭhaṃ cālayeta punaḥ punaḥ .. 87 ..
3.7.d:
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा सर्वाङ्गुल्यो विकुञ्जिताः ॥
कृत्वा चोपरि चाङ्गुष्ठं चालयेत पुनः पुनः ॥ 87 ॥
3.7.m:
Having turned both hands upward, with all fingers curled,
and placing the thumb above, one should move it again and again.

3.7.s:
sarvāsāmeva śaktīnāṃ mudraiṣā samprakīrtitā ..
dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtirvimalā tathā ..88 ..
3.7.d:
सर्वासामेव शक्तीनां मुद्रैषा सम्प्रकीर्तिता ॥
दीप्ता सूक्ष्मा जया भद्रा विभूतिर्विमला तथा ॥88 ॥
3.7.m:
This is proclaimed as the mudrā of all the powers:
Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā,

3.7.s:
amoghā vidyutā caiva navamā sarvatomukhī ..
iti nāmāni śaktīnāṃ sarahasyāni nirdiśet .. 89 ..
3.7.d:
अमोघा विद्युता चैव नवमा सर्वतोमुखी ॥
इति नामानि शक्तीनां सरहस्यानि निर्दिशेत् ॥ 89 ॥
3.7.m:
Amoghā, Vidyutā, and the ninth, Sarvatomukhī—
thus one should indicate the secret names of the powers.

3.7.s:
sammukhau tu karau kṛtvā śliṣṭau caiva prasāritau ..
iyaṃ mudrā namaskāre ravi sānnidhyakāriṇī .. 3.33.90 ..
3.7.d:
सम्मुखौ तु करौ कृत्वा श्लिष्टौ चैव प्रसारितौ ॥
इयं मुद्रा नमस्कारे रवि सान्निध्यकारिणी ॥ 3.33.90 ॥
3.7.m: Having placed the hands facing each other, joined and extended, / this is the mudrā for salutation, bringing about the presence of the Sun.

3.7.s:
anāmikāyāḥ sandeśo ravimudrā prakīrtitā ..
somamudrā madhyamayā bhīmamudrā hyanāmayā .. 91 ..
3.7.d:
अनामिकायाः सन्देशो रविमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
सोममुद्रा मध्यमया भीममुद्रा ह्यनामया ॥ 91 ॥
3.7.m: The contact of the ring finger is declared to be the Sun mudrā; / with the middle finger, the Moon mudrā; with the ring finger, the Bhīma mudrā.

3.7.s:
kanīyasyā budhe mudrā unmūle jīvasaṃjñitā ..
anāmikāmūlagā tu śukramudrā prakīrtitā..92 ..
3.7.d:
कनीयस्या बुधे मुद्रा उन्मूले जीवसंज्ञिता ॥
अनामिकामूलगा तु शुक्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता॥92 ॥
3.7.m: With the little finger, the mudrā for Mercury; at its root, it is named for Jupiter; / but at the base of the ring finger is declared to be the mudrā for Venus.

3.7.s:
madhyamāmūlagāṃguṣṭhā śanimudrā prakīrtitā ..
tarjanīmūlagāṃguṣṭhe rāhu mudrā prakīrtitā .. 93 ..
3.7.d:
मध्यमामूलगांगुष्ठा शनिमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
तर्जनीमूलगांगुष्ठे राहु मुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 93 ॥
3.7.m: The thumb at the base of the middle finger is declared to be the Saturn mudrā; / with the thumb at the base of the forefinger, it is declared to be the Rāhu mudrā.

3.7.s:
tarjanī calanājjñeyā ketumudrā narādhipa ..
vāmahastena śikharāḥ krodhamudrā prakīrtitā .. 94 ..
3.7.d:
तर्जनी चलनाज्ज्ञेया केतुमुद्रा नराधिप ॥
वामहस्तेन शिखराः क्रोधमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 94 ॥
3.7.m: By moving the forefinger, O lord of men, the Ketu mudrā is to be known; / the śikhara hand with the left hand is declared to be the Anger mudrā.

3.7.s:
sampuṭau tu karau kṛtvā vāmocchrāyāṃ narādhipa ..
eṣā varāhamudrā tu sarvakarmakarī śubhā .. 95 ..
3.7.d:
सम्पुटौ तु करौ कृत्वा वामोच्छ्रायां नराधिप ॥
एषा वराहमुद्रा तु सर्वकर्मकरी शुभा ॥ 95 ॥
3.7.m: Having cupped the hands, raised towards the left, O king, / this is the Boar mudrā, auspicious and fulfilling all actions.

3.7.s:
vāmena veṣṭitau hastau dakṣiṇā bhairavī bhavet ..
hastāvadho mukhau yatra dṛṣṭiścādhastathā bhavet .. 96 ..
3.7.d:
वामेन वेष्टितौ हस्तौ दक्षिणा भैरवी भवेत् ॥
हस्तावधो मुखौ यत्र दृष्टिश्चाधस्तथा भवेत् ॥ 96 ॥
3.7.m: When the hands are wrapped around with the left, it becomes the Bhairavī; / where both hands face downwards and the gaze is likewise directed downwards,

3.7.s:
pātālabhañjinī nāma mudraiṣā kathitā nṛpa ..
kapitthānāmikā dīrghāstambhanī tu nigadyate .. 97 ..
3.7.d:
पातालभञ्जिनी नाम मुद्रैषा कथिता नृप ॥
कपित्थानामिका दीर्घास्तम्भनी तु निगद्यते ॥ 97 ॥
3.7.m: this mudrā is called Pātālabhañjinī, O king. / The kapittha with the ring finger outstretched is said to be the Stambhanī.

3.7.s:
karamadhyāttu saṃgrāhyamiva madhyena cāhatam ..
evaṃ madhyena saṃyuktā krodhinī parikīrtitā .. 98 ..
3.7.d:
करमध्यात्तु संग्राह्यमिव मध्येन चाहतम् ॥
एवं मध्येन संयुक्ता क्रोधिनी परिकीर्तिता ॥ 98 ॥
3.7.m: Seized from the middle of the hand, struck with the middle [finger], / thus joined with the middle [finger], it is proclaimed as Krodhinī.

3.7.s:
sahamadhyā tu saṃgrāhyā khātamadhye dvidhāhatam ..
evamadhyena saṃyuktā vīryamudrā prakīrtitā .. 99 ..
3.7.d:
सहमध्या तु संग्राह्या खातमध्ये द्विधाहतम् ॥
एवमध्येन संयुक्ता वीर्यमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 99 ॥
3.7.m: Held together in the middle, struck doubly in the hollow of the middle, / thus joined with the middle, it is declared to be the Vīryamudrā.

3.7.s:
evamadhyena saṃyuktaṃ bhairavī cāparā bhavet ..
kṣetramadhyā tu saṃgrāhyā iramadhyena saṃyutam .. 3.33.100 ..
3.7.d:
एवमध्येन संयुक्तं भैरवी चापरा भवेत् ॥
क्षेत्रमध्या तु संग्राह्या इरमध्येन संयुतम् ॥ 3.33.100 ॥
3.7.m: Thus joined in the middle, another Bhairavī arises. / Held in the center of the hand, joined in the middle,

3.7.s:
evamadhyena ca krāntaṃ stambhanī cāparā bhavet ..
lasanmadhyā tu saṃgrāhyamekamadhyena cāhatam .. 101 ..
3.7.d:
एवमध्येन च क्रान्तं स्तम्भनी चापरा भवेत् ॥
लसन्मध्या तु संग्राह्यमेकमध्येन चाहतम् ॥ 101 ॥
3.7.m: and crossed in this manner in the middle, it becomes another Stambhanī. / Shining in the middle, grasped, struck by the one in the middle,

3.7.s:
pātālabhañjanī nāma mudreyamaparā bhavet ..
tarjanī madhyamā caiva tathā caiva tvanāmikām .. 102 ..
3.7.d:
पातालभञ्जनी नाम मुद्रेयमपरा भवेत् ॥
तर्जनी मध्यमा चैव तथा चैव त्वनामिकाम् ॥ 102 ॥
3.7.m: this becomes another mudrā named Pātālabhañjanī. / The forefinger, the middle finger, and likewise the ring finger,

3.7.s:
madhyaparvasu saṃyuktāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kārayetkare ..
śaṅkhamudreyamuddiṣṭā pūrvamuktā tathāparā ..] 03 ..
3.7.d:
मध्यपर्वसु संयुक्तां पृष्ठतः कारयेत्करे ॥
शङ्खमुद्रेयमुद्दिष्टा पूर्वमुक्ता तथापरा ॥] 03 ॥
3.7.m: joined at the middle joints, one should place at the back of the hand; / this is designated as the Conch mudrā, and another was mentioned previously.

3.7.s:
prasārya sarvāścāṅgulyaḥ karapṛṣṭhe ca yojayet ..
cakramudrā bhavetteṣāṃ pūrvamuktā tathāparā .. 104 ..
3.7.d:
प्रसार्य सर्वाश्चाङ्गुल्यः करपृष्ठे च योजयेत् ॥
चक्रमुद्रा भवेत्तेषां पूर्वमुक्ता तथापरा ॥ 104 ॥
3.7.m: Having extended all fingers and joined them at the back of the hand, / it becomes the Discus mudrā among them; another was also stated earlier.

3.7.s:
kaṭibhāgapradeśe tu muṣṭistu triśirā bhavet ..
gadā mudrā bhavatyeṣā sarvavighnapraṇāśinī .. 105 ..
3.7.d:
कटिभागप्रदेशे तु मुष्टिस्तु त्रिशिरा भवेत् ॥
गदा मुद्रा भवत्येषा सर्वविघ्नप्रणाशिनी ॥ 105 ॥
3.7.m: In the region of the waist, a fist should be three-headed; / this becomes the Mace mudrā, destroying all obstacles.

3.7.s:
anyonyābhimukhau kṛtvā karau saṃveṣṭitāṅgulī ..
sahāṅguṣṭhena nirdiṣṭā mudrā kaustubhasaṃjñitā .. 106 ..
3.7.d:
अन्योन्याभिमुखौ कृत्वा करौ संवेष्टिताङ्गुली ॥
सहाङ्गुष्ठेन निर्दिष्टा मुद्रा कौस्तुभसंज्ञिता ॥ 106 ॥
3.7.m: Having made the hands face each other, the fingers entwined / along with the thumbs, it is designated as the mudrā named Kaustubha.

3.7.s:
saṃspṛśya vahniśikhirāṃ vāmacakriṇakaṃ spṛśet ..
iyaṃ mudrā vinirdiṣṭā vanamāleti pārthiva .. 107 ..
3.7.d:
संस्पृश्य वह्निशिखिरां वामचक्रिणकं स्पृशेत् ॥
इयं मुद्रा विनिर्दिष्टा वनमालेति पार्थिव ॥ 107 ॥
3.7.m: Having touched the flame-crest, one should touch the left discus; / this mudrā is designated, O king, as the Garland of Wild Flowers.

3.7.s:
anāmīnāśane dravye srajaṃ dravya karadvaye ..
jaṃghāmadhyagatau kṛtvā cibuko'rdhasamāyutau .. 108 ..
3.7.d:
अनामीनाशने द्रव्ये स्रजं द्रव्य करद्वये ॥
जंघामध्यगतौ कृत्वा चिबुकोऽर्धसमायुतौ ॥ 108 ॥
3.7.m: In the ritual substance […] a garland of substances in both hands; / placed between the shanks, joined at half the chin,

3.7.s:
mukhaṃ vivṛtakaṃ kuryājjvalajjihvā tu lelihā ..
eṣā mudrā mahāmudrā nārasiṃhīti kīrtitā..109..
3.7.d:
मुखं विवृतकं कुर्याज्ज्वलज्जिह्वा तु लेलिहा ॥
एषा मुद्रा महामुद्रा नारसिंहीति कीर्तिता॥109॥
3.7.m: one should make the mouth wide open, licking with a blazing tongue; / this mudrā is the great mudrā proclaimed as Nārasiṃhī.

3.7.s:
aṅguṣṭhaṃ muṣṭinā grāhyaṃ hyamudrāṃ parikīrtitā ..
muṣṭiṃ baddhvaiva cāṅguṣṭhe tiryaggaṃ kārayecchiraḥ..3.33.110..
3.7.d:
अङ्गुष्ठं मुष्टिना ग्राह्यं ह्यमुद्रां परिकीर्तिता ॥
मुष्टिं बद्ध्वैव चाङ्गुष्ठे तिर्यग्गं कारयेच्छिरः॥3.33.110॥
3.7.m: The thumb grasped with the fist is declared to be the [Haya]mudrā; / having bound the fist upon the thumb, one should make the head turn sideways.

3.7.s:
spaṣṭā tu tarjanīmuṣṭau śikhāmudrā prakīrtitā ..
tarjanīprāntasaṃlagne dve muṣṭī kavacaṃ bhavet .. 111..
3.7.d:
स्पष्टा तु तर्जनीमुष्टौ शिखामुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
तर्जनीप्रान्तसंलग्ने द्वे मुष्टी कवचं भवेत् ॥ 111॥
3.7.m: The forefinger clear on the fist is declared to be the Śikhā mudrā; / two fists touching at the tips of the forefingers becomes the Armor.

3.7.s:
muṣṭī baddhvā tu hastau dve ubhayāṃguliyojitau..
gadāmudrā samākhyātā sarvakarmakarī śubhā .. 1 12..
3.7.d:
मुष्टी बद्ध्वा तु हस्तौ द्वे उभयांगुलियोजितौ॥
गदामुद्रा समाख्याता सर्वकर्मकरी शुभा ॥ 1 12॥
3.7.m: Having clenched the fists with both hands, joined with both fingers, / it is declared as the Mace mudrā, auspicious and fulfilling all actions.

3.7.s:
tarjanī tu tathāṅguṣṭhe pratiśliṣṭau tu kārayet ..
śeṣāḥ prasāritāṅgulyo netramudrā bhavennṛpa..113..
3.7.d:
तर्जनी तु तथाङ्गुष्ठे प्रतिश्लिष्टौ तु कारयेत् ॥
शेषाः प्रसारिताङ्गुल्यो नेत्रमुद्रा भवेन्नृप॥113॥
3.7.m: One should make the forefinger closely attached to the thumb; / the remaining fingers extended becomes the Eye mudrā, O king.

3.7.s:
anāmyo'rdhelinau kṛtvā tarjanyānāṃ samaṃ śrayāt..
madhyamau connatau kṛtvā aṅguṣṭhau śleṣitau samau...114..
3.7.d:
अनाम्योऽर्धेलिनौ कृत्वा तर्जन्यानां समं श्रयात्॥
मध्यमौ चोन्नतौ कृत्वा अङ्गुष्ठौ श्लेषितौ समौ॥.114॥
3.7.m: Having made the two ring fingers bent halfway, resting equally with the forefingers, / having raised the two middle fingers, and joined the two thumbs equally,

3.7.s:
eṣā mudā samākhyātā divyā ca śiraso nṛpa..
añjaliḥ pramadā mudrā kṣipraṃ devaprasāritam .. 115..
3.7.d:
एषा मुदा समाख्याता दिव्या च शिरसो नृप॥
अञ्जलिः प्रमदा मुद्रा क्षिप्रं देवप्रसारितम् ॥ 115॥
3.7.m: this divine mudrā of the head is declared, O king. / The Añjali is the Pramadā mudrā, quickly extending towards the deity.

3.7.s:
vandane hṛdayā mattā pūrvadakṣiṇato'parā ..
ūrdhvo'ṅguṣṭho vāmamuṣṭirdakṣiṇo'ṅguṣṭhabandhanaḥ .. 116..
3.7.d:
वन्दने हृदया मत्ता पूर्वदक्षिणतोऽपरा ॥
ऊर्ध्वोऽङ्गुष्ठो वाममुष्टिर्दक्षिणोऽङ्गुष्ठबन्धनः ॥ 116॥
3.7.m: In obeisance, joyous at the heart, another from east to south; / the left fist with the thumb upright, the right thumb binding,

3.7.s:
saṃnyasya tasya cāṅguṣṭhau yasyā ūrdhvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ..
vāsudevasya mudraiṣā baddhā syātpāpanāśinī .. 117 ..
3.7.d:
संन्यस्य तस्य चाङ्गुष्ठौ यस्या ऊर्ध्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
वासुदेवस्य मुद्रैषा बद्धा स्यात्पापनाशिनी ॥ 117 ॥
3.7.m: having placed the two thumbs of it, positioned upright above, / this is the mudrā of Vāsudeva, which when bound destroys sins.

3.7.s:
hastayorubhayoreva kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhagarbhakau ..
śeṣāḥ prasāritaḥ śliṣṭā mudrā saṅkarṣaṇasya tu .. 118 ..
3.7.d:
हस्तयोरुभयोरेव कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठगर्भकौ ॥
शेषाः प्रसारितः श्लिष्टा मुद्रा सङ्कर्षणस्य तु ॥ 118 ॥
3.7.m: With the little finger and the thumb held within both hands, / the rest extended and joined, it is the mudrā of Saṃkarṣaṇa.

3.7.s:
tarjanyāvardhataḥ śliṣṭau samāṅguṣṭhau tu śleṣitau ..
eṣā muṣṭiṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mudrā pradyumnasaṃjñikā .. 119 ..
3.7.d:
तर्जन्यावर्धतः श्लिष्टौ समाङ्गुष्ठौ तु श्लेषितौ ॥
एषा मुष्टिं ततः कृत्वा मुद्रा प्रद्युम्नसंज्ञिका ॥ 119 ॥
3.7.m: The two forefingers half-joined, the two thumbs equal and adhered; / having then formed a fist, this is the mudrā named Pradyumna.

3.7.s:
aṅgulyau valitau yatra sūrpākārau tu kārayet..
veṣṭyāṅguṣṭhāvadhaḥ kāryāvaniruddhe tu kārayeta .. 3.33.120 ..
3.7.d:
अङ्गुल्यौ वलितौ यत्र सूर्पाकारौ तु कारयेत्॥
वेष्ट्याङ्गुष्ठावधः कार्यावनिरुद्धे तु कारयेत ॥ 3.33.120 ॥
3.7.m: Where the fingers are bent, one should make them winnowing-basket shaped; / having wrapped the thumbs, they should be directed downwards in the Aniruddha [mudrā].

3.7.s:
ityuddeśe tu te proktā mudrāhastā mayā nṛpa ..
darśayenmantrayuktānāṃ parāṃ siddhimabhīpsitām ..121..
3.7.d:
इत्युद्देशे तु ते प्रोक्ता मुद्राहस्ता मया नृप ॥
दर्शयेन्मन्त्रयुक्तानां परां सिद्धिमभीप्सिताम् ॥121॥
3.7.m: Thus the mudrā-hands have been briefly declared to you by me, O king; / one should display them joined with mantras to achieve supreme desired success.

3.7.s:
yathāmantraṃ yathādevaṃ yathāvidhirataṃdritaḥ ..
mantreṣu devatāyuktā bahvyo mudrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..122..
3.7.d:
यथामन्त्रं यथादेवं यथाविधिरतंद्रितः ॥
मन्त्रेषु देवतायुक्ता बह्व्यो मुद्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥122॥
3.7.m: According to the mantra, according to the deity, according to the rule, without sloth, / many mudrās associated with deities have been proclaimed in the mantras.

3.7.s: tāsāṃ mantraṃ tu vijñeyaṃ niyogo nṛpa iṣyate .. 123 ..
3.7.d: तासां मन्त्रं तु विज्ञेयं नियोगो नृप इष्यते ॥ 123 ॥
3.7.m: Their mantra should be known, and their application is prescribed, O king.

3.7.s:
etāvaduktaṃ nṛpa nṛttaśāstraṃ samāsataḥ pārthivavaṃśamukhya ..
niḥśeṣametadgaditaṃ mahārthaṃ vistārataḥ sarvajagatpradhānam ..124..
3.34
vajra uvāca ..
nṛttamutpāditaṃ kena ṛṣiṇā daivatena vā ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ chindhi tvaṃ hi sarvaviducyase .. 1 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ekārṇave purā loke naṣṭasthāvarajaṃgame ..
śeṣaparyaṅkaśayane supte madhuniṣūdane .. 2 ..
saṃvāhyamānacaraṇe lakṣmyā yadukulodvaha ..
nābhyāṃ tasya samutpannaṃ padmaṃ padmanibhekṣaṇa .. .. 3 ..
tatra jātaḥ svayaṃ brahmā devaḥ śubhacaturmukhaḥ ..
daivaiḥ saha mahābhāga saśarīrairnarādhipa .. 4 ..
padmodabindu sambhūtau tatraiva madhukaiṭabhau ..
rajastamomayau corau dānavau tau bhayānakau .. 5 ..
tato jagṛhaturvedānbrahmaṇastau narādhipa ..
hata vedastato brahmā tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam .. 6 ..
3.7.d:
एतावदुक्तं नृप नृत्तशास्त्रं समासतः पार्थिववंशमुख्य ॥
निःशेषमेतद्गदितं महार्थं विस्तारतः सर्वजगत्प्रधानम् ॥124॥
3.34
वज्र उवाच ॥
नृत्तमुत्पादितं केन ऋषिणा दैवतेन वा ॥
एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि त्वं हि सर्वविदुच्यसे ॥ 1 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एकार्णवे पुरा लोके नष्टस्थावरजंगमे ॥
शेषपर्यङ्कशयने सुप्ते मधुनिषूदने ॥ 2 ॥
संवाह्यमानचरणे लक्ष्म्या यदुकुलोद्वह ॥
नाभ्यां तस्य समुत्पन्नं पद्मं पद्मनिभेक्षण ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
तत्र जातः स्वयं ब्रह्मा देवः शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥
दैवैः सह महाभाग सशरीरैर्नराधिप ॥ 4 ॥
पद्मोदबिन्दु सम्भूतौ तत्रैव मधुकैटभौ ॥
रजस्तमोमयौ चोरौ दानवौ तौ भयानकौ ॥ 5 ॥
ततो जगृहतुर्वेदान्ब्रह्मणस्तौ नराधिप ॥
हत वेदस्ततो ब्रह्मा तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.7.m:
This much has been told in brief concerning the treatise on dance, O king, foremost of the royal lineage; / all of this profound meaning has been proclaimed at length, foremost in all the world.
Vajra said: / By whom was dance originated—by a sage or by a deity? / Sever this doubt of mine, for you are said to know everything.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, when the world was a single ocean, motionless and moving beings destroyed, / while the Slayer of Madhu slept upon the couch of Śeṣa,
his feet being massaged by Lakṣmī, O scion of the Yadu lineage, / from his navel arose a lotus, O lotus-eyed one.
There was born self-existent Brahmā, the auspicious four-faced god, / together with the deities, O fortunate one, endowed with bodies, O king.
Born from two drops of water on that lotus, right there, were Madhu and Kaiṭabha, / full of rajas and tamas, thieves, two terrifying Dānavas.
Then, O king, the two seized the Vedas from Brahmā; / bereft of the Vedas, Brahmā then praised Madhusūdana:

3.7.s:
vedā me paramaṃ cakṣurvedā me paramaṃ balam ..
dānavāpahṛtā vedā andho jātosmi śatruhan .. 7 ..
evamuktastadā viṣṇurbrahmaṇā puruṣottamaḥ ..
utthāya salilāttasmādbabhrāma salilāśaye .. 8 ..
aṅgahāraiḥ sulalitaistathā padaparikramaiḥ ..
tathā bhramantantaṃ devaṃ dadarśāyatalocanā .. 9 ..
atīva lalitaṃ lakṣmīrjātarāgā viśeṣataḥ ..
devopyaśvaśiro bhūtvā pātālatalagaḥ kṣaṇāta .. 3.34.10 ..
sa daityāndṛṣṭavānvedāṃstyaktvāśvaśirasastanum ..
jaghāna tau mahākāyau dānavau madhukaiṭabhau .. 11 ..
hatvā vedasahāyastu samprāpto brahmaṇo'ntike ..
dadau vedāṃstatastasmai devadevaḥ svayambhuve .. 12 ..
dattvā vedāṃstataḥ prāha sṛṣṭiṃ kuru pitāmaha..
vedagrāmayuto brahmā sargaṃ cakre tataḥ prabhuḥ .. 13 ..
3.7.d:
वेदा मे परमं चक्षुर्वेदा मे परमं बलम् ॥
दानवापहृता वेदा अन्धो जातोस्मि शत्रुहन् ॥ 7 ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा विष्णुर्ब्रह्मणा पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
उत्थाय सलिलात्तस्माद्बभ्राम सलिलाशये ॥ 8 ॥
अङ्गहारैः सुललितैस्तथा पदपरिक्रमैः ॥
तथा भ्रमन्तन्तं देवं ददर्शायतलोचना ॥ 9 ॥
अतीव ललितं लक्ष्मीर्जातरागा विशेषतः ॥
देवोप्यश्वशिरो भूत्वा पातालतलगः क्षणात ॥ 3.34.10 ॥
स दैत्यान्दृष्टवान्वेदांस्त्यक्त्वाश्वशिरसस्तनुम् ॥
जघान तौ महाकायौ दानवौ मधुकैटभौ ॥ 11 ॥
हत्वा वेदसहायस्तु सम्प्राप्तो ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिके ॥
ददौ वेदांस्ततस्तस्मै देवदेवः स्वयम्भुवे ॥ 12 ॥
दत्त्वा वेदांस्ततः प्राह सृष्टिं कुरु पितामह॥
वेदग्रामयुतो ब्रह्मा सर्गं चक्रे ततः प्रभुः ॥ 13 ॥
3.7.m:
“The Vedas are my supreme eye, the Vedas are my supreme strength; / the Vedas have been stolen by the Dānavas; I have become blind, O slayer of foes!”
Thus addressed then by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Puruṣottama, / rising up from that water, wandered upon the body of water.
With graceful major body-movements and step-sequences,
as the god was roaming in this way, the wide-eyed [goddess] saw him.
Lakṣmī became exceedingly charmed, especially filled with love.
And the god, having assumed a horse's head, went in an instant to the underworld.
He saw the demons and the Vedas, abandoned the horse-headed form,
and slew the two giant-bodied Dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
Having slain [them], accompanied by the Vedas he approached Brahmā;
then the god of gods gave the Vedas to the self-born [creator].
Having given the Vedas, he then said, "Carry out creation, grandfather!"
Then the lord Brahmā, endowed with the assembly of the Vedas, performed creation.

3.7.d:
शेषस्याङ्कगतं देवं लक्ष्मीः पप्रच्छ पार्थिव॥
लक्ष्म्युवाच ॥
देवदेव जगन्नाथ शङ्खचक्रगदाधर ॥ 14 ॥
परिक्रमं मया तोये दृष्टः सललितः प्रभो ॥
अतीव रमणीयाङ्ग किं तत्प्रब्रूहि मे प्रभो॥15॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच॥
नृत्तमुत्पादितं ह्येतन्मया पद्मनिभेक्षणे॥
अङ्गहारैः सकरणैः संयुक्तं सपरिक्रमैः॥16॥
नृत्तेनाराधयिष्यन्ति भक्तिमन्तस्तु मां शुभे ॥
त्रैलोक्यस्यानुकरणं नृत्ते देवि प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 17 ॥
एतावदुक्त्वा तां देवो ब्रह्माणं वाक्यमव्रवीत ॥
गृहाण नृत्तं धर्मज्ञ लक्ष्यलक्षणसंयुतम् ॥ 18 ॥
एतावदुक्त्वा ब्रह्माणं ग्राहयामास केशवः ॥
तद्गृहीत्वा ततो ब्रह्मा ददौ रुद्राय वेधसे ॥
गृहीत्वा तच्च रुद्रोपि तोषयामास केशवम् ॥
तेन नृत्तेन सततं देवेशं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥ 3.34.20 ॥
3.7.m:
Lakṣmī questioned the god seated on the lap of Śeṣa, O king:
Lakṣmī said:
"O god of gods, lord of the world, wielder of the conch, discus, and mace!
A graceful stepping was seen by me in the water, O lord,
with exceedingly beautiful limbs. Tell me, O lord, what was that?"
The Holy One said:
"Indeed, this dance was created by me, O lotus-eyed one,
joined with major body-movements, minor body-movements, and step-sequences.
The devoted will worship me through dance, O auspicious one;
the representation of the three worlds is established in dance, O goddess."
Having said this much to her, the god spoke these words to Brahmā:
"Receive the dance, O knower of dharma, along with its practice and theory!"
Having spoken this much to Brahmā, Keśava instructed him.
Having received it, Brahmā then transmitted it to the creator Rudra;
and Rudra, having received it, also pleased Keśava
constantly with that dance—the lord of gods who is loving to devotees.

3.7.d:
एवमुत्पादितं नृत्तं वासुदेवेन पार्थिव ॥
एकार्णवे पुरा लोके नष्टस्थावरजङ्गमे ॥ 21 ॥
ततः प्रभृति देवेशः शङ्करः शङ्करो नृणाम् ॥
नृत्तेनाराधयन्नास्ते देवं चक्रगदाधरम् ॥ 22 ॥
नृत्तेश्वरत्वं चावाप तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् ॥
सोऽपि तुष्यति नृत्तेन सम्यगाराधितो हरः ॥ 22 ॥
अन्ये च देवास्तुष्यन्ति सम्यङ् नृत्तेन तोषिताः ॥
आप्यायनं परं ह्येतत्कथितं तु दिवौकसाम् ॥24॥
एतदेव हि देवत्वं दीव्यतां सततं दिवि ॥
पुष्पनैवेद्यदानेभ्यो नृत्तदानं विशिष्यते॥ 25 ॥
स्वयं नृत्तेन यः कुर्याद्देवदेवस्य पूजनम् ॥
विशेषेण महाभाग तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 26 ॥
नृत्तं गीतं तथा वाद्यं दत्त्वा देवाय विष्णवे ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥ 27 ॥
नृत्तेन वृत्तिं यः कुर्यात्स तु वर्ज्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥
कुशीलवाद्यैर्यः कुर्यान्नृत्तविक्रयकारकः ॥ 28 ॥
3.7.m:
In this way dance was created by Vāsudeva, O king,
long ago when the world was a single ocean and the mobile and immobile had perished.
From then on, the lord of gods Śaṅkara, who brings peace to men,
remains worshipping the god who bears the discus and mace with dance.
And he attained lordship over dance and praised the slayer of Madhu;
Hara too is pleased when properly worshipped through dance.
And other gods are pleased when properly gratified with dance;
for this is declared to be the supreme gratification of the celestials.
This alone indeed is divinity for those constantly sporting in heaven;
the gift of dance is superior to the gifts of flowers and food-offerings.
Whoever performs the worship of the god of gods himself through dance—
Keśava is especially pleased with him, O fortunate one.
Having offered dance, song, and instrumental music to the god Viṣṇu,
one enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires.
He who makes a livelihood by dance is to be diligently avoided,
who practices with actors and musicians, a seller of dance.

3.7.s:

3.7.d:
देवताराधनं कुर्याद्यस्तु नृत्तेन धर्मवित् ॥
स सर्वकामानाप्नोति मोक्षोपायं च विन्दति ॥ 29 ॥
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्गलोकप्रदं तथा ॥
ईश्वराणां विलासं तु चार्तानां दुःखनाशनम् ॥ 3.34.30 ॥
मूढानामुपदेशं तत्स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥
शान्तिकं पौष्टिकं काम्यं वासुदेवेन निर्मितम् ॥31॥
एतावदुक्तं तव नृत्तशास्त्रं समासतो लोकहिताय राजन ॥
नृत्तेन यत्नः पुरुषेण कार्यो लोकद्वयञ्जेतुमभीप्सता वै ॥ 32 ॥
3.35
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि चित्रसूत्रं तवानघ॥
उर्वशीं सृजतः पूर्वे चित्रसूत्रं नृपात्मज॥1॥
नारायणेन मुनिना लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
प्राप्तानां वञ्चनार्थाय देवस्त्रीणां महामुनिः ॥ 2 ॥
सहकाररसं गृह्य उर्व्यां चक्रे वरस्त्रियम् ॥
चित्रेण सा ततो जाता रूपयुक्ता वराप्सराः ॥ 3 ॥
3.7.m:
However, the knower of dharma who performs the worship of deities with dance
obtains all desires and finds the means to liberation.
[It is] auspicious, bringer of fame and longevity, granter of the heavenly realm,
the sport of lords, and the destroyer of suffering for the afflicted;
it is instruction for the ignorant, the enhancer of fortune for women,
pacifying, nourishing, fulfilling desires, fashioned by Vāsudeva.
"This dance treatise has been told to you in brief for the welfare of the world, O king;
indeed, an effort with dance should be made by a man desiring to conquer both worlds."
3.35
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
"Hereafter I shall declare to you the Citrasūtra, O sinless one.
Formerly, while creating Urvaśī, the Citrasūtra [was produced], O prince,
by the sage Nārāyaṇa, desiring the welfare of the worlds,
for the sake of deceiving the celestial women who had arrived, the great sage.
Having taken mango juice, he drew an excellent woman upon the earth;
through painting she was then born, an excellent apsaras endowed with beauty.

3.7.s:
yāṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍitāḥ sarvā jagmustā devayoṣitaḥ ..
evaṃ mahāmuniḥ kṛtvā citraṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyutam .. 4 ..
grāhayāmāsa sa tadā viśvakarmāṇamacyutam ..
yathā nṛtte tathā citre trailokyānukṛtiḥ smṛtā .. 5 ..

nṛtte pramāṇaṃ yenoktaṃ tatpravakṣyāmyataḥ śṛṇu .. 7 ..
haṃso bhadro'tha mālavyo rucakaḥ śaśakastathā ..

3.7.d:
यां दृष्ट्वा व्रीडिताः सर्वा जग्मुस्ता देवयोषितः ॥
एवं महामुनिः कृत्वा चित्रं लक्षणसंयुतम् ॥ 4 ॥
ग्राहयामास स तदा विश्वकर्माणमच्युतम् ॥
यथा नृत्ते तथा चित्रे त्रैलोक्यानुकृतिः स्मृता ॥ 5 ॥
दृष्टयश्च तथा भावा अङ्गोपाङ्गानि सर्वशः ॥
कराश्च ये महानृत्ते पूर्वोक्ता नृपसत्तम ॥ 6 ॥
त एव चित्रे विज्ञेया नृत्तं चित्रं परं मतम् ॥
नृत्ते प्रमाणं येनोक्तं तत्प्रवक्ष्याम्यतः शृणु ॥ 7 ॥
हंसो भद्रोऽथ मालव्यो रुचकः शशकस्तथा ॥
विज्ञेयाः पुरुषाः पञ्च तेषां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥ 8 ॥
उच्छ्रायायामतुल्यास्ते सर्वे ज्ञेयाः प्रमाणतः ॥
स्वेनेवाङ्गुलमानेन शतमष्टाधिकं भवेत् ॥9 ॥
प्रमाणं नृप हंसस्य भद्रस्य तु षडुत्तरम् ॥
चतुर्भिरधिकं ज्ञेयं मालव्यस्य तथा नृप ॥ 3.35.10 ॥
3.7.m:
Having seen her, all those celestial women departed in shame.
Having thus made a painting endowed with [canonical] characteristics, the great sage
then transmitted it to the unswerving Viśvakarman.
Just as in dance, so in painting, the representation of the three worlds is recognized.
The glances, the emotional states, and all the major and minor limbs,
and the hands which were earlier declared in [the chapter on] great dance, O best of kings—
those very ones are to be known in painting; dance and painting are considered supreme.
Listen now as I will explain the proportion that has been stated in dance.
Haṃsa, Bhadra, and then Mālavya, Rucaka, and Śaśaka:
five [types of] men are to be recognized; I will declare their characteristics.
Their height and span should all be known as equal in proportion;
by his own finger-measure it should be one hundred and eight [aṅgulas]:
the measure of the Haṃsa, O king; but of the Bhadra it is six more [than a hundred];
of the Mālavya it is to be known as four more [than a hundred], O king;

3.7.d:
शतं च रुचकस्योक्तं दशोनं शशकस्य च ॥
द्वादशाङुलविस्तारस्ताल इत्यभिधीयते ॥ 11 ॥
अङ्गुल्फन्तच्चतुर्भागं पादोच्छ्रायः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
द्वौ च तालौ तथा जङ्घे पादतुल्ये च जानुनी ॥ 12 ॥
जंघातुल्यौ तथा चोरू नाभिस्तालं तु मेढ्रतः ॥
तावच्च नाभिहदयं हृदयात्कण्ठ एव च ॥ 13 ॥
कण्ठस्तालत्रिभागः स्यात्तालं च वदनं भवेत् ॥
तालषड्भागमप्युक्तं ललाटोपरि मस्तकम् ॥ 14 ॥
मध्ये मेढ्रं तु विज्ञेयमिति दैर्घ्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
तालः प्रोक्तः करो राजन्बाहू सप्तदशाङ्गुलौ ॥ 15 ॥
प्रबाहू तावदेवोक्तौ वक्षसोर्धमथाष्टकम्।
एतदायामतः प्रोक्तं मानं हंसस्य पार्थिव॥16॥
अनेनैवानुसारेण शेषाणामपि कल्पयेत्॥
आयामपरिणाहाभ्यां समाः सर्वे नराधिप॥17॥

3.7.s:
sāmānyataste nṛpavarya mānaṃ proktaṃ mayā haṃsa narādhipasya ..
pratyaṅgamānaṃ ca mayocyamānaṃ samāsatastvaṃ śṛṇu rājasiṃha.. 18..
3.7.d:
सामान्यतस्ते नृपवर्य मानं प्रोक्तं मया हंस नराधिपस्य ॥
प्रत्यङ्गमानं च मयोच्यमानं समासतस्त्वं शृणु राजसिंह॥ 18॥
3.7.m:
The general measure of the Haṃsa ruler of men has been proclaimed by me to you, O best of kings;
now listen to the measure of the individual limbs being spoken by me in brief, O lion among kings."
