3.8.d:
3.36
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अथ प्रत्यङ्गविभागो भवति तत्र द्वादशाङ्गुलपरीणाहो मूर्धा ।
चतुरंगुलोच्छ्रायं अष्टाङ्गुलं ललाटम् ।
शङ्खौ चतुरङ्गुलौ द्व्यङ्गुलोच्छ्रायौ पञ्चाङ्गुलौ गण्डौ चतुरङ्गुलो हनुः ।
द्व्यङ्गुलौ कर्णौ चतुरङ्गुलोच्छ्रायौ ।
कर्णमध्याङ्गुलं तद्रन्ध्रमुदकम् ॥
पालिरनियमेन । ( कर्णस्य लुटिकापालिः)
नासा चतुरङ्गुला अग्रे द्व्यङ्गुलोच्छ्राया त्रिकायामा च नासापुटावंगुलीविस्तारौ द्विगुणद्विगुणायामौ ।
नासौष्ठमध्यमर्धाङ्गुलम् ।
ओष्ठश्चाङ्गुलः ।
चतुरङ्गुलायाममास्यम्।
अधरोङ्गुलं द्व्यंगुलं चिबुकम् ।
चत्वारिंशद्दन्ताः ।
तेष्वष्टौ दंष्ट्राः ।
अधार्ङ्गुलोच्छ्रिता दन्ताः ।
अङ्गुलद्वादशभागिका दंष्ट्रा ।
अङ्गुल विस्तृता त्र्यङ्गुलायामे नेत्रे ।
नेत्रत्रिभागं कृष्णमंडलम्।
पञ्चभागास्तारा ।
अर्धाङ्गुलिविस्तृते त्र्याङ्गुलायामे भ्रुवौ ।
तयोर्द्व्यंगुलमन्तरम् ।
चतुरङ्गुलं न्नेत्रान्तकर्णविवरम् ।
दशाङ्गुलविस्तृता ग्रीवा।
एकविंशत्यङ्गुलपरिणाहा षोडशाङ्गुलस्तनान्तरम् ।
षडङ्गुलं स्तनजत्र्वन्तरम् ।
षोडश बाहुमूलपरिणाहः।
द्वादशाग्रे सप्ताङ्गुलं करतलम् ।
पंचाङ्गुलं विस्तृतं पंचाङ्गुलप्रमाणा मध्यमिका ।
तत्पूर्वदलहीना प्रदेशिनी ।
तत्तुल्या चानामिका ।
तत्परिहीना कनिष्ठिका सर्वाः समत्रिभागपर्वाः ।
पर्वार्धा नखाः ।
त्र्यङ्गुलमङ्गुष्ठं द्विपर्वः।
जठरपरिणाहो द्वाचत्वारिंशांगुलः ।
वेद्यप्रमाणाभ्यामङ्गुलं नाभिः ।
कटिरष्टादशांगुला विपुला ।
तत्परिधिश्चतुश्चत्वारिंशत् ।
चतुरंगुलविस्तृतौ वृषणौ ।
षडङ्गुलं तावत्परिणाहं मेढ्रम् ।
तन्मध्यत ऊरू चतुरङ्गुलौ ।
तद्द्विगुणपरिणाहाङ्गुलविपुले जानुनी ।
तत्त्रिगुणपरिणाहं जङ्घाग्रम् ।
पञ्चागुलं चतुर्दशपरिणाहं द्वादश दीर्घौ षडङ्गुलविस्तृतौ पदौ त्रिकायताङ्गुष्ठौ ।
अङ्गुष्ठतुल्या प्रदेशिनी ।
तदष्टांगोनाः शेषाः ।
अङ्गुलचतुर्भागहीनोऽङ्गुष्ठनखः ।
तदर्धप्रमाणं प्रदेशिन्याः ।
तदष्टभागः शेषाणाम् ।
सर्वपादमङ्गुलमष्टाङ्गुलोत्सेधः ।
त्र्यङ्गुले पार्ष्णीः।
चतुरङ्गुलोच्छ्रायौ इति हंसप्रमाणं भवति।
भवंति चात्र ॥
शेषाणां पार्थिवेन्द्राणां मानं युक्त्या प्रकल्पयेत॥
अनेनैवानुसारेण स्वमानस्यानुसारतः॥1॥
3.8.m:
3.36
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now begins the division of individual limbs. In that regard, the crown of the head is twelve digits in circumference.
The forehead is eight digits wide and four digits high.
The temples are four digits across and two digits high; the cheeks are five digits; the chin is four digits.
The ears are two digits across and four digits high.
The ear-aperture inside is one digit, and water [should be clear within it].
The ear-lobe is without fixed measure. (The pendant lobe of the ear.)
The nose is four digits long, two digits high at the tip, and three [digits wide] across the bridge; the nostrils are one digit broad and twice that in length.
The space between the nose and the upper lip is half a digit.
The upper lip is one digit.
The mouth is four digits in length.
The lower lip is one digit; the chin is two digits.
There are forty teeth.
Among them are eight tusks.
The teeth are half a digit high.
The tusks are one-twelfth of a digit.
The eyes are one digit broad and three digits in length.
The dark circle of the eye is one-third of the eye.
The pupil is one-fifth [of that].
The eyebrows are half a digit broad and three digits in length.
The space between them is two digits.
The space between the corner of the eye and the ear is four digits.
The neck is ten digits broad,
twenty-one digits in circumference; the space between the breasts is sixteen digits.
The space between the breast and the collarbone is six digits.
The circumference of the base of the arm is sixteen digits.
At the tip [the wrist] it is twelve [digits in circumference]; the palm of the hand is seven digits long
and five digits broad; the middle finger is five digits in length.
The index finger is less by the first phalange of that [middle finger].
The ring finger is equal to that [index finger].
The little finger is smaller than that; all [fingers] have phalanges equal to one-third [of their length].
The nails are half a phalange.
The thumb is three digits long and has two phalanges.
The circumference of the belly is forty-two digits.
The navel is one digit in depth and width.
The waist is eighteen digits across;
its circumference is forty-four digits.
The testicles are four digits broad.
The penis is six digits long and of the same circumference.
Between them, the thighs are four digits [in separation].
The two knees are two digits broad and twice that in circumference.
The top of the calf is three times that in circumference.
The foot is five digits [high], fourteen in circumference, twelve digits long, and six digits broad; the big toes are three [digits] in length.
The second toe is equal to the big toe.
The remaining toes are each less by an eighth of that.
The nail of the big toe is less than a fourth of a digit.
That of the second toe is half that measure.
That of the remaining toes is an eighth part of that.
The whole foot has [toes each of] one digit, and its elevation is eight digits.
The heels are three digits wide
and four digits high. Such is the measure of the Haṃsa type.
And on this subject there are [these verses]:
One should logically calculate the measure of the remaining kings
according to this very model, in accordance with their own measure.

3.8.s:
madhakṣaścandragaurastu nāgarājabhujo balī..
haṃsagāmī sumadhyaśca haṃsaśca sumukho bhavet .. ..2..
3.8.d:
मधक्षश्चन्द्रगौरस्तु नागराजभुजो बली॥
हंसगामी सुमध्यश्च हंसश्च सुमुखो भवेत् ॥ ॥2॥
3.8.m: With eyes resembling honey, fair as the moon, with arms like the king of serpents, strong, / walking like a swan, having a fine waist, a Haṃsa type should possess a handsome face.

3.8.s:
romaruddhakapolastu gajagāmī mahāmatiḥ ..
vṛttopacitabāhustu bhadraḥ padmanibho bhavet ..3..
3.8.d:
रोमरुद्धकपोलस्तु गजगामी महामतिः ॥
वृत्तोपचितबाहुस्तु भद्रः पद्मनिभो भवेत् ॥3॥
3.8.m: With cheeks covered in hair, walking like an elephant, highly intelligent, / with rounded, well-fleshed arms, a Bhadra type should resemble a lotus.

3.8.s:
mudgaśyāmastu mālavyaḥ kṛśamadhyastanucchaviḥ ..
ājānubāhuḥ pīnāṃso dantighoṇo mahāhanuḥ .. 4 ..
3.8.d:
मुद्गश्यामस्तु मालव्यः कृशमध्यस्तनुच्छविः ॥
आजानुबाहुः पीनांसो दन्तिघोणो महाहनुः ॥ 4 ॥
3.8.m: Dark as a mung bean, slender-waisted, and of bright complexion, / with arms reaching to his knees, muscular shoulders, an elephant-like nose, and large jaws is the Mālavya type.

3.8.s:
śaradgaurastu rucakaḥ kambugrīvo mahāmatiḥ ..
satyastu sikataścaiva balavāṃśca prakīrtitaḥ .. 5 ..
3.8.d:
शरद्गौरस्तु रुचकः कम्बुग्रीवो महामतिः ॥
सत्यस्तु सिकतश्चैव बलवांश्च प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 5 ॥
3.8.m: Fair as the autumn sky, with a neck like a conch, highly intelligent, / truthful, endowed with fine proportions, and powerful is celebrated the Rucaka type.

3.8.s:
raktaśyāmastu śaśakaḥ kiṃcitkarburakastathā ..
pūrṇagaṇḍaśca caturo madhvakṣaśca prakīrtitaḥ .. 6 ..
3.37
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
aṅgapratyaṅgamānena yathā pañca narāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
striyaḥ pañca tathā jñeyāstā eva manujottama .. 1 ..
puruṣasya samīpasthā kartavyā yoṣidīśvara ..
naraskandhapramāṇena kāryaikā sā yathāmiti .. 2 ..
aṅgulī dvau narātkṣāmaṃ striyo madhyaṃ vidhīyate ..
adhikā ca kaṭiḥ kāryā tathaiva caturaḍulam .. 3 ..
uraḥpramāṇataḥ kāryau stanau nṛpa manoharau ..
nṛpāśca sarve kartavyā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāḥ .. 4 ..
jālapādakarāḥ kāryāstathā vai cakravartinaḥ ..
ūrṇeyaṃ ca bhuvormadhye teṣāṃ kāryaṃ tathā śubham .. .. 5 ..
rekhāśca karayoḥ kāryāstisro rājñāṃ manoharāḥ ..
śaśakṣatajasaṅkāśāḥ śastrā vai kṣāmakoṭakāḥ .. 6 ..
3.8.d:
रक्तश्यामस्तु शशकः किंचित्कर्बुरकस्तथा ॥
पूर्णगण्डश्च चतुरो मध्वक्षश्च प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 6 ॥
3.37
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गमानेन यथा पञ्च नराः स्मृताः ॥
स्त्रियः पञ्च तथा ज्ञेयास्ता एव मनुजोत्तम ॥ 1 ॥
पुरुषस्य समीपस्था कर्तव्या योषिदीश्वर ॥
नरस्कन्धप्रमाणेन कार्यैका सा यथामिति ॥ 2 ॥
अङ्गुली द्वौ नरात्क्षामं स्त्रियो मध्यं विधीयते ॥
अधिका च कटिः कार्या तथैव चतुरडुलम् ॥ 3 ॥
उरःप्रमाणतः कार्यौ स्तनौ नृप मनोहरौ ॥
नृपाश्च सर्वे कर्तव्या महापुरुषलक्षणाः ॥ 4 ॥
जालपादकराः कार्यास्तथा वै चक्रवर्तिनः ॥
ऊर्णेयं च भुवोर्मध्ये तेषां कार्यं तथा शुभम् ॥ ॥ 5 ॥
रेखाश्च करयोः कार्यास्तिस्रो राज्ञां मनोहराः ॥
शशक्षतजसङ्काशाः शस्त्रा वै क्षामकोटकाः ॥ 6 ॥
3.8.m:
Dark reddish, slightly mottled, / with full cheeks, clever, and with eyes resembling honey is celebrated the Śaśaka type.
3.37
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Just as five types of men are known through the measures of their major and minor limbs, / so too should five types of women be known, O best among men.
A woman standing beside a man should be depicted, O lord: / she should be made to reach up to the man's shoulder, according to proper proportion.
A woman's waist is prescribed to be two digits narrower than a man's; / and her hips should be made larger by four digits in the same manner.
Her breasts should be made charming according to the proportion of her chest, O king. / And all kings should be depicted with the marks of a cosmic man.
Universal emperors should be depicted with webbed hands and feet; / and an auspicious tuft of hair between their eyebrows should also be made.
Three charming lines should be depicted on the hands of kings; / their weapons, resembling the blood of a hare, should have slender tips.

3.8.s:
tadaṅgabhaṅginaḥ sūkṣmā nijasnehābhyalaṃkṛtāḥ ..
ghanendranīlasadṛthāḥ keśāḥ kāryāstathā śubhāḥ .. 7 ..
3.8.d:
तदङ्गभङ्गिनः सूक्ष्मा निजस्नेहाभ्यलंकृताः ॥
घनेन्द्रनीलसदृथाः केशाः कार्यास्तथा शुभाः ॥ 7 ॥
3.8.m: Curling along their limbs, fine, adorned with natural gloss, / resembling dense sapphire, their auspicious hair should be made.

3.8.s:
kuntalā dakṣiṇāvartāstaraṅgā siṃhakesarāḥ ..
vardharā jūṭaṭasarā ityetāḥ keśajātayaḥ .. 8 ..
3.8.d:
कुन्तला दक्षिणावर्तास्तरङ्गा सिंहकेसराः ॥
वर्धरा जूटटसरा इत्येताः केशजातयः ॥ 8 ॥
3.8.m: Curled, curling to the right, wavy, resembling a lion's mane, / straight, or tied in a topknot—such are the varieties of hair.

3.8.s:
cāpākāraṃ bhavennetraṃ matsyodaramathāpi vā ..
netramutpalapatrābhaṃ padmapatranibhaṃ tathā .. 9 ..
3.8.d:
चापाकारं भवेन्नेत्रं मत्स्योदरमथापि वा ॥
नेत्रमुत्पलपत्राभं पद्मपत्रनिभं तथा ॥ 9 ॥
3.8.m: An eye may be bow-shaped, or resembling a fish's belly, / or an eye resembling a blue lotus petal, or resembling a lotus petal,

3.8.s:
śānākṛtirmahārāja pañcamaṃ parikīrtitam ..
cāpākāraṃ bhavennetraṃ pramāṇena yathā striyaḥ .. 3.37.10 ..
3.8.d:
शानाकृतिर्महाराज पञ्चमं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
चापाकारं भवेन्नेत्रं प्रमाणेन यथा स्त्रियः ॥ 3.37.10 ॥
3.8.m: and the fifth is proclaimed to be shaped like an arrow, O great king. / The eye of a woman should be bow-shaped according to measure.

3.8.s:
matsyodarākhyaṃ kathitaṃ tathā yavacatuṣṭayam ..
netramutpalapatrākhyaṃ pramāṇātṣaḍyavaṃ smṛtam .. 11 ..
3.8.d:
मत्स्योदराख्यं कथितं तथा यवचतुष्टयम् ॥
नेत्रमुत्पलपत्राख्यं प्रमाणात्षड्यवं स्मृतम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.8.m: The one called resembling a fish's belly is stated to be four barleycorns; / the eye called resembling a blue lotus petal is declared to be six barleycorns in measure;

3.8.s:
padmapatranibhaṃ netraṃ pramāṇena yavā nava ..
śaśākṛtiṃ ca vijñeyaṃ tathaiva ca yavā daśa .. 12 ..
3.8.d:
पद्मपत्रनिभं नेत्रं प्रमाणेन यवा नव ॥
शशाकृतिं च विज्ञेयं तथैव च यवा दश ॥ 12 ॥
3.8.m: the eye resembling a lotus petal is nine barleycorns in measure; / and that shaped like an arrow is to be known as ten barleycorns.

3.8.s:
svamānā'ṅgulamānasya yavamānaṃ prakalpayet ..
cāpākāraṃ bhavennetraṃ yogabhūminirīkṣaṇāt .. 13 ..
3.8.d:
स्वमानाऽङ्गुलमानस्य यवमानं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
चापाकारं भवेन्नेत्रं योगभूमिनिरीक्षणात् ॥ 13 ॥
3.8.m: One should calculate the barleycorn measure from the digit of one's own standard. / The eye becomes bow-shaped when gazing down at the ground of meditation.

3.8.s:
matsyodarākṛti kāryaṃ nārīṇāṃ kāmināṃ tathā ..
netramutpalapatrābhaṃ nirvikārasya śasyate .. 14 ..
3.8.d:
मत्स्योदराकृति कार्यं नारीणां कामिनां तथा ॥
नेत्रमुत्पलपत्राभं निर्विकारस्य शस्यते ॥ 14 ॥
3.8.m: The shape of a fish's belly should be made for women and impassioned lovers; / the eye resembling a blue lotus petal is commended for one free of passion.

3.8.s:
trastassa rudataścaiva padmapatranibhaṃ bhavet ..
kruddhasya vedanāntasya netraṃ śārākṛtirbhavet .. 15 ..
3.8.d:
त्रस्तस्स रुदतश्चैव पद्मपत्रनिभं भवेत् ॥
क्रुद्धस्य वेदनान्तस्य नेत्रं शाराकृतिर्भवेत् ॥ 15 ॥
3.8.m: The eye of one terrified or weeping should resemble a lotus petal; / the eye of one enraged or in intense pain should be shaped like an arrow.

मुष्णन्तस्तेजसां तेजः परेषां नृपसत्तम ॥ 16॥
3.8.m: Sages, ancestors, and deities, O lord of men, / should be depicted adorned with their own radiance and full of splendour, / eclipsing the radiance of all others with their brilliance, O best of kings.

सम्यग्विचार्य नृपतिः स्वधिया यथोक्तं ह्येतत्प्रमाणमनुरूपमनिन्दितं च ॥
स्थानैरनेककिरणैः स्थिरभूमिलम्भैः कार्यं तदेव सकुमारमजिह्मरेखम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.38
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
नेत्रमुत्पलपत्राभं रक्तान्तं कृष्णतारकम॥
प्रसन्नं दीर्घपक्ष्मान्तं मनोज्ञं मृदु सत्तम। 1॥
देवतानां करं राजन्प्रजाहितकरं भवेत्॥
समे गोक्षीरवर्णाभे स्निग्धे जिह्माग्रपक्ष्मले ॥ 2 ॥
प्रसन्ने पद्मनेत्रान्ते मनोज्ञे प्रियदर्शने ॥
कृष्णतारे विशाले च नयने श्रीसुखप्रदे ॥ 3 ॥
चतुरस्रं सुसम्पूर्णं प्रसन्नं शुभलक्षणम् ॥
अत्रिकोणमवक्रं च अधिकारमुखं भवेत् ॥ 4 ॥
दीर्घमण्डलचक्राणि त्रिकोणादीनि यानि च ॥
वर्ज्यानि तानि देवानां प्रजासु शिवमिच्छता ॥ 5 ॥
कार्या हसप्रमाणेन देवा यदुकुलोद्वह ॥
तेषां च लोम कर्त्तव्यमक्षिपक्ष्मसु च भ्रुवोः ॥ 6 ॥
3.8.m:
Deliberating properly with his own intellect, the king should make this very [figure], graceful and with straight outlines, in accordance with the prescribed, faultless, and appropriate proportions, / through stances with multiple lines of light and firm vertical plummets.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / An eye resembling the petal of a blue lotus, red at the corners, with a black pupil, / clear, long-lashed, pleasing, and soft, O best of men,
gives [prosperity] when belonging to deities, O king, and brings welfare to subjects. / Symmetrical, with the colour and luster of cow's milk, glossy, with curved tips on the eyelashes,
serene, lotus-cornered, charming, pleasant to behold, / having black pupils, and broad—eyes such as these bestow fortune and happiness.
Square, well-filled, serene, having auspicious marks, / not triangular, and unbent should be an authoritative face.
Elongated, circular, discus-like, and triangular [shapes] / should be avoided for the gods by one wishing welfare among the subjects.
The gods, O descendant of Yadu, are to be made according to the proportion of a haṃsa; / and hair should be made on their eyelashes and eyebrows.

mukuṭaiḥ kuṇḍalairhāraiḥ keyūrairaṅgadaistathā .. 8 ..

śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā pādābharaṇacāriṇā .. 9 ..

aṃśukaṃ ca tathā kāryaṃ devatānāṃ manoharam .. 11 ..

3.8.d:
अतः शेषेषु गात्रेषु देवाः स्युर्लोमवर्जिताः ॥
द्विरष्टवर्षाकाराश्च तथा कार्या दिवौकसः ॥ 7 ॥
प्रसन्नवदना नित्यं तथा च स्मितदृष्टयः ॥
मुकुटैः कुण्डलैर्हारैः केयूरैरङ्गदैस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
भूषितास्तेऽथ कर्तव्याः शुभस्रग्दामधारिणः॥
श्रोणीसूत्रेण महता पादाभरणचारिणा ॥ 9 ॥
यज्ञोपवीतवंतश्च सावतंसास्तथैव च ॥
जान्वधोलम्बिना कार्याः शोभिना कटिवाससा ॥ 3.38.1 0॥
वामे मनुजशार्दूल दक्षिणं जानु दर्शयेत् ॥
अंशुकं च तथा कार्यं देवतानां मनोहरम् ॥ 11 ॥
प्रभा च तेषां कर्तव्या मूर्ध्नि मूर्ध्नः प्रमाणतः ॥
मण्डलाभा महाराज देवतातोऽनुकारिणी ॥ 12 ॥
ऊर्ध्वा दृष्टिरधोदृष्टिस्तिर्यक् तेषां विवर्जयेत ॥
हीनाधिका वा दीना वा क्रुद्धा रूक्षा तथैव च ॥ 13 ॥
ऊर्ध्वा तु मरणायोक्ता शोकायाधः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
तिर्यग्धनविनाशाय हीना भवति मृत्यवे ॥ 14 ॥
3.8.m:
On the rest of their limbs, the gods should be free of hair. / The dwellers of heaven should be made looking sixteen years of age,
ever with serene faces and smiling glances. / Adorned with diadems, earrings, necklaces, keyūras, and armlets,
they must be made wearing auspicious garlands and wreaths, / with a broad girdle and ankle-ornaments,
having sacred threads and ear-ornaments as well, / and wearing a handsome waist-garment hanging down below the knees.
On the left side, O tiger among men, one should show the right knee; / and the charming garment of the deities should be depicted in this manner.
A halo should be made on their head, proportionate to the head, / circular in appearance, O great king, matching the deity.
An upward gaze, a downward gaze, or an oblique gaze must be avoided for them, / or one that is deficient, excessive, wretched, angry, or dry.
For an upward gaze is said to bring death, a downward one is declared to bring grief, / an oblique one destroys wealth, and a deficient one causes demise.

3.8.s:
adhikā śokajananī dīnā ca nṛpasattama ..

अधिका शोकजननी दीना च नृपसत्तम ॥
रूक्षा धनक्षयाय स्यात्क्रुद्धा भयविवर्धिनी ॥ 15 ॥
शातोदरी न कर्तव्या न कार्या चाधिकोदरी ॥
सक्षता च न कर्तव्या तथा यदुकुलोद्वह ॥ 16 ॥
हीनाधिकप्रमाणा च रूक्षवर्णा तथैव च ॥
विवृतेन च वक्त्रेण नता च यदुनन्दन ॥ 17 ॥

शातोदरी क्षुद्भयदा मरणायाधिकोदरी ॥ 18 ॥
3.8.m: Nor [an image] with limbs that are deficient or excessive in measurement, O ruler of the earth. / An emaciated belly brings fear of famine; an overly large belly brings death.

3.8.s:

अधिका शोकजननी रूक्षवर्णा भयप्रदा ॥ 19 ॥
3.8.m: A wounded [image] is said to bring death; one deficient [in proportions] destroys wealth; / an excessive one produces sorrow; one of dry complexion instils fear;

3.8.s:
vivṛttena ca vaktreṇa kulanāśakarī bhavet ..

विवृत्तेन च वक्त्रेण कुलनाशकरी भवेत् ॥
प्राच्याभा धननाशाय दक्षिणेन च मृत्यवे ॥ 3.38.20 ॥
3.8.m: one with an open mouth brings about the ruin of the lineage; / leaning to the east brings loss of wealth, and leaning to the south brings death;

3.8.s:
paścimena sutaghnī ca codagbhayavivṛddhaye ..
pramāṇahīnā nāśāya adhikā deśanāśinī .. 21 ..
3.8.d:
पश्चिमेन सुतघ्नी च चोदग्भयविवृद्धये ॥
प्रमाणहीना नाशाय अधिका देशनाशिनी ॥ 21 ॥
3.8.m: leaning to the west kills sons, and to the north increases fear; / deficient in proportion it leads to destruction, and excessive it destroys the country;

3.8.s:

pramāṇahīnāṃ pratimāṃ tathā lakṣaṇavarjitām .. 22 ..
3.8.d:
अश्लक्ष्णा मरणायोक्ता क्रुद्धा रूपविनाशिनी ॥
प्रमाणहीनां प्रतिमां तथा लक्षणवर्जिताम् ॥ 22 ॥
3.8.m: rough, it is said to cause death, and angry, it destroys beauty. / An image that is deficient in proportion and devoid of [canonical] marks

3.8.s: āvāhitāñca viprendrairnāviśanti divaukasaḥ ..23..
3.8.d: आवाहिताञ्च विप्रेन्द्रैर्नाविशन्ति दिवौकसः ॥23॥
3.8.m: the dwellers of heaven will not enter, even when invoked by foremost brahmins.

3.8.s:
āviśaṃti tu tāṃ nityaṃ piśācā daityadānavāḥ ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena mānahīnāṃ vivarjayet .. 24 ..
3.8.d:
आविशंति तु तां नित्यं पिशाचा दैत्यदानवाः ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन मानहीनां विवर्जयेत् ॥ 24 ॥
3.8.m: Instead, piśācas, daityas, and dānavas enter it constantly; / therefore, with all effort, one should avoid an image lacking proper measurements.

3.8.s:
citralakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ praśastaṃ sarvamucyate ..

चित्रलक्षणसंयुक्तं प्रशस्तं सर्वमुच्यते ॥
आयुष्यं च यशस्यं च धनधान्यविवर्धनम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.8.m: Possessed of the characteristics of painting, everything is declared auspicious; / it prolongs life, confers fame, and increases wealth and grain.

3.8.s:

3.8.d:
तदेव लक्षणापेतं धनधान्यविनाशनम् ॥
देवा नरेन्द्र कर्त्तव्याः शोभावन्तः सदैव तु ॥
मृगेंद्रवृषनागानां हंसानां गतिभिः समाः ॥ 26 ॥
3.8.m: Devoid of those marks, it destroys wealth and grain. / The gods, O ruler of men, should always be made splendid, / matching the gaits of lions, bulls, elephants, and swans.

3.39
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
शुभाकारविहाराणि नानावर्णधराणि च॥
नव स्थानानि रूपाणां शृणु तान्यनुपूर्वशः ॥ 1 ॥
ऋज्वागतं भवेत्पूर्वमनृजु तदनन्तरम् ॥
साचीकृतशरीरं च भवत्यर्धविलोचनम् ॥ 2 ॥
ततः पार्श्वागतं नाम पुरावृत्तमनन्तरम् ॥
पृष्ठागतमधः कार्यं पुरावृत्तं समानतम् ॥ 3 ॥
एतान्यनेकभेदानि नव स्थानानि भूषिते ॥
एकैकस्येह भवतः शृणु मे नृप लक्षणम् ॥ 4 ॥
तत्राभिमुखमेवादौ स्पष्टमानगुणान्वितम् ॥
सुसम्पूर्णं सुचार्वङ्गं सुश्लक्ष्णमलवर्तकम् ॥ 5॥
सुशुद्धं मधुरं स्पष्टरेखासंस्कारभूषितम् ॥
यद्भवेत्स्थानमक्षीणगात्रं पृष्ठगतं तु तत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.8.m:
A painting endowed with auspicious marks is proclaimed blessed for the country, for the patron, and for the sovereign of the earth; / therefore, men devoted to careful exertion should diligently make it possessed of auspicious marks according to rule.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / With auspicious forms and movements, and bearing various colours, / there are nine stances of figures; hear them in proper order.
The frontal stance comes first, and next to that the non-frontal; / then the stance with turned body, and then the half-eyed.
Then the profile stance, next the averted; / the back-view is to be depicted downwards, [then] the averted, and the bowed.
These are the nine stances, having various divisions, O adorned one; / hear from me, O king, the characteristic of each one here.
Among them, first is the frontal stance, endowed with clear virtues of measurement, / fully complete, with very lovely limbs, very smooth, with subtle modelling,
very pure, sweet, adorned with refined and distinct line-work; / that stance in which the body is not diminished is indeed [to be known as] the [true frontal stance].

मुखस्यादावतोऽक्षीणं वक्षस उदरं तथा ॥
कट्या च स्कन्ध देशाच्च ऊरुतश्च क्षयं गता ॥ 7 ॥
नासापुटाधरोष्ठानां चतुर्थांशं च बुद्धिमत् ॥
क्षयं नीतं त्रिभागं च यस्य गात्रेभ्य एव च ॥ 8 ॥
कान्तारूपं परं स्थानं स्थानलम्भोपपादितम् ॥
एतदेवर्जुनामोक्तमनेककरणान्वितम् ॥ 9॥
यत्तिर्यग्भूमिलम्भेन नेत्रहारि सुवर्तनम्॥
सुकुमारं चतुर्भागं क्षीणं सर्वांगशोभनम् ॥ 3.39.10 ॥
अध्यर्धभ्रूललाटे चाप्यध्यर्धघ्राणमुत्कटम् ॥
भागक्षयावशेषार्धं कलापक्षीणलोचनम् ॥ 11 ॥
कलावलुप्तभ्रूलेखं लिखितं स्निग्धलेखया ॥
न च च्छायागतं कालं न चावऋजुकोपनम् ॥ 12 ॥
खेकारिकत्वाच्च नृप साचीकृतमिहोच्यते ॥
अर्धं नेत्रं मुखे यस्य लुप्तमवभ्रुवे तथा ॥ 13 ॥
3.8.m:
From the front of the face, the chest and belly are undiminished; / but at the waist, shoulder-region, and thighs, they are foreshortened.
A fourth part of the nostrils and the lower lip, O wise one, / and a third part from the limbs is brought to foreshortening;
a supreme stance of lovely form, executed through vertical plummets— / this very stance is called straight, endowed with multiple bodily gestures.
That which, by oblique vertical plummet, is eye-captivating, with excellent shading, / delicate, reduced by a fourth part, and charming in all its limbs,
with one and a half eyebrows and forehead, with a prominent one and a half nose, / having a remaining half after the reduction of parts, and an eye diminished by a kalā,
with the line of the eyebrow reduced by a kalā, drawn with a glossy line, / not fallen into dark shadow, and not trembling with crooked anger—
this is here called sācīkṛta, O king, because of its slanted stance. / In which half an eye is vanished on the face, and likewise on the lower brow,

3.8.s:

yasyāvalokyate pārśvaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ savyameva vā .. 17 ..

3.8.d:
भङ्गो ललाटमात्रश्च दृश्यानां सारमेव तु ॥
मात्रार्धां चैकतो गण्डं दृश्यमर्धकृतक्षयम् ॥ 14 ॥
मात्रार्धं कण्डरेखाया यवमाविष्कृतं हनोः ॥
उरसोऽर्धं मुखं लिप्तं नाभ्यास्याच्छिष्टमंगुलम् ॥ 15 ॥
अध्यर्धशेषा च कटी अन्यच्च दर्शनीकृतम् ॥
अध्यर्धाक्षं परिज्ञेयमाकारेणैवमादिना ॥ 16 ॥
च्छायागतमिति प्रोक्तं पर्यायेणैतदेव तु ॥
यस्यावलोक्यते पार्श्वं दक्षिणं सव्यमेव वा ॥ 17 ॥
कृत्स्नमन्यर्क्षयातं तदङ्गमङ्गगतिस्तथा ॥
एकाक्षमेकभ्रूलेखमरनामा ललाटवत् ॥ 18 ॥
एकं श्रोत्रं यदर्धं स्याच्चिबुकार्धं शिरोरुहम् ॥
गृहीतमानलावण्यमाधुर्यादिगुणान्वितम् ॥ 19 ॥
पार्श्वागतमिति प्रोक्तं तत्स्याद्भित्तिकसंज्ञितम् ॥
अपाक्रुद्धे कलक्षीणे कण्ठदेशे तथैव च ॥ 3.39.20॥
3.8.m:
and the curve is merely of the forehead, which is the very essence of what is seen, / and the cheek is seen on one side reduced by half a measure, foreshortened by half—
Half a measure of the throat line is revealed, and one barley-corn of the chin; / half of the chest and face is obscured, and one finger-breadth remains from the navel and mouth.
The waist has one and a half [parts] remaining, and the other [part] is brought into view; / through this and other such forms, it should be known as the three-quarter profile (adhyardhākṣa).
This very [posture] is also called the side-turned (chāyāgata) by another name. / That in which only the right or the left side is observed,
and the other limb has fully passed into diminution, as has the movement of that limb; / which has one eye, one brow-line, and whose forehead is without distinction,
in which there is one ear, half [the nose], half the chin, and [half] the hair of the head, / endowed with the qualities of standard proportion, loveliness, charm, and the like,
is called the profile (pārśvāgata); it is also designated as the wall-facing (bhittika). / In one turned away, diminished by time, and likewise in the region of the neck,

3.8.d:
बाहुगण्डललाटेषु कालाख्यं क्षयमागतम् ॥
बाहुवक्षःकटितटस्थितिगु॥॥॥॥॥॥॥॥। 21 ॥
द्विकलं द्विकलं ज्ञात्वा यथाभागं कृषीकृतम् ॥
अनुरूपप्रमाणेन नातितीक्ष्णाङ्गमेव च ॥ 22 ॥
एतद्गण्डपरावृत्तं स्थानं च परिकीर्तितम् ॥
पृष्ठतो यदपि व्यक्तं देहबन्धं मनोहरम् ॥ 23 ॥
वक्रभ्रुकुटिसर्वज्ञसन्धिबन्धनमेव च ॥
ईषच्च दर्शितापाङ्गकपोलजठरे पुनः ॥ 24 ॥
प्रकाशितैकपार्श्वेन सुस्थिरं दृष्टिहारि च ॥
स्वहीनमानलावण्यमाधुर्यादिगुणान्वितम् ॥ 25 ॥
लेखेषु पुस्तदेशेषु पृष्ठागतमिति स्मृतम् ॥
यस्योर्धमङ्गपत्येन भागेन समवस्थितम् ॥ 26 ॥
स्थितेर्ष्याभमुखेर्धाङ्गे परिवृत्तिवशाद्भवेत् ॥
किञ्चिच्छायागतौ कार्यावुपरिष्टादधः पुरः ॥ 27 ॥
3.8.m:
in the arms, cheeks, and forehead, that which has undergone the diminution called [foreshortening by] time, / the position of the arms, chest, and slopes of the waist...
recognising [each] as reduced by two digits according to the respective division, / with suitable proportions, and having limbs that are not overly sharp,
this is declared to be the cheek-turned (gaṇḍaparāvṛtta) posture. / Moreover, that which distinctly displays an attractive bodily form from behind,
with curved knitting of the brows, joints and sinews fully visible, / and where the outer corner of the eye, the cheek, and the belly are shown just slightly,
revealing one side, firm and captivating to the sight, / endowed with its own proper qualities of measurement, loveliness, charm, and so forth,
is remembered in drawings and model-work as the back-turned (pṛṣṭhāgata). / That whose upper limb is positioned in equal measure by its fallen part,
in the posture of one showing malice, where half the limb of the face is turned around by revolution; / slightly in the side-turned posture, it should be rendered above, below, and in front,

3.8.s:
ardhārdhagatasārūpyaṃ cirasagrāmyasaṃsthitam ..
madhyena netraramyena yathāyogavilopinā .. 28 ..
3.8.d:
अर्धार्धगतसारूप्यं चिरसग्राम्यसंस्थितम् ॥
मध्येन नेत्ररम्येन यथायोगविलोपिना ॥ 28 ॥
3.8.m: having the likeness of being quarter-turned, lasting and rustic in its posture, / with a pleasing eye in the middle, disappearing as appropriate,

3.8.s:
vijñeyaṃ dadhataḥ kāryaṃ parivṛttaṃ nareśvara ..
samagradṛṣṭisphigdeśaṃ daṣṭapādatalaṃ tu yat .. 29 ..
3.8.d:
विज्ञेयं दधतः कार्यं परिवृत्तं नरेश्वर ॥
समग्रदृष्टिस्फिग्देशं दष्टपादतलं तु यत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.8.m: holding [this], it is to be understood and executed as the rotated (parivṛtta), O lord of men. / That in which the region of the buttocks is viewed completely, but the sole of the foot is concealed,

3.8.s:
arvataḥ kṣīṇadṛṣṭārdhaṃ dṛśyā śeṣaṃ kaṭisthalam ..
luptapādāṅgulitalaṃ dṛśyāśeṣataladvayam .. 3.39.30 ..
3.8.d:
अर्वतः क्षीणदृष्टार्धं दृश्या शेषं कटिस्थलम् ॥
लुप्तपादाङ्गुलितलं दृश्याशेषतलद्वयम् ॥ 3.39.30 ॥
3.8.m: in which half the view is diminished from the front, and the remaining part of the waist is visible, / with the toes and sole vanished, yet both soles otherwise remaining visible,

3.8.s:
caturasraṃ susampūrṇamabhayānakadarśanam ..
prakāśīkṛtabāhuñca sudaṣṭamukhakandharam .. 31..
3.8.d:
चतुरस्रं सुसम्पूर्णमभयानकदर्शनम् ॥
प्रकाशीकृतबाहुञ्च सुदष्टमुखकन्धरम् ॥ 31॥
3.8.m: four-cornered, completely filled out, terrible in appearance, / with the arms displayed and the neck and face held tightly,

3.8.s:
luptaṃ jaṅghaikato jñeyaṃ nāmnā sthānaṃ samānataḥ ..
nīcānyetāni sarvāṇi tathoktairabhirājitam .. 32 ..
3.8.d:
लुप्तं जङ्घैकतो ज्ञेयं नाम्ना स्थानं समानतः ॥
नीचान्येतानि सर्वाणि तथोक्तैरभिराजितम् ॥ 32 ॥
3.8.m: with one shank hidden from view, should be known by name as the fully bowed (samānata) posture. / All these [nine] are inferior [to the central frontal view], yet adorned with the aforesaid [qualities].

3.8.s:
lakṣitairlakṣitavyāni tvayānukramaśo nava ..
eṣāṃ prajñāvaśeṣeṇa vikārāṇi bahūnyapi .. 33 ..
3.8.d:
लक्षितैर्लक्षितव्यानि त्वयानुक्रमशो नव ॥
एषां प्रज्ञावशेषेण विकाराणि बहून्यपि ॥ 33 ॥
3.8.m: These nine are to be perceived by you in succession, characterised by their marks. / Through the diversity of intellect, there are indeed many variations of these.

3.8.s:
ekaikaśaśca bhūbhāgaiḥ kartavyāni yathāvadhi ..
tvayā santaḥ samāsādya samyaṅ mānaṃ tu bhūtale .. 34 .
3.8.d:
एकैकशश्च भूभागैः कर्तव्यानि यथावधि ॥
त्वया सन्तः समासाद्य सम्यङ् मानं तु भूतले ॥ 34 ।
3.8.m: They are to be executed one by one according to the divisions of the surface as prescribed, / by you, O good one, having fully mastered the correct measurement upon the earth.

3.8.s:
sthānānīmāni mānādyairguṇairlekhyāni yatnataḥ ..
navaivaitāni dṛṣṭāni sarvabhāveṣvanindita .. .. 35 ..
3.8.d:
स्थानानीमानि मानाद्यैर्गुणैर्लेख्यानि यत्नतः ॥
नवैवैतानि दृष्टानि सर्वभावेष्वनिन्दित ॥ ॥ 35 ॥
3.8.m: These postures must be painted with effort, endowed with qualities such as proportion. / Only these nine have been seen in all situations, O blameless one;

3.8.s:
sthānāni nādhikamataḥ paramasti hi kiṃcana ..
jīvalokaṃ parikramya satataṃ sthāṇujaṅgamam ..36..
3.8.d:
स्थानानि नाधिकमतः परमस्ति हि किंचन ॥
जीवलोकं परिक्रम्य सततं स्थाणुजङ्गमम् ॥36॥
3.8.m: there is no posture whatsoever beyond this, / as one traverses through the world of living beings, both stationary and moving.

3.8.s:
uttamādhamamadhyeṣu pramāṇaguṇataḥ sadā..
citraṃ vicitraṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇaṃ trayameva ca ..37 ..
3.8.d:
उत्तमाधममध्येषु प्रमाणगुणतः सदा॥
चित्रं विचित्रं त्रिविधं प्रमाणं त्रयमेव च ॥37 ॥
3.8.m: In superior, inferior, and middling [beings], ever according to the quality of proportion, / painting is varied; and proportion is indeed threefold.

3.8.s:
kṣayavṛddhī ca kārtsyena mayā te'bhihite'nagha..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kṣayavṛddhividhiṃ kramāta..38..
3.8.d:
क्षयवृद्धी च कार्त्स्येन मया तेऽभिहितेऽनघ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि क्षयवृद्धिविधिं क्रमात॥38॥
3.8.m: Diminution and increase have been declared to you in their entirety, O sinless one. / Hereafter I shall explain the rule of diminution and increase in order.

3.8.s:
citravidbhirasaṃjñeyaṃ samāsenetareṇa ca ..
trayodaśavidhaivātra kṣayavṛddhirudāhṛtā .. 39 ..
3.8.d:
चित्रविद्भिरसंज्ञेयं समासेनेतरेण च ॥
त्रयोदशविधैवात्र क्षयवृद्धिरुदाहृता ॥ 39 ॥
3.8.m: Though not designated by painters in brief or otherwise, / thirteen kinds of diminution and increase are spoken of here,

3.8.s:
sthānānāṃ bahusaṃsthatvādaṅgāvayavasambhavā ..
sthānaṃ pṛṣṭha gataṃ pūrvamavarjugatameva ca .. 3.39.40 ..
3.8.d:
स्थानानां बहुसंस्थत्वादङ्गावयवसम्भवा ॥
स्थानं पृष्ठ गतं पूर्वमवर्जुगतमेव च ॥ 3.39.40 ॥
3.8.m: arising from the limbs and minor parts because of the various configurations of postures. / First is the back-facing posture (pṛṣṭhagata), then the straight posture (ṛjugata),

3.8.s:
madhyārdhārdhaṃ tathārdhārdhaṃ sācīkṛtamukhaṃ tathā ..
nataṃ gaṇḍaparāvṛttaṃ pṛṣṭhāgatamathāpi ca.. 41..
3.8.d:
मध्यार्धार्धं तथार्धार्धं साचीकृतमुखं तथा ॥
नतं गण्डपरावृत्तं पृष्ठागतमथापि च॥ 41॥
3.8.m: the three-quarter profile (madhyārdhārdha), the quarter profile (ardhārdha), the inclined-face (sācīkṛtamukha), / the bent (nata), the cheek-turned (gaṇḍaparāvṛtta), and also the back-turned (pṛṣṭhāgata),

3.8.s:
pārśvāgataṃ ca vijñeyamullepaṃ calitaṃ tathā ..
uttānaṃ valitaṃ ceti sthānāni tu trayodaśa .. 42 ..
3.8.d:
पार्श्वागतं च विज्ञेयमुल्लेपं चलितं तथा ॥
उत्तानं वलितं चेति स्थानानि तु त्रयोदश ॥ 42 ॥
3.8.m: the profile (pārśvāgata) is to be known, the anointed (ullepa), the moving (calita), / the supine (uttāna), and the twisted (valita)—these are the thirteen postures.

3.8.s:
kāryāṇyetāni sarvāṇi nāmasaṃsthānato nṛpa ..
maṇḍalānīha vaiśākhapratyālīḍhakriyākramaiḥ .. 43 ..
3.8.d:
कार्याण्येतानि सर्वाणि नामसंस्थानतो नृप ॥
मण्डलानीह वैशाखप्रत्यालीढक्रियाक्रमैः ॥ 43 ॥
3.8.m: All these are to be executed according to their names and configurations, O king, / as well as circular stances (maṇḍala) by the procedure of the vaiśākha, pratyālīḍha, and other [stances].

3.8.s:
samāścārddhasamāḥ pādāḥ susthitāni calāni ca ..
samāsamapadasthaṃ ca dvividhaṃ sthānakaṃ bhaveta .. 44 ..
3.8.d:
समाश्चार्द्धसमाः पादाः सुस्थितानि चलानि च ॥
समासमपदस्थं च द्विविधं स्थानकं भवेत ॥ 44 ॥
3.8.m: The feet are even and half-even, firm and moving; / the standing posture (sthānaka) is of two kinds: standing with feet even or uneven.

3.8.s:
tadgatvā padabhūyiṣṭhaṃ sthānaṃ samapadaṃ smṛtam ..
maṇḍalañca dvitīyaṃ syātsthānānyanyāni yāni ca .. 45 ..
3.8.d:
तद्गत्वा पदभूयिष्ठं स्थानं समपदं स्मृतम् ॥
मण्डलञ्च द्वितीयं स्यात्स्थानान्यन्यानि यानि च ॥ 45 ॥
3.8.m: That which is primarily based on [even] feet is remembered as the even-footed (samapada) posture; / the circular stance (maṇḍala) is the second; and whatever other postures there may be,

3.8.s:
tānyekasamapādāni vicitrāṇi calāni ca ..
tatra vaiśākhamālīḍhaṃ pratyālīḍhaṃ ca dhanvinām .. 46 ..
3.8.d:
तान्येकसमपादानि विचित्राणि चलानि च ॥
तत्र वैशाखमालीढं प्रत्यालीढं च धन्विनाम् ॥ 46 ॥
3.8.m: they have one foot even, and are diverse and mobile. / Among these, the vaiśākha, ālīḍha, and pratyālīḍha stances are for archers;

त्रिप्रकारेष्टिकाचूर्णं त्र्यंशं क्षिप्त्वा मृदस्ततः ॥
गुग्गुलं समधूच्छिष्टं मधुकं मुरुकं गुडम् ॥ 1 ॥
कुसुम्भं तैलसंयुक्तं कृत्वा दध्यात्समांशकम्॥
त्रिभागमग्निदग्धाया सुधायास्तत्र चूर्णयेत्.2॥
बिल्वजं द्व्यंशमिश्रं तत्प्रक्षिप्य मषकं कषम्॥
वालुकांशं ततो दद्यात्स्वानुरूपेण बुद्धिमान्॥3॥
ततः शकलतोयेन प्लावयेत्पिच्छिलेन तम्॥

3.8.d:
यदा शुष्कं भवेत्कुड्यं तत्प्रलिप्तमसत्कृतम् ॥
तया मृदा सर्जरसा तैलभागावियुक्तया ॥ 7 ॥
श्लक्ष्णीकुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन लेपनैः श्लक्ष्णमञ्जनैः ॥
मुहुर्मुहुश्च क्षीरेण सिक्ता मार्जनयत्नतः ॥ 8 ॥
सद्यः शोषमुपायातं कुड्यं तन्मनुजेश्वर ॥
अपि वर्षशतस्यान्ते न प्रणश्येत्तु कर्हिचित् ॥ 9 ॥
अनेनैव प्रकारेण द्विविधैर्वर्णकैर्युताः ॥
कर्तव्याश्चित्रवपुषा विविधा मणिभूमयः ॥ 3.40.10 ॥
कुड्ये शुष्के तिथौ शस्ते रूक्षे च गुणसंयुते ॥
चित्रायोगे विशेषेण श्वेतवासा यतात्मवान्॥ ॥ 11 ॥
ब्राह्मणान्पूजयित्वा तु स्वस्ति वाच्य प्रणम्य च ॥
तद्विदश्च यथान्यायं गुरूम्̐श्च गुरुवत्सलः ॥ 12 ॥
प्राङ्मुखो देवताध्यायी चित्रकर्म समाचरेत् ॥
श्वेतकाद्रवकृष्णाभिर्वर्तिकाभिर्यथाक्रमम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.8.m:
When the plastered wall has dried and been prepared,
[then] with that clay mixed with pine-resin and a proportion of oil,
he should diligently make it smooth with coats [of plaster] and smooth polishes,
sprinkled again and again with milk, through careful wiping.
That wall which has instantly attained dryness, O ruler of men,
even at the end of a hundred years would never be destroyed.
In this very manner, endowed with two kinds of pigments,
various jewel-floors should be made with painted forms.
When the wall is dry, on an auspicious lunar day, [when it is] free of moisture and endowed with [good] qualities,
especially in the conjunction with the constellation Citrā, clad in white, self-controlled,
having worshipped the brahmins, caused them to utter blessings, bowed down,
and [honoured] those skilled in the art according to rule, and his teachers, fond of his preceptors,
facing east, meditating on the deity, he should undertake the work of painting.
With white, yellow, and black brushes, in due order,

3.8.d:
आलिख्य स्थापयेद्विद्वान्प्रमाणे स्थानके तथा ॥
ततस्तु रञ्जयेद्रङ्गैर्यथास्थानानुरूपतः ॥ 14 ॥
श्यामा गौरी तथा तस्य च्छविः स्यात्तां प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
तस्याश्च लक्षणं प्रोक्तं प्राप्ताया नृप विस्तरे ॥ 15 ॥
मूलरङ्गाः स्मृताः पञ्च श्वेतः पीतो विलोमतः ॥
कृष्णो नीलश्च राजेन्द्र शतशोन्तरतः स्मृताः ॥ 16॥
पूर्णरङ्गविभागेन भावकल्पनया तथा॥
स्वबुद्ध्या कारयेद्रङ्गाञ्शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 17 ॥
नीलेष्वतिव्यतिकृतिः पालाश इति शस्यते ॥
स शुद्धः श्वेतमिश्रश्च नीलाभ्यधिक एव च ॥ 18 ॥
एकाधिकं च भवति च्छवीनामनुरूपतः ॥
श्वेताधिको वा न्यूनो वा समांशश्चेति स त्रिधा ॥19॥
स एकस्तम्भनायुक्तो बहुधैवं विकल्पते ॥
तेन दूर्वांकुरा पीतः कपित्थहरितः शुभाः ॥ 3.40.20 ॥

3.8.d:
मुद्गश्यामप्रकृतयः कर्तव्याश्छवयो नृप! ॥
नीलः पाण्डुरसम्पृक्तो विरङ्गः सोऽप्यनेकधा ॥ 21 ॥
अन्योन्याभ्यधिकं न्यूनं समांशवशकल्पना ॥
तेन नीलोत्पलनिभा माषसच्छायसुप्रभा ॥ 22 ॥
क्रियते च्छवयो रम्या यथायोगविनिश्चयात् ॥
लाक्षया श्वेतया युक्ता लाक्षारोधपिनद्धया।
रक्ता रक्तोत्पलश्यामा च्छविर्भवति शोभना॥
सापि नानाविधानन्यान्वर्णान्विकुरुते बहून् ॥24॥
रङ्गद्रव्याणि कनकं रजतं ताम्रमेव च ॥
अभ्रकं गजवन्तं च सिन्दूरं त्रपुरेव च ॥ 25 ॥
हरितालं सुधा लाक्षा तथा हिङ्गुलकं नृप ॥
नीलं च मनुजश्रेष्ठ तथान्ये सन्त्यनेकशः ॥ 26 ॥
देशेदेशे महाराज कार्यास्ते स्तम्भनायुताः ॥
लोहानां पत्रविन्यासं भवेद्वापि रसक्रिया ॥ 27 ॥
संकटं लोहविन्यस्तमभ्रकं द्रावणं भवेत ॥
एवं भवति लोहानां लेखने कर्मयोग्यता ॥ 28 ॥
3.8.m:
and mudga-dark complexions should be made, O king.
Blue mixed with pale yellow becomes an altered colour, and that too is manifold,
through the determination of parts where one exceeds the other, is less, or is equal;
by this, [a complexion] resembling a blue lotus and having the fair lustre of black gram,
charming complexions are made through accurate application.
Joined with white lac, bound with a mordant of lac,
red, and dark like a red lotus, the complexion becomes beautiful;
it also generates many other various colours.
The colour substances are gold, silver, copper,
mica, ivory, red lead, and tin,
yellow orpiment, lime, lac, and cinnabar, O king,
and indigo, O best of men; and likewise there are others in large numbers.
In various regions, O great king, they are to be prepared with a binding medium.
There should be the application of leaf or liquid preparation of metals.
When applied with metals, thick mica should be liquefied;
thus occurs the fitness of metals for work in painting.

3.8.s:
abhrakadrāvaṇaṃ proktaṃ surasendrajabhūmije ..
cambhāṃkutho'tha bakulā niryāsastambhanādbhaveta ..
sarveṣāmeva raṅgāṇāṃ sindūrakṣīra iṣyate .. 29 ..
mātaṅgadūrvārasapaṭṭabaddhaiḥ saṃstambhitaṃ citramudārapucchaiḥ ..

3.8.d:
अभ्रकद्रावणं प्रोक्तं सुरसेन्द्रजभूमिजे ॥
चम्भांकुथोऽथ बकुला निर्यासस्तम्भनाद्भवेत ॥
सर्वेषामेव रङ्गाणां सिन्दूरक्षीर इष्यते ॥ 29 ॥
मातङ्गदूर्वारसपट्टबद्धैः संस्तम्भितं चित्रमुदारपुच्छैः ॥
धौतं जलेनापि न नाशयेत तिष्ठत्यनेकान्यपि वत्सराणि ॥ 3.40.30 ॥
3.8.m:
The liquefaction of mica is declared in [liquids] produced from earth, tulsi, and indraja;
there may be camphor, nut-grass, or the resin from the bakula for binding.
For all colours, the milk of the sindūra [tree] is preferred.
A painting bound with juices of elephant-grass and dūrvā on a cloth base, fixed with noble [hair] brushes,
even when washed with water would not perish, and endures for many years.

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
satyaṃ ca vaiṇikaṃ caiva nāgaraṃ miśrameva ca ..

3.9.d:
3.41
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सत्यं च वैणिकं चैव नागरं मिश्रमेव च ॥
चित्रं चतुर्विधं प्रोक्तं तस्य वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.9.m:
3.41
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
'Satya', 'vaiṇika', 'nāgara', and 'miśra'—
painting is declared to be of four kinds; I shall state their characteristics.

3.9.s:
yatkiñcillokasādṛśyaṃ citraṃ tatsatyamucyate ..
dīrghāṅge sapramāṇaṃ ca sukumāraṃ subhūmikama..2..
3.9.d:
यत्किञ्चिल्लोकसादृश्यं चित्रं तत्सत्यमुच्यते ॥
दीर्घाङ्गे सप्रमाणं च सुकुमारं सुभूमिकम॥2॥
3.9.m:
That painting which has some resemblance to the world is called 'satya';
[it is] with elongated limbs, proportionate, delicate, and on an excellent ground.

3.9.s:
caturasraṃ susampūrṇaṃ na dīrghaṃ nolbaṇākṛtim..
pramāṇaṃ sthānalambhāḍhyaṃ vaiṇikaṃ tannigadyate..3..
3.9.d:
चतुरस्रं सुसम्पूर्णं न दीर्घं नोल्बणाकृतिम्॥
प्रमाणं स्थानलम्भाढ्यं वैणिकं तन्निगद्यते॥3॥
3.9.m:
Square, well-proportioned, not long, not of exaggerated form,
rich in proportion, posture, and line—that is called 'vaiṇika'.

3.9.s:
dṛḍhopacitasarvāṅgaṃ vartulaṃ nadyanolbaṇama ..
citraṃ taṃ nāgaraṃ jñeyaṃ svalpamālyavibhūṣaṇam .. 4 ..
3.9.d:
दृढोपचितसर्वाङ्गं वर्तुलं नद्यनोल्बणम ॥
चित्रं तं नागरं ज्ञेयं स्वल्पमाल्यविभूषणम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.9.m:
Having firm, well-developed limbs all over, rounded, not slack, not exaggerated,
with few garlands and ornaments—that painting is to be known as 'nāgara'.

3.9.s:
citramiśraṃ samākhyātaṃ samāsānmanujottama ..
tisraśca vartanāḥ proktāḥ patrāhaivikabindujāḥ .. 5 ..
3.9.d:
चित्रमिश्रं समाख्यातं समासान्मनुजोत्तम ॥
तिस्रश्च वर्तनाः प्रोक्ताः पत्राहैविकबिन्दुजाः ॥ 5 ॥
3.9.m:
The mixed [style] of painting is declared concisely, O best of men.
And three methods of shading are spoken of: produced by lines, by hairs, and by dots.

3.9.s:
patrākṛtibhī rekhābhiḥ kathitātra ca vartanā ..
atīva kathitā sūkṣmā tathāhairikavartanā .. 6 ..
3.9.d:
पत्राकृतिभी रेखाभिः कथितात्र च वर्तना ॥
अतीव कथिता सूक्ष्मा तथाहैरिकवर्तना ॥ 6 ॥
3.9.m:
Shading by lines of leaf-like shape is declared here;
likewise, shading by hairs is spoken of as exceedingly fine;

3.9.s:
tathā ca stambhanāyuktā kathitā binduvartanā ..
daurbalyabiṃdurekhatvamavibhaktatvameva ca .. 7 ..
3.9.d:
तथा च स्तम्भनायुक्ता कथिता बिन्दुवर्तना ॥
दौर्बल्यबिंदुरेखत्वमविभक्तत्वमेव च ॥ 7 ॥
3.9.m:
and shading by dots is declared as combined with binding.
Weakness, line of dots, lack of differentiation,

3.9.s:
bṛhadaṇḍauṣṭhanetratvamaviruddhatvameva ca ..
mānavākāratā ceti citraśeṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 8 ..
3.9.d:
बृहदण्डौष्ठनेत्रत्वमविरुद्धत्वमेव च ॥
मानवाकारता चेति चित्रशेषाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 8 ॥
3.9.m:
enlarged testicles, lips, and eyes, and inconsistency,
and [mere] human form—these are proclaimed as defects in painting.

3.9.s:
sthānapramāṇabhūlambo madhuratvaṃ vibhaktatā ..
sādṛśyaṃ pakṣavṛddhiśca guṇāścitrasya kīrtitāḥ .. 9 .
3.9.d:
स्थानप्रमाणभूलम्बो मधुरत्वं विभक्तता ॥
सादृश्यं पक्षवृद्धिश्च गुणाश्चित्रस्य कीर्तिताः ॥ 9 ।
3.9.m:
Posture, proportion, plumb-line, sweetness, distinctness,
resemblance, and foreshortening are proclaimed as the merits of a painting.

3.9.s:
rekhā ca vartanā caiva bhūṣaṇaṃ varṇameva ca ..
vijñeyā manujaśreṣṭha citrakarmasu bhūṣaṇam .. 3.41.10 ..
3.9.d:
रेखा च वर्तना चैव भूषणं वर्णमेव च ॥
विज्ञेया मनुजश्रेष्ठ चित्रकर्मसु भूषणम् ॥ 3.41.10 ॥
3.9.m:
Line, shading, ornamentation, and colour
are to be known, O best of men, as the adornment in works of painting.

3.9.s:
rekhāṃ praśaṃsantyācāryā vartanāṃ ca vicakṣaṇāḥ ..
striyo bhūṣaṇamicchanti varṇāḍhyamitare janāḥ .. 11 ..
3.9.d:
रेखां प्रशंसन्त्याचार्या वर्तनां च विचक्षणाः ॥
स्त्रियो भूषणमिच्छन्ति वर्णाढ्यमितरे जनाः ॥ 11 ॥
3.9.m:
Masters praise the line, and connoisseurs the shading;
women desire ornamentation, and other people richness of colour.

3.9.s:
iti matvā tathā yatnaḥ kartavyaścitrakarmaṇi ..
sarvasya cittagrahaṇaṃ yathā syānmanujottama .. 12 ..
3.9.d:
इति मत्वा तथा यत्नः कर्तव्यश्चित्रकर्मणि ॥
सर्वस्य चित्तग्रहणं यथा स्यान्मनुजोत्तम ॥ 12 ॥
3.9.m:
Thinking thus, such effort should be made in the work of painting
that it may captivate the minds of all, O best of men.

3.9.s:
durāsanaṃ durānītaṃ pipāsā cānyacittatā ..
ete citravināśasya hetavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 13 ..
3.9.d:
दुरासनं दुरानीतं पिपासा चान्यचित्तता ॥
एते चित्रविनाशस्य हेतवः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 13 ॥
3.9.m:
An uncomfortable seat, an ill-prepared [surface], thirst, and inattention—
these are proclaimed as the causes of the ruin of a painting.

3.9.s:
svānuliptāvakāśā ca nideśaṃ madhukā śubhā ..
suprasannābhiguptā ca bhūmiḥ syāccitrakarmaṇi .. 14 ..
3.9.d:
स्वानुलिप्तावकाशा च निदेशं मधुका शुभा ॥
सुप्रसन्नाभिगुप्ता च भूमिः स्याच्चित्रकर्मणि ॥ 14 ॥
3.9.m:
With its space well plastered, auspicious with honey-coloured coating,
very bright, and well protected should be the ground in the work of painting.

3.9.s:
susnigdhavispaṣṭasuvarṇarekhaṃ vidvānyathādeśaviśeṣaveśam ..
pramāṇaśobhābhirahīyamāna kṛtaṃ bhaveccitramatīva citram .. 15 ..
3.42
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
yathā devastathā citre kartavyaḥ pṛthivīśvara ..
ekaikaṃ rūpake loma kartavyaṃ pṛthivīkṣitām .. 1 ..
ṛṣayaśca sagandharvā daityāśca saha dānavāḥ ..
mantriṇaśca mahārāja saṃvatsarapurohitau .. 2 ..
kāryā bhadrapramāṇena brāhmaṇāśca nareśvara ..
ṛṣayastatra kartavyā jaṭājūṭopaśobhitāḥ .. 3 ..
kṛṣṇājinottarāsaṅgā durbalāstejasā yutāḥ ..
devatāścāpi gandharvā mukuṭena vivarjitāḥ .. 4 ..
kartavyāste mahārāja śikharairupaśobhitāḥ ..
brahmavarcasvino viprāḥ śuklāmbaradharāstathā .. 5 ..
mantriṇaśca mahārāja sāṃvatsarapurohitau ..
sarvālaṅkārasaṃyuktānevolbaṇavibhūṣaṇān .. 6 ..
3.9.d:
सुस्निग्धविस्पष्टसुवर्णरेखं विद्वान्यथादेशविशेषवेशम् ॥
प्रमाणशोभाभिरहीयमान कृतं भवेच्चित्रमतीव चित्रम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.42
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
यथा देवस्तथा चित्रे कर्तव्यः पृथिवीश्वर ॥
एकैकं रूपके लोम कर्तव्यं पृथिवीक्षिताम् ॥ 1 ॥
ऋषयश्च सगन्धर्वा दैत्याश्च सह दानवाः ॥
मन्त्रिणश्च महाराज संवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥ 2 ॥
कार्या भद्रप्रमाणेन ब्राह्मणाश्च नरेश्वर ॥
ऋषयस्तत्र कर्तव्या जटाजूटोपशोभिताः ॥ 3 ॥
कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासङ्गा दुर्बलास्तेजसा युताः ॥
देवताश्चापि गन्धर्वा मुकुटेन विवर्जिताः ॥ 4 ॥
कर्तव्यास्ते महाराज शिखरैरुपशोभिताः ॥
ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनो विप्राः शुक्लाम्बरधरास्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
मन्त्रिणश्च महाराज सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥
सर्वालङ्कारसंयुक्तानेवोल्बणविभूषणान् ॥ 6 ॥
3.9.m:
A painting made by the wise [artist] with very glossy, distinct, and beautifully coloured lines, with dress appropriate to the specific region,
not lacking in proportion and beauty, becomes exceedingly wondrous.
3.42
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Just as a god is, so should he be made in painting, O ruler of the earth;
each single hair should be made in the depiction of kings of the earth.
Sages, along with gandharvas, daityas together with dānavas,
and ministers, O great king, the astrologer and the family priest,
And brahmins, O lord of men, should be made according to the Bhadra proportion. / There, sages should be represented adorned with matted locks,
having upper garments of black antelope skin, emaciated, [yet] full of spiritual brilliance. / The gods and also Gandharvas, devoid of crowns,
should be made, O great king, adorned with crests. / Brahmins should be endowed with the splendour of sacred learning and dressed in white garments.
Ministers as well, O great king, and the astrologer and the royal priest, / should be provided with all ornaments, yet without excessive embellishment.

3.9.s:
mukuṭena vihīnāṃstu soṣṇīṣānkārayecca tān ..
daityāśca dānavāścaiva kartavyā bhrukuṭīmukhāḥ .. '7 ..
vartulākṣāstathā kāryā bhīmavaktrāstathaiva ca ..
teṣāmabhyuddhato veṣaḥ kartavyaḥ pṛthivīpate .. 8 ..
rudrapramāṇāḥ kartavyāstathā vidyādharā nṛpa ..
sapatnīkāśca te kāryā mālyālaṅkāradhāriṇaḥ .. 9 ..
khaḍgahastāśca te kāryā gagane vātha vā bhuvi ..
mālavyaparimāṇena kinnaroragarākṣasāḥ .. 3.42.10 ..
rucakasya pramāṇena yakṣāḥ kāryā narādhipa ..
śaśakasya pramāṇena pradhānaṃ mānavaṃ likhet .. 11 ..
piśācā vāmanāḥ kubjāḥ pramathāśca mahībhujaḥ ..
mānanniyamataḥ kāryaṃ rūpanniyamatastathā .. 12..
svānurūpapramāṇāśca sarveṣāṃ yoṣitaḥ smṛtāḥ..
kinnarā dvividhāḥ proktā nṛvaktrā hayavigrahāḥ .. 13 ..
3.9.d:
मुकुटेन विहीनांस्तु सोष्णीषान्कारयेच्च तान् ॥
दैत्याश्च दानवाश्चैव कर्तव्या भ्रुकुटीमुखाः ॥ '7 ॥
वर्तुलाक्षास्तथा कार्या भीमवक्त्रास्तथैव च ॥
तेषामभ्युद्धतो वेषः कर्तव्यः पृथिवीपते ॥ 8 ॥
रुद्रप्रमाणाः कर्तव्यास्तथा विद्याधरा नृप ॥
सपत्नीकाश्च ते कार्या माल्यालङ्कारधारिणः ॥ 9 ॥
खड्गहस्ताश्च ते कार्या गगने वाथ वा भुवि ॥
मालव्यपरिमाणेन किन्नरोरगराक्षसाः ॥ 3.42.10 ॥
रुचकस्य प्रमाणेन यक्षाः कार्या नराधिप ॥
शशकस्य प्रमाणेन प्रधानं मानवं लिखेत् ॥ 11 ॥
पिशाचा वामनाः कुब्जाः प्रमथाश्च महीभुजः ॥
मानन्नियमतः कार्यं रूपन्नियमतस्तथा ॥ 12॥
स्वानुरूपप्रमाणाश्च सर्वेषां योषितः स्मृताः॥
किन्नरा द्विविधाः प्रोक्ता नृवक्त्रा हयविग्रहाः ॥ 13 ॥
3.9.m:
One should have them made devoid of crowns, but wearing turbans. / Daityas and Dānavas should be made with frowning faces; / they should also be made round-eyed and with terrible mouths. / Their attire, O lord of the earth, should be haughty.
Vidyādharas, O king, should be made according to the Rudra proportion; / and they should be represented accompanied by their wives, wearing garlands and ornaments.
They should be made with swords in hand, whether in the sky or on the earth. / Kinnaras, serpents, and Rākṣasas are to be made according to the Mālavya proportion.
Yakṣas, O lord of men, should be made according to the Rucaka proportion; / one should paint the principal mortal according to the Śaśaka proportion.
Piśācas, dwarfs, hunchbacks, and the Pramathas of the lord of the earth / should be made in measurement according to rule, and likewise in form according to rule.
And the women of all [these classes] are taught to have the proportion appropriate to their [males]. / Kinnaras are declared to be of two kinds: having human faces and horse bodies,

3.9.s:
nṛdehāścāśvavaktrāśca tathānye parikīrtitāḥ ..
aśvavaktrāstu kartavyāḥ sarvālaṅkāradhāriṇaḥ .. 14 ..
gītavādyasamāyuktā dyutimantastathaiva ca ..
utkacā rākṣasāḥ kāryā vikalākṣā vibhīṣaṇāḥ .. 15 ..
3.9.d:
नृदेहाश्चाश्ववक्त्राश्च तथान्ये परिकीर्तिताः ॥
अश्ववक्त्रास्तु कर्तव्याः सर्वालङ्कारधारिणः ॥ 14 ॥
गीतवाद्यसमायुक्ता द्युतिमन्तस्तथैव च ॥
उत्कचा राक्षसाः कार्या विकलाक्षा विभीषणाः ॥ 15 ॥
3.9.m:
and the others are renowned as having human bodies and horse faces. / Those with horse faces should be made wearing all ornaments,
accompanied by song and musical instruments, and endowed with radiant beauty. / Rākṣasas should be made with dishevelled hair, irregular eyes, and terrifying.

3.9.s:
devakārāśca kartavyā nāgāḥ phaṇavirājitāḥ ..
sālaṃkārā smṛtāḥ sarve yakṣāste'bhihitā mayā .. 16 ..
3.9.d:
देवकाराश्च कर्तव्या नागाः फणविराजिताः ॥
सालंकारा स्मृताः सर्वे यक्षास्तेऽभिहिता मया ॥ 16 ॥
3.9.m: Nāgas should be made in the form of gods, adorned with hoods. / All Yakṣas have been declared by me as endowed with ornaments.

3.9.s:
surāṇāṃ pramathāḥ kāryāḥ pramāṇena vivarjitāḥ ..
piśācāśca tathā kāryā pramāṇena vivarjitāḥ .. 17 ..
3.9.d:
सुराणां प्रमथाः कार्याः प्रमाणेन विवर्जिताः ॥
पिशाचाश्च तथा कार्या प्रमाणेन विवर्जिताः ॥ 17 ॥
3.9.m: The Pramathas of the gods should be made devoid of [standard] proportions; / Piśācas, likewise, should be made devoid of [standard] proportions.

3.9.s:
nānāsattvamukhāḥ kāryā devatānāṃ tathā gaṇāḥ ..
nānāveśā mahārāja nānāyudhadharāstathā .. 18 ..
3.9.d:
नानासत्त्वमुखाः कार्या देवतानां तथा गणाः ॥
नानावेशा महाराज नानायुधधरास्तथा ॥ 18 ॥
3.9.m: The troops of the gods should be made with faces of various creatures, / in various dress, O great king, and bearing various weapons,

3.9.s:
nānākrīḍāprasaktāśca nānākarmakarāstathā ..
ekarūpāstu kartavyā vaiṣṇavānāṃ tathā gaṇāḥ .. 19 ..
3.9.d:
नानाक्रीडाप्रसक्ताश्च नानाकर्मकरास्तथा ॥
एकरूपास्तु कर्तव्या वैष्णवानां तथा गणाः ॥ 19 ॥
3.9.m: intent upon various sports and performing various tasks. / But the troops of the Vaiṣṇavas should be made of uniform appearance.

3.9.s:
tatrāpi teṣāṃ kartavyā bhedāścatvāra eva ca ..
vāsudevasamāḥ kāryā vāsudevagaṇāḥ śubhāḥ .. 3.42.20 ..
3.9.d:
तत्रापि तेषां कर्तव्या भेदाश्चत्वार एव च ॥
वासुदेवसमाः कार्या वासुदेवगणाः शुभाः ॥ 3.42.20 ॥
3.9.m: Even there, four divisions of them should be made: / the auspicious attendants of Vāsudeva should be made resembling Vāsudeva;

3.9.s:
saṃkarṣaṇena sadṛśāstadgaṇāśca tathā smṛtāḥ ..
pradyumnenāniruddhena tadgaṇāḥ sadṛśāstathā .. 21 ..
3.9.d:
संकर्षणेन सदृशास्तद्गणाश्च तथा स्मृताः ॥
प्रद्युम्नेनानिरुद्धेन तद्गणाः सदृशास्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
3.9.m: his attendants are also taught to be similar to Saṃkarṣaṇa; / likewise, his attendants are similar to Pradyumna and Aniruddha.

3.9.s:
tatprabhāvāḥ smṛtāḥ sarve tadāyudhadharāstathā ..
nīlotpaladalaśyāmāścandraśubhrāstathaiva ca .. 22 ..
3.9.d:
तत्प्रभावाः स्मृताः सर्वे तदायुधधरास्तथा ॥
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामाश्चन्द्रशुभ्रास्तथैव च ॥ 22 ॥
3.9.m: They are all taught to have their splendour and to bear their weapons: / dark like the petal of a blue lotus, and bright as the moon,

3.9.s:
tathā marakatākārā sindūrasadṛśaprabhāḥ ..
rucakasya tu mānena veśyāḥ kāryāstathā striyaḥ .. 23 ..
3.9.d:
तथा मरकताकारा सिन्दूरसदृशप्रभाः ॥
रुचकस्य तु मानेन वेश्याः कार्यास्तथा स्त्रियः ॥ 23 ॥
3.9.m: and also having the appearance of emerald, or radiant like red lead. / Courtesans and [similar] women should be made according to the Rucaka proportion.

3.9.s:
veśyānāmuddhataṃ veśaṃ kāryaṃ śṛṅgārasammatam ..
mālavyāmānataḥ kāryā lajjāvatyaḥ kulastriyaḥ .. 24 ..
3.9.d:
वेश्यानामुद्धतं वेशं कार्यं शृङ्गारसम्मतम् ॥
मालव्यामानतः कार्या लज्जावत्यः कुलस्त्रियः ॥ 24 ॥
3.9.m: The dress of courtesans should be made alluring, appropriate to erotic passion. / Women of good family, possessing modesty, should be made according to the Mālavya proportion,

3.9.s:
nātyunnatena veśena sālaṃkārāstathaiva ca ..
daityadānavayakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 25 ..
3.9.d:
नात्युन्नतेन वेशेन सालंकारास्तथैव च ॥
दैत्यदानवयक्षाणां राक्षसानां तथैव च ॥ 25 ॥
3.9.m: with attire not excessively prominent, and likewise adorned with ornaments. / For Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas alike,

3.9.s:
rūpavatyastathā kāryāḥ patayo manujasattama ..
mātaraḥ svena rūpeṇa tathā kāryā narādhipa .. 26 ..
3.9.d:
रूपवत्यस्तथा कार्याः पतयो मनुजसत्तम ॥
मातरः स्वेन रूपेण तथा कार्या नराधिप ॥ 26 ॥
3.9.m: their wives, O best of men, should be made beautiful. / The mothers should be represented in their own form, O lord of men;

3.9.s:
piśācānāṃ ca patnyo'pi kāryāstadrūpasaṃyutā ..
vibhartṛkāstu kartavyā striyaḥ palitasaṃyutāḥ .. 27 ..
3.9.d:
पिशाचानां च पत्न्योऽपि कार्यास्तद्रूपसंयुता ॥
विभर्तृकास्तु कर्तव्या स्त्रियः पलितसंयुताः ॥ 27 ॥
3.9.m: and the wives of Piśācas should also be made endowed with their form. / Women without husbands, however, should be made with grey hair,

3.9.s:
śuklavastraparīdhānāḥ sarvālaṅkāravarjitāḥ ..
kubjā vāmanikā vṛddhā tathā rūpavatī bhavet .. 28 ..
3.9.d:
शुक्लवस्त्रपरीधानाः सर्वालङ्कारवर्जिताः ॥
कुब्जा वामनिका वृद्धा तथा रूपवती भवेत् ॥ 28 ॥
3.9.m: clad in white garments, and stripped of all ornaments. / A hunchbacked, dwarfish, or elderly woman may likewise be beautiful.

3.9.s:
rājastrīṇāṃ parīvāre vṛddhaḥ syātkañcukī punaḥ ..
rucakasya tu mānena vaiśyamānaṃ vidhīyate .. 29 ..
3.9.d:
राजस्त्रीणां परीवारे वृद्धः स्यात्कञ्चुकी पुनः ॥
रुचकस्य तु मानेन वैश्यमानं विधीयते ॥ 29 ॥
3.9.m: In the retinue of royal women there should also be an aged chamberlain. / The proportion of a vaiśya is prescribed according to the Rucaka [measurement],

3.9.s:
śaśakasya tu mānena śūdramānaṃ tathaiva ca ..
yathā jātyanurūpeṇa veṣeṇa manujeśvara .. 3.42.30 ..
3.9.d:
शशकस्य तु मानेन शूद्रमानं तथैव च ॥
यथा जात्यनुरूपेण वेषेण मनुजेश्वर ॥ 3.42.30 ॥
3.9.m: and the proportion of a śūdra according to the Śaśaka [measurement]. / In attire according to caste, O lord of men,

3.9.s:
daityādiyoṣitāṃ kāryāḥ paricārastriyaḥ sadā ..
mahāśirā mahorasko mahānāso mahāhanuḥ .. 31 ..
3.9.d:
दैत्यादियोषितां कार्याः परिचारस्त्रियः सदा ॥
महाशिरा महोरस्को महानासो महाहनुः ॥ 31 ॥
3.9.m: the maidservants of the women of Daityas and the rest should always be made. / With a large head, broad chest, large nose, and large jaw,

3.9.s:
pīta skandhabhujagrīvaḥ parimāṇena cocchritaḥ ..
tritaraṅgalalāṭaśca vyomadṛṣṭirmahākaṭiḥ .. 32 ..
3.9.d:
पीत स्कन्धभुजग्रीवः परिमाणेन चोच्छ्रितः ॥
त्रितरङ्गललाटश्च व्योमदृष्टिर्महाकटिः ॥ 32 ॥
3.9.m: with stout shoulders, arms, and neck, tall in stature, / with a forehead [creased] with three waves, gazing towards the sky, with a broad waist,

3.9.s:
dṛptaścitravidā kāryaḥ senāyāḥ patirūrjitaḥ .. .
yodhāḥ kāryā mahārāja prāyaśo bhrukuṭīmukhāḥ .. 33 ..
3.9.d:
दृप्तश्चित्रविदा कार्यः सेनायाः पतिरूर्जितः ॥ ।
योधाः कार्या महाराज प्रायशो भ्रुकुटीमुखाः ॥ 33 ॥
3.9.m: haughty and mighty, the commander of an army should be made by one skilled in painting. / Warriors, O great king, should mostly be made with frowning faces,

3.9.s:
kiṃciduddhatavegāśca kāryāścoddhatadarśanāḥ ..
abhyudgatāśca kartavyā āyudhīyāḥ padātayaḥ .. 34 ..
3.9.d:
किंचिदुद्धतवेगाश्च कार्याश्चोद्धतदर्शनाः ॥
अभ्युद्गताश्च कर्तव्या आयुधीयाः पदातयः ॥ 34 ॥
3.9.m: with somewhat impetuous speed, and having a haughty appearance. / Infantrymen bearing weapons should be made rushing forward;

3.9.s:
khaḍgacarmadharāḥ kāryāḥ karṇāṭakavapurdharāḥ ..
varabāṇadharāḥ kāryā nagnajaṅghāśca dhanvinaḥ .. 35 ..
3.9.d:
खड्गचर्मधराः कार्याः कर्णाटकवपुर्धराः ॥
वरबाणधराः कार्या नग्नजङ्घाश्च धन्विनः ॥ 35 ॥
3.9.m: they should be made holding sword and shield, with the build of Karṇāṭaka [soldiers]. / Archers should be made bearing excellent arrows, with bare shanks,

3.9.s:
nātyuddhatena veṣeṇa sopānatkāstathaiva te ..
yathoktalakṣaṇāḥ kāryāḥ kuñjarāsturagādayaḥ .. 36 ..
3.9.d:
नात्युद्धतेन वेषेण सोपानत्कास्तथैव ते ॥
यथोक्तलक्षणाः कार्याः कुञ्जरास्तुरगादयः ॥ 36 ॥
3.9.m: with attire not excessively showy, and wearing shoes. / Elephants, horses, and the like should be made with their prescribed characteristics.

3.9.s:
hastyārohāstu kartavyā muhuḥ śyāmāstu varṇataḥ ..
keśaiśca jūṭaṭamaraiḥ sālaṃkārāstathaiva ca. .. 37 ..
3.9.d:
हस्त्यारोहास्तु कर्तव्या मुहुः श्यामास्तु वर्णतः ॥
केशैश्च जूटटमरैः सालंकारास्तथैव च॥। 37 ॥
3.9.m: Elephant riders, however, should be made dark in complexion, / with hair tied in high topknots, and likewise adorned with ornaments.

3.9.s:
udīcyaveśāḥ kartavyāsturagāṇāṃ tu sādinaḥ ..
uddhatena tu veṣeṇa kartavyā bandinastathā ..38 ..
3.9.d:
उदीच्यवेशाः कर्तव्यास्तुरगाणां तु सादिनः ॥
उद्धतेन तु वेषेण कर्तव्या बन्दिनस्तथा ॥38 ॥
3.9.m: Horse riders should be made in northern dress. / Bards should be made in haughty attire,

3.9.s:
sirādarśitakaṇṭhāśca tathaivonmukhadṛṣṭayaḥ ..
āhvānakāstu kartavyāḥ kapilāḥ kekarekṣaṇāḥ .. 39 ..
3.9.d:
सिरादर्शितकण्ठाश्च तथैवोन्मुखदृष्टयः ॥
आह्वानकास्तु कर्तव्याः कपिलाः केकरेक्षणाः ॥ 39 ॥
3.9.m: with veins visible in their necks, and with their gaze directed upward. / Summoners should be made tawny, with squinting eyes,

3.9.s:
kiṃciddānavasaṅkāśāḥ prāyaśo daṇḍapāṇayaḥ ..
na kekarānna kapilānyuddhe dvaṃdvānsamālikhet .. 3.42.40 ..
3.9.d:
किंचिद्दानवसङ्काशाः प्रायशो दण्डपाणयः ॥
न केकरान्न कपिलान्युद्धे द्वंद्वान्समालिखेत् ॥ 3.42.40 ॥
3.9.m: somewhat resembling Dānavas, mostly holding a staff in hand. / One should not paint combatants in a duel as squint-eyed or tawny.

3.9.s:
nātyunnatena veṣeṇa na ca śāntena śasyate ..
pārśvabaddhena khaḍgena pratīhārastu daṇḍavān .. 41 ..
3.9.d:
नात्युन्नतेन वेषेण न च शान्तेन शस्यते ॥
पार्श्वबद्धेन खड्गेन प्रतीहारस्तु दण्डवान् ॥ 41 ॥
3.9.m: A doorkeeper is commended with attire neither excessively prominent nor subdued, / bearing a staff, with a sword fastened at his side.

3.9.s:
saṃveṣṭitaśiraskāśca kartavyā vaṇijastathā ..
gāyanā nartakā ye vā vādyavādaviśuddhaye .. 42 ..
3.9.d:
संवेष्टितशिरस्काश्च कर्तव्या वणिजस्तथा ॥
गायना नर्तका ये वा वाद्यवादविशुद्धये ॥ 42 ॥
3.9.m: Merchants should be made with their heads wrapped [in turbans]. / Singers and dancers who [perform] for the excellence of instrumental music

3.9.s:
uddhatena tu veṣeṇa kāryāste manujottama ..
āsannapalitā kāryāḥ svabhūṣaṇavibhūṣitāḥ .. 43 ..
3.9.d:
उद्धतेन तु वेषेण कार्यास्ते मनुजोत्तम ॥
आसन्नपलिता कार्याः स्वभूषणविभूषिताः ॥ 43 ॥
3.9.m: should be made in haughty attire, O best of men. / Elders with grey hair should be made adorned with their proper ornaments.

3.9.s:
paurajānapadāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ śubhavastravibhūṣaṇāḥ ..
prasṛtapravaṇāḥ prahvāḥ svabhāvapriyadarśinaḥ .. 44 ...
3.9.d:
पौरजानपदाः श्रेष्ठाः शुभवस्त्रविभूषणाः ॥
प्रसृतप्रवणाः प्रह्वाः स्वभावप्रियदर्शिनः ॥ 44 ॥।
3.9.m: Eminent citizens and villagers should have auspicious garments and ornaments; / they should be gracious, humble, bowed, and pleasing in their natural appearance.

3.9.s:
svakarmopaskaravyagraḥ kāryaḥ karmakaro janaḥ..
prāṃśavaḥ pīnagātrāśca pīnagrīvaśirodharāḥ .. 45 ..
3.9.d:
स्वकर्मोपस्करव्यग्रः कार्यः कर्मकरो जनः॥
प्रांशवः पीनगात्राश्च पीनग्रीवशिरोधराः ॥ 45 ॥
3.9.m: A working person should be made occupied with the implements of his work. / Tall, stout of body, with thick necks and heads,

3.9.s:
ugrāśca nīcakeśāśca mallāḥ kāryāstathoddhatāḥ ..
vṛṣāḥ kesariṇaścaiva yāścānyāḥ sattvajātayaḥ .. 46 ..
3.9.d:
उग्राश्च नीचकेशाश्च मल्लाः कार्यास्तथोद्धताः ॥
वृषाः केसरिणश्चैव याश्चान्याः सत्त्वजातयः ॥ 46 ॥
3.9.m: fierce, with cropped hair, and arrogant should wrestlers be made. / Bulls, lions, and other species of animals

3.9.s:
yathābhūminiveśāste lokaṃ dṛṣṭvā narādhipa ..
etadrūpasamuddeśamadṛṣṭānāṃ taveritam .. 47 .
3.9.d:
यथाभूमिनिवेशास्ते लोकं दृष्ट्वा नराधिप ॥
एतद्रूपसमुद्देशमदृष्टानां तवेरितम् ॥ 47 ।
3.9.m: should be placed according to their habitat, having observed the world, O lord of men. / This brief statement of forms has been declared to you for [things] unseen.

3.9.s:
dṛṣṭaṃ susadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ ..
citre sādṛśyakaraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ parikīrtitam .. 48 ..
3.9.d:
दृष्टं सुसदृशं कार्यं सर्वेषामविशेषतः ॥
चित्रे सादृश्यकरणं प्रधानं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 48 ॥
3.9.m: What is visible should be rendered in faithful likeness for all without distinction; / in painting, the production of likeness is proclaimed as foremost.

3.9.s:
buddhyā rūpaṃ yathāveśaṃ varṇaṃ ca manujottama ..
deśedeśe narāḥ kāryā yathāvattatsamudbhavāḥ ..49..
3.9.d:
बुद्ध्या रूपं यथावेशं वर्णं च मनुजोत्तम ॥
देशेदेशे नराः कार्या यथावत्तत्समुद्भवाः ॥49॥
3.9.m: Having understood their form, dress, and colour, O best of men, / people native to each respective region should be rendered correctly.

3.9.s:
deśaṃ niyogaṃ sthānaṃ ca karma buddhvā ca yatnataḥ ..
āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ veśaṃ kāryaṃ narādhipa .. 3.42.50 ..
3.9.d:
देशं नियोगं स्थानं च कर्म बुद्ध्वा च यत्नतः ॥
आसनं शयनं यानं वेशं कार्यं नराधिप ॥ 3.42.50 ॥
3.9.m: Having carefully ascertained the region, the occupation, the rank, and the activity, / the seat, bed, vehicle, and dress should be executed, O king.

3.9.s:
saritāṃ saśarīrāṇāṃ vāhanāni pradarśayet ..
pūrṇakumbhakarāḥ kāryāstathā nāmitajānavaḥ .. 51 ..
3.9.d:
सरितां सशरीराणां वाहनानि प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
पूर्णकुम्भकराः कार्यास्तथा नामितजानवः ॥ 51 ॥
3.9.m: One should show the mounts of the personified rivers; / they should be made holding full jars in their hands, with knees slightly bent.

3.9.s:
śailānāṃ śikharaṃ mūrdhni darśayenmanujottama ..
dvīpānāṃ ca karaiḥ kāryaṃ tathā bhūmaṇḍalaṃ śubham .. 92 ..
3.9.d:
शैलानां शिखरं मूर्ध्नि दर्शयेन्मनुजोत्तम ॥
द्वीपानां च करैः कार्यं तथा भूमण्डलं शुभम् ॥ 92 ॥
3.9.m: One should show the crest of mountains on their heads, O best of men; / and of continents, the auspicious orb of the earth should be depicted in their hands.

3.9.s:
. .. ... ..........rājaṃstathā śikharapāṇayaḥ ..
ratnapātrakarāḥ kāryāḥ sāgarā manujottama .. 53 ..
3.9.d:
॥॥॥ ॥॥॥॥॥राजंस्तथा शिखरपाणयः ॥
रत्नपात्रकराः कार्याः सागरा मनुजोत्तम ॥ 53 ॥
3.9.m: [...] O king, holding mountain crests in their hands; / the oceans should be made holding vessels filled with jewels, O best of men.

3.9.s:
samudrāṇāṃ prabhāsthāne salilaṃ tu pradarśayet ..
āyudhānāṃ ca taccihnaṃ kiñcinmūrdhani darśayet .. 54 ..
3.9.d:
समुद्राणां प्रभास्थाने सलिलं तु प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
आयुधानां च तच्चिह्नं किञ्चिन्मूर्धनि दर्शयेत् ॥ 54 ॥
3.9.m: In place of the halo of oceans, one should display water; / and as for weapons, one should show a small sign of each upon their heads.

3.9.s:
nidhīnāṃ darśayetkumbhaṃ śaṃkhaṃ śaṃkhasya darśayet ..
padmaṃ padmasya rājendra śeṣāṇāmanurūpataḥ .. 55 ..
3.9.d:
निधीनां दर्शयेत्कुम्भं शंखं शंखस्य दर्शयेत् ॥
पद्मं पद्मस्य राजेन्द्र शेषाणामनुरूपतः ॥ 55 ॥
3.9.m: Of the treasures, one should show a jar; one should show a conch for Śaṅkha, / a lotus for Padma, O king of kings, and in accordance with the form of the rest.

3.9.s:
kāryasyāvayavāḥ kāryāḥ svaddehasadṛśāḥ pṛthak ..
divyānāṃ darśayeccihnamakṣamālāṃ ca pustakam .. 56 ..
3.9.d:
कार्यस्यावयवाः कार्याः स्वद्देहसदृशाः पृथक् ॥
दिव्यानां दर्शयेच्चिह्नमक्षमालां च पुस्तकम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.9.m: The limbs of an activity should be executed appropriately to their respective bodies; / one should show the emblems of divine beings, such as the rosary and the book.

3.9.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rūpaṃ yadyasya dṛśyate ..
ākāśaṃ daśaryedvidvānvivarṇaṃ khagamākulam .. 57 ..
3.9.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि रूपं यद्यस्य दृश्यते ॥
आकाशं दशर्येद्विद्वान्विवर्णं खगमाकुलम् ॥ 57 ॥
3.9.m: Henceforth I will declare the form of each thing as it is seen: / the wise painter should show the sky devoid of colour and crowded with birds.

3.9.s:
tathaiva darśayedrājaṃstārakāmaṇḍitaṃ divam .
bhūmiṃ ca jāṅgalānūpamiśrāṃ svaiḥsvaistathā guṇaiḥ .. 58 ..
3.9.d:
तथैव दर्शयेद्राजंस्तारकामण्डितं दिवम् ।
भूमिं च जाङ्गलानूपमिश्रां स्वैःस्वैस्तथा गुणैः ॥ 58 ॥
3.9.m: Likewise, O king, one should show the heavens adorned with stars; / and the earth, whether arid, marshy, or mixed, along with their respective attributes.

3.9.s:
parvataṃ tu śilājālaiḥ śikharairdhātubhirdrumaiḥ ..
nirjharairbhujagaiścaiva darśayennṛpasattama .. 59 ..
3.9.d:
पर्वतं तु शिलाजालैः शिखरैर्धातुभिर्द्रुमैः ॥
निर्झरैर्भुजगैश्चैव दर्शयेन्नृपसत्तम ॥ 59 ॥
3.9.m: A mountain, however, one should show with heaps of stones, peaks, minerals, trees, / waterfalls, and serpents, O best of kings.

3.9.s:
vanaṃ nānāvidhairvṛkṣairvihaṅgaiḥ śvāpadaistathā ..
toyaṃ ca darśayedvidvānanantairmatsyakacchapaiḥ .. 3.42.60 ..
3.9.d:
वनं नानाविधैर्वृक्षैर्विहङ्गैः श्वापदैस्तथा ॥
तोयं च दर्शयेद्विद्वाननन्तैर्मत्स्यकच्छपैः ॥ 3.42.60 ॥
3.9.m: A forest with diverse kinds of trees, birds, and wild beasts; / and the wise painter should show water with innumerable fish and tortoises,

3.9.s:
padmākṣaiśca mahārāja tathānyairjalajairguṇaiḥ ..
devatāveśmabhiścitraiḥ prāsādāpaṇaveśmabhiḥ .. 61 ..
3.9.d:
पद्माक्षैश्च महाराज तथान्यैर्जलजैर्गुणैः ॥
देवतावेश्मभिश्चित्रैः प्रासादापणवेश्मभिः ॥ 61 ॥
3.9.m: and with lotuses, O great king, as well as other aquatic qualities; / a city the wise painter should show with diverse shrines of deities, with palaces, shops, and houses,

3.9.s:
nagaraṃ darśayedvidvān rājamārgaiśca śobhanaiḥ ..
vamatyā darśayedgrāmaṃ kiñcidudyānabhūṣitam .. 62 ..
3.9.d:
नगरं दर्शयेद्विद्वान् राजमार्गैश्च शोभनैः ॥
वमत्या दर्शयेद्ग्रामं किञ्चिदुद्यानभूषितम् ॥ 62 ॥
3.9.m: and with splendid royal highways; / one should show a village with residences, slightly adorned with gardens.

3.9.s:
sarveṣāmatha durgāṇāṃ kartavyaṃ darśanaṃ tathā ..
svabhūmiviniveśena vaprāṭṭālakaparvataiḥ .. 63 ..
3.9.d:
सर्वेषामथ दुर्गाणां कर्तव्यं दर्शनं तथा ॥
स्वभूमिविनिवेशेन वप्राट्टालकपर्वतैः ॥ 63 ॥
3.9.m: Likewise, the presentation of all kinds of fortresses is to be executed / according to their proper placement on the terrain, with ramparts, turrets, and mountains.

3.9.s:
paṇyayuktāstu kartavyāstathaivāpaṇabhūmayaḥ ..
ādhānabhūmiḥ kartavyā pānayuktā narākulā .. 64 ..
3.9.d:
पण्ययुक्तास्तु कर्तव्यास्तथैवापणभूमयः ॥
आधानभूमिः कर्तव्या पानयुक्ता नराकुला ॥ 64 ॥
3.9.m: Marketplaces should indeed be made provided with merchandise; / a tavern should be made provided with liquor and crowded with people.

3.9.s:

3.9.m:
Thus painted by the wise through conceptualisation, with postures, grace, playfulness, aesthetic flavours, and the like, / a painting delights the gaze of the eyes and respectfully grants desired wishes.
3.43 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The erotic, comic, pathetic, heroic, furious, terrifying, / odious, wondrous, and peaceful are traditionally known as the nine aesthetic flavours of painting.
Among these, whatever is beautiful with splendour, charm, sweetness of line, / and the clever ornaments of women, belongs to the erotic aesthetic flavour.
Whatever is largely composed of hunchbacks and dwarfs, looking slightly grotesque, / and needlessly contracting the hand, produces laughter in the comic aesthetic flavour.
Whatever evokes pity in circumstances of begging, separation, abandonment, sale, misfortune, and the like, / one should paint in the pathetic aesthetic flavour.
Harshness, deformity, and anger do not impair [the work] if intended for an expressive purpose; / executed with blazing weapons and ornaments, it belongs to the furious aesthetic flavour.
In matters of heroic resolution, displaying nobility, / having a proud smile, knitted brows, valorous, wondrous—this belongs to the heroic sentiment (vīrarasa).

3.9.m:
Whatever involves the wicked, repulsive sights, madmen, beasts of prey, murderers, and the like, / that belongs to the fearful sentiment (bhayānakarasa) in the application of the art of painting.
Despised cremation grounds, acts of slaughter, fearful places— / whatever painting is excellent in being varied, that belongs to the odious sentiment (bībhatsarasa).
When it shows modest horripilation, thought, the face bent like Tārkṣya's, / and looking at one another, that is based on the wondrous sentiment (adbhutarasa).
Whatever has gentle forms, postures of meditation and absorption, / consisting mostly of ascetics, that belongs to the peaceful sentiment (śāntarasa).
Those known as the erotic, the comic, and the peaceful should be painted in residential homes.
The remaining ones should never be made anywhere for anyone. / In the house of the gods, all sentiments are to be made, O king, and in a king's palace.
They must not be made in the royal residence, in the bedchambers of kings; / in the assembly halls in the king's palace all sentiments are to be made.
Excluding the king's assembly hall and the house of the gods, / war, cremation grounds, sorrow, the dead, those afflicted by grief, vile persons,

3.9.m:
and inauspicious subjects should never be painted in homes. / Horned bulls that indicate treasure, O king, hands indicating treasure, bent-bodied youths,
treasures, Vidyādharas, O king, ṛṣis, as well as Garuḍa, / and Hanūmān, and those known in the world as highly auspicious,
must always be painted, O great king, in the homes of men. / A man must not execute painting in his own house by himself, O king.
Weakness, heaviness of line, lack of division, / and confusion of colors are declared here to be the defects of painting.
Stance, proportion, weightiness, sweetness, clarity of division, / resemblance, and foreshortening and elongation: this is remembered as the group of eight virtues.
Lacking stance, bereft of sentiment, blank-eyed, dirty, / or devoid of life: that is declared inauspicious.
Where weightiness seems to shine forth, [where it] seems to fear, O king, / where sweetness seems to smile, [there] it appears as if alive.

प्रतीतं च लिखेद्धीमान्नाप्रतीतेः कथंचन ॥ 23 ॥
शास्त्रज्ञैः सुकृतैर्दक्षैश्चित्रं हि मनुजाधिप ॥
श्रियमावहति क्षिप्रमलक्ष्मीं चापकर्षति ॥ 24 ॥
निर्णेजयति चोत्कण्ठां निरुणद्ध्यागतं शुभम् ॥
शुद्धां प्रथयति प्रीतिं जनयत्यतुलामपि ॥ 25 ॥
दुःस्वप्नदर्शनं हन्ति प्रीणाति गृहदैवतम् ॥
न तु शून्यमिवाभाति यत्र चित्रं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 26 ॥
॥॥॥॥॥॥॥दकर्णं चाप्यनलंकृतम् ॥
शल्यविद्धं च वृद्धं च यः करोति स चित्रवित् ॥ 27 ॥
तरङ्गाग्निखिखाधूमं वैजयन्त्यस्वरादिकम् ॥
वायुगत्या लिखेद्यस्तु विज्ञेयो मत्तचित्रवित् ॥ 28 ॥
3.9.m:
A painting that appears as if breathing is a painting of auspicious signs. / Lacking limbs, dirty, blank, surrounded by persons bound, sick, or terrified,
and with disheveled hair: a man of good fortune should avoid [these]. / And the wise man should paint what is known, never what is unknown.
A painting made well by skilled men knowledgeable in the treatises, O king, / quickly brings prosperity and removes misfortune;
it washes away longing, obstructs incoming misfortune, / spreads pure joy, and produces peerless [delight];
it destroys bad dreams, and pleases the deity of the house. / And where a painting is established, [the place] does not seem empty.
[…] ear, unadorned, / pierced by an arrow, and aged: he who executes [these] is a knower of painting.
Waves, tongues of flame, smoke, fluttering banners, and the like: / he who paints these according to the motion of the wind is considered an accomplished knower of painting.

अनेनैव विधानेन यथा चित्रमुदाहृतम्॥32॥
तथानेन विधानेन पुस्तकर्म विधीयते ॥

अशक्यो विस्तराद्वक्तुं बहुवर्षशतैरपि ॥ ॥ 36 ॥
3.9.m:
The sleeping imbued with consciousness, and the dead devoid of consciousness, / and the differentiation of depressions and elevations: he who executes [these] is a knower of painting.
For all these, natural perspective is indeed praised; / frontal positioning should be avoided with effort in painting.
As painting is, so is relief-work declared, O king; / and that should be displayed in metals: gold, silver, copper, and the like.
The making of images in stone, wood, and metals / should be done by this very rule, just as set forth for painting.
Likewise, modeling in clay or plaster (pustakarma) is prescribed by this rule; / and that is spoken of as twofold: solid and hollow.
The solid should always be made with metals, stones, wood, and clay; / the hollow should be made with leather, and likewise with wood and metals.
A firm coating of clay is to be applied to a model made of leather. / According to this rule in the treatise, one should likewise paint on cloth.
When this has been told to you in mere summary, O king, / it is impossible to state it in detail even in many hundreds of years.

3.9.m:
Whatever has not been stated here is to be understood from dance, O lord of the earth; / what has not been stated even in dance should not be applied to painting here, O king.
Painting is the foremost of the arts, conferring dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation; / and it is the first auspicious thing in a house where it is established.
Just as Sumeru is foremost of mountains, just as Garuḍa is chief of birds, / just as a king is foremost of men, so in this world the art of painting is foremost of arts.
The Citrasūtra is completed.
3.44
Vajra said:
Tell me, O sinless one, about the fashioning of divine forms,
so that, made according to the treatise, [the deity] may always be present.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, O king, as I speak of the fashioning of divine forms;
at the very beginning I will describe the Triple Form to you, O king.
The auspicious characteristics of the image of Viṣṇu of boundless valor: / his form associated with Brahmā is passionate (rājasī), setting everything into motion;
his Vaiṣṇava form is known as pure (sāttvikī), protecting the world; / and his form associated with Rudra is known as dark (tāmasī), bringing about dissolution.
